layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Cook to Safe Temperatures

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cook all food to the minimum safe internal temperatures on the chart above. Use a food thermometer to be sure your food is safe. When you think your food is done, place the food thermometer in the thickest part of the food, making sure not to touch bone, fat, or gristle.

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: Table of Contents

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Separate Hazardous Foods

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Use one cutting board for hazardous foods (e.g. raw meat, poultry, seafood, eggs) and another for non-hazardous foods (e.g. fresh produce, cooked foods, foods that won't be cooked).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Use separate plates and utensils for cooked and raw foods. Use hot, soapy water to wash all plates, utensils, and cutting boards that touched hazardous foods before using them again.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Refrigerate and Freeze Properly

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Your refrigerator should be set to 40°F or below and your freezer to 0°F or below. Use a refrigerator and/or freezer thermometer to be sure. Place raw meat, poultry, and seafood on plates, in containers, or in sealed plastic bags. Freeze them if you're not planning to use them within a few days. Freezing does not kill harmful germs, but it does keep food safe until you can cook it.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Avoid the Danger Zone

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Bacteria that cause food poisoning grow quickest between 41^{\circ}\mathrm{F} and 135°F, also known as the danger zone. Never leave perishable foods at room temperature for more than two hours. If the food is exposed to temperatures above 90°F, refrigerate it within one hour.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If you're not serving food right after cooking, keep it out of the temperature danger zone by using a heat source like a chafing dish, warming tray, or slow cooker. Cold foods can be kept on ice or in a cooler for longer serving times.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Never thaw or marinate foods at room temperature. The safest way to thaw or marinate is in the refrigerator. Leftovers should be placed in small shallow containers and refrigerated promptly to allow for quick cooling.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Wash Produce

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cut away any damaged or bruised areas on fruits and vegetables, then rinse under warm running water. Scrub firm produce like melons, potatoes, or cucumbers with a clean produce brush. Air dry or pat dry with a paper towel or clean cloth towel. Don't rinse raw meat, poultry, seafood, or shell eggs.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: When In Doubt, Throw It Out

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The germs that make you sick are not always the same ones that cause food to go bad. Don't use smell, taste, and appearance as your only guides. Use the storage times on the table above to guide you. If you're still not sure whether a food item is safe, it's better to be safe than sorry and throw it away.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Apricot Chicken Tagine

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 50 minutes | Total: 1 hour

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yield: 6 servings | Serving Size:  $\sim 1\frac{1}{20}$ cups

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Region: Africa | Country: South Africa

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ?  cup light (reduced-fat) sour cream

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ?  teaspoon hot sauce or hot chili oil

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ?  teaspoon salt

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ?  teaspoon ground black pepper

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4 (3- to 4-ounce) boneless skinless chicken thighs (thigh fillets; about 1 pound)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2 tablespoons olive oil

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 large sweet onion, thinly sliced (about 3 cups)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2 cloves garlic, minced (about 1 teaspoon)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ?  teaspoon ground allspice

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 (15-ounce) can low-sodium garbanzo beans (chickpeas), drained and rinsed

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 (14.5-ounce) can no-added-salt diced tomatoes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ?  cup dried apricots, sliced or chopped

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 cinnamon stick (or 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, added to step 7)

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. In a small bowl, whisk together the sour cream, parsley, and hot sauce or chili oil. Set in the refrigerator to chill.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. In a separate small bowl, stir together the salt and pepper.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Pat the chicken dry with paper towels, then sprinkle evenly with the salt-pepper mixture.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Heat a tagine, a Dutch oven, or a large stockpot over medium-high heat.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6. Place the chicken in the pan and cook until golden-brown but not cooked through, about 3-5 minutes on each side. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 7. Reduce the heat to medium, then add the onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the garlic and allspice. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 8. Add the beans, tomatoes with their juice, apricots, and cinnamon. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 9. Return the browned chicken to the pan and cover with a lid, Cook until the chicken is cooked through (internal temperature of 175^{\circ}\mathrm{F}, about 33-35 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 10. Serve warm, with a heaping tablespoon of the sour cream mixture on top of each portion.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Recipe Notes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - This recipe also does very well in a pressure cooker. Follow steps 1-4 on "saute" mode, then add the chicken, seal the lid, and pressure cook on high for 20 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally after cooking.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Instead of the allspice, a spice blend may be used such as Ras el Hanout, garam masala, or Chinese five-spice.

layout_dets.text: Roasted Eggplant Spread

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 30 minutes | Total: 40 minutes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yield: 4 servings | Serving Size:  $\sim 1\frac{1}{4}$ cup

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Region: Africa | Country: Egypt

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 medium eggplant, peeled and cut into 1- to 2-inch chunks (about 12 ounces or 4 cups)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 medium onion, chopped (about 1 cup)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 tablespoon olive oil

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4}  teaspoon garlic powder

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4}  teaspoon salt

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4}  teaspoon ground black pepper

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 tablespoon tomato paste

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Preheat oven to $400^{\circ}\mathrm{F}$.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. In a medium mixing bowl, toss together the eggplant, onion, oil, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Transfer the mixture to a baking sheet and spread into a single layer.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Roast in preheated oven until caramelized and tender, about 25-30 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Remove from oven and set aside to cool slightly, about 10 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6. Transfer the roasted vegetable mixture to a food processor or high-powered blender and add the tomato paste.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 7. Pulse to chop up and mix in the tomato paste. The spread will remain chunky.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 8. Serve right away, or store in the refrigerator for later. Reheat in the microwave or let sit at room temperature for 20-30 minutes when ready to serve.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Recipe Notes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Try this spread on toasted crusty bread, pita chips, crackers, or sandwiches.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This spread may be stored in the refrigerator for up to 7 days.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 表格

Nonstick cooking spray
3 cups uncooked old-fashioned (rolled) oats
? cup honey
3 eggs
1 teaspoon baking powder
? teaspoon salt
? teaspoon ground cinnamon
1? cups lowfat (1%) milk
? cup chopped shelled pistachios
? cup chopped toasted walnuts

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Spray an 8x8-inch baking dish or a 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. In a large mixing bowl, stir together the oats, honey, eggs, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Add the milk, pistachios, walnuts, orange zest, and lemon zest. Stir to combine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish or divide between the muffin tin cups.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6. Bake until fully set, about 30-35 minutes in an 8x8-inch baking dish or 25-30 minutes in a 12-cup muffin tin. The center should be firm when tapped and not indent.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 7. Let cool for 5 minutes before slicing or removing from the muffin tin, then serve warm or at room temperature.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Recipe Notes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk (e.g. almond milk, soy milk), if desired.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Store in an airtight container on the counter or in the refrigerator for up to 7 days, or freeze for up to 6 months.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - A non-nutritive sweetener like \(1/4\) teaspoon stevia or 2 tablespoons monk fruit can be substituted for \(1/4\) cup of the honey. It is not recommended to replace all of the honey, as it is an essential flavor element of baklava.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1? pounds (24 ounces) boneless skinless chicken breast阿??

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2} teaspoon salt

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{3} cup olive oil mayonnaise

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ?  cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? cup finely diced onion

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 tablespoon lime juice (about \( \frac{1}{2} \) lime)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4 teaspoons curry powder

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 teaspoon honey

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? teaspoon grated fresh ginger人?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? teaspoon ground black pepper

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 cup diced fresh or frozen mango, thawed if frozen (about 1 large mango)

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Add the mango, grapes, and chicken. Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.text: Kofta (Turkey Kebabs)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 20 minutes | Total: 35 minutes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yield: 4 servings | Serving Size: 1 kebab

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Region: Africa | Country: Egypt

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Warm water

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2} medium onion (or 1 small onion)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2}  teaspoon salt

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2}  teaspoon ground black pepper

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2} teaspoon ground turmeric

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2}  teaspoon lemon juice or apple cider vinegar

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 pinch baking soda

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Fill a 9x13-inch baking dish about halfway with warm water. Place four wooden skewers in the water and set aside.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Peel the onion, then grate it using a box grater. Press with paper towels to remove the excess juice.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Add the onion, salt, black pepper, turmeric, lemon juice or vinegar, baking soda, and ground turkey to a medium mixing bowl. Knead the mixture until it is dough-like in texture, about 5 minutes, then divide into four portions.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Fill a small bowl or liquid measuring cup about halfway with water. Dampen your clean hands with the water, shaking off any excess, then take each portion of the turkey mixture and roll it into a sausage-like shape, about 4-5 inches long.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Push a skewer lengthwise into each portion of the turkey mixture. Squeeze the mixture gently, spreading it evenly to be about 7-8 inches long and \( \frac{3}{2} \)-inch-thick. Using your thumb and pointer finger, make indentations about 1 inch apart down the length of each kebab.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6. Cook the kebabs on an outdoor (gas/charcoal) or indoor (electric) grill over medium-high heat until cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 4-5 minutes on each side. Serve warm.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.text: Microwave White Bean and Egg Shakshuka

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 5 minutes | Total: 10 minutes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yield: 1 serving | Serving Size: 1 bowl

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Region: Africa | Country: Tunisia

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nonstick cooking spray

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4} cup no-salt-added tomato sauce

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4}  cup no-salt-added white beans (e.g. cannellini, great northern), drained and rinsed

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4}  teaspoon dried thyme

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4} teaspoon sweet or smoked paprika

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4}  teaspoon onion powder

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 pinch garlic powder

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 pinch salt

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 pinch ground black pepper

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2 eggs

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Coat the inside of a microwave-safe bowl with nonstick cooking spray.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Add the tomato sauce, beans, thyme, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Stir to combine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Make a well in the center of the sauce, and crack the eggs into it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Microwave on high power (default setting) for 1 minute.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Continue cooking in 1-minute bursts at \(50\%\) power until the egg yolks and whites are set. Depending on your microwave, this will take about 1-3 minutes in total.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6. Serve warm.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Recipe Notes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If you like heat, try adding a pinch of cayenne or crushed red pepper flakes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Transfer any extra beans and tomato sauce from the cans to airtight storage containers, then refrigerate for up to 5 days. The leftover tomato sauce could also be frozen in an ice cube tray, then transferred to a plastic storage zip-top bag and stored in the freezer for up to 3 months.

layout_dets.text: Black Rice Porridge

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 45 minutes | Total: 50 minutes  
Yield: 4 servings | Serving Size: \( \frac{1}{2} \) cup without toppings  
Region: Eastern Asia | Country: Indonesia

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2}  cup uncooked black rice

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 (13.5-ounce) can light coconut milk, shaken

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3 tablespoons honey

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4} teaspoon vanilla extract

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{8} teaspoon salt

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 8 tablespoons (? cup) fresh or frozen fruit, chopped or sliced if needed (optional; e.g. mango, strawberries, blackberries, pineapple)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4 tablespoons (\frac{1}{4} cup) toasted coconut flakes (optional)

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Add the rice and coconut milk to a medium saucepan. Stir to combine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Bring to a boil over high heat, reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Cover with a lid and cook until the liquid has been mostly absorbed and the rice is tender, about 35-45 minutes, without opening the lid or moving the pan.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Add the honey, vanilla, and salt. Stir to combine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Serve warm, topped with the 2 tablespoons of the fruit (if using) and 1 tablespoon of the coconut (if using).

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Recipe Notes

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.text: Chicken Chow Mein

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 20 minutes | Total: 30 minutes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yield: 2 servings | Serving Size: ~2 cups

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Region: Eastern Asia | Country: China

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 tablespoon olive oil

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? pound (8 ounces) boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized strips

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? medium onion, thinly sliced (about 1 cup)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2 stalks celery, thinly sliced on the bias (diagonal; about \( \frac{1}{2} \) cup)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3 white button or cremini mushrooms, thinly sliced (about \( \frac{1}{2} \) cup)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2 cups chopped or shredded Napa cabbage

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 cup (8 ounces) low-sodium chicken broth

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 (8-ounce) can bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 (8-ounce) can sliced water chestnuts, drained and rinsed

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 tablespoon cornstarch

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 tablespoon water

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? teaspoon sugar

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? teaspoon ground black pepper

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? cup crunchy chow mein noodles, divided

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Add the chicken and cook, stirring often, until cooked through (internal temperature of \(165^{\circ}\mathrm{F}\)), about 6-8 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Set the pan back over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, and mushrooms. Cook until softened, about 6-8 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Add the cabbage, broth, bamboo shoots, and water chestnuts. Stir to combine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6. Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 7. Cook until the cabbage is tender, about 5-7 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 8. In a small bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and water with a fork to make a slurry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 9. Add the slurry, sugar, and black pepper to the vegetable mixture. Stir to combine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 10. Cook until a slightly thickened sauce forms, about 3-5 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 11. Return the cooked chicken to the pan and stir to combine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 12. Serve warm, topping each serving with \( \frac{1}{4} \) cup of the chow mein noodles.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Recipe Notes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Tofu can be used in place of the chicken, if desired.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Try substituting bok choy for the Napa cabbage, if desired.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Garlic Edamame

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 5 minutes | Total: 10 minutes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yield: 2 servings | Serving Size: \( \frac{1}{2} \) cup shelled edamame beans

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Region: Eastern Asia | Country: Japan

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 (16-ounce) bag unshelled frozen edamame (in the pod)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6 cloves garlic, minced (about 1 tablespoon)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2 tablespoons unsalted butter

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 tablespoon lite (reduced-sodium) soy sauce

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ?-? teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, to taste

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 teaspoon sugar

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Add the edamame to a medium microwave-safe bowl and cook on high power (default setting) for 5 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Meanwhile, stir together the soy sauce, red pepper flakes and sugar in a small bowl. Set aside.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Add the butter to a large skillet or sauté pan and place over medium-high heat.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Once the butter starts to brown, add garlic and cooked edamame. Cook, stirring often, until any liquid is evaporated, about 4-5 minutes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Add the soy sauce mixture and continue to cook, stirring constantly, until the liquid is mostly evaporated and a sticky dark sauce starts to form.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6. Serve warm, removing the beans from the shell before eating (see Recipe Notes).

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Recipe Notes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Edamame shells (the outside of the pod) are not edible, only the beans inside. To remove the beans from the shell, place the edamame pod between your teeth, bite down gently, then pull the shell out.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Fresh green beans (trimmed) can be substituted for the edamame, if desired.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nutrition Facts Per Serving: Calories: 215 | Total Fat: 15 g | Saturated Fat: 8.5 g Sodium: 450 mg | Total Carbohydrate: 12.5 g | Dietary Fiber: 2.5 g | Protein: 8.5 g

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Hot-and-Sour Soup

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 15 minutes | Total: 20 minutes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yield: 4 servings | Serving Size: 1? cups

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Region: Eastern Asia | Country: Philippines

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ingredients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4 cups (32 ounces) low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? cup thinly sliced mushrooms

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2-3 tablespoons unseasoned rice vinegar, to taste

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2-3 tablespoons lite (reduced-sodium) soy sauce, to taste

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1 clove garlic, minced (about \( \frac{1}{2} \) teaspoon)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? teaspoon ground dried ginger

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4}-1 teaspoon hot sauce or hot chili oil, to taste 1 egg

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2}  cup cubed firm tofu (about 4 ounces)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2 scallions (green onions), thinly sliced

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{4}  cup fresh or frozen corn

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: \frac{1}{2}  teaspoon toasted sesame oil

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Directions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Add the broth to a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Add the mushrooms, vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and hot sauce or chili oil. Stir to combine, then return to a simmer.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Crack the egg into a small bowl, then gently beat with a fork to combine the whites and yolk.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 页脚

layout_dets.label: 页脚

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING OVERVIEW

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: ABOUT

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Foundations of Fitness Programming (FFP) was written to highlight the essential, research-based components of designing fitness programs, and to "bridge the gap" by providing recommendations to apply research to practice. It is not meant to replace individualized training, nor is it a "cookie-cutter," one-size-fits-all program. It is meant to serve as a resource and educational tool for personal trainers to design training programs quickly and effectively, which are progressive in nature and specific to the needs and goals of their clients.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The FFP provides supporting rationale and scientific references for the recommendations made, and these references can be found in the appendix. Practical training tips and links to relevant journal articles and exercise technique videos have also been added.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There are corresponding spreadsheet "templates" formatted to provide periodized training programs that include drop-down menus for exercise selection, pre-programmed exercise variables that correspond to the phases of training, and recommendations for aspects of a personal training session including dynamic warm-up, resistance, cardiovascular, and flexibility training.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: WHY WAS THE FFP DEVELOPED?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As the worldwide authority on strength and conditioning, the National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA) supports and disseminates research-based knowledge and its practical application to improve performance and fitness. Since the practical application often provides the greatest challenge to novice personal trainers, the FFP was developed to bridge that gap, helping personal trainers

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING | NSCA.COM/PROGRAM-DESIGN-ESSENTIALS Copyright © 2015 National Strength and Conditioning Association. All Rights Reserved.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: efficiently and effectively design training programs based on scientific principles, specific to the individual needs of their clients.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Personal training is often referred to as an art form (i.e., the art of applying research-based knowledge to individual situations including, but not limited to, a client's goals, current/previous injuries, health and fitness status, level of physical competency, self-efficacy, self-confidence, etc.). While there are general training principles that apply to everyone, there are a number of factors that affect program design and client motivation. Regardless, programs should adhere to the principles put forth by the NSCA. These principles (Haff G. H., 2012) are:

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1. Specificity (individuality)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Designing training programs/workouts with a specific goal in mind based on each client's individual needs. Specificity in training can be accomplished by targeting muscle groups, energy systems, speed of movement, movement patterns, and/or muscle action types (Haff G. H., 2012).

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 2. Overload

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The training stress (based on frequency, intensity, and type of exercise as well as recovery processes) placed on a client should exceed the training stress experienced during the previous workout. This is accomplished by increasing the load, sets, reps, or by decreasing the rest periods.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 3. Progression

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Similar to overload, progression (or progressive overload) refers to the systematic modification of a training program over time. In addition to exercise intensity, progression also refers to frequency and increasing the difficulty of exercise selection (advancement from low-skill to high-skill exercises). Exercises are progressed on an individual basis rather than a pre-determined schedule, based on a client's ability and speed of adaptation.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 4. Variation

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Variation is considered planned variety in exercise selection and training variables.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Keeping in line with these principles, the FFP provides a recommended (linear periodization) training sequence that consists of muscular endurance, hypertrophy, strength, and power phases for relatively untrained through advanced clients. While other periodization models exist, a linear model is suggested for beginners.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: DESIGNING INDIVIDUALIZED FITNESS PROGRAMS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A training program should be based on the individual needs and abilities of a client in order to maximize the effectiveness and efficacy of the training program as well as decrease the risk of injury or overtraining. These needs and abilities should be determined during the initial consultation and fitness

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: assessment, and then updated every 4 - 6 weeks of training. The following steps identify a systematic process used to develop the training program:

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1. Consultation and Discussion of Goals

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The initial consultation is an opportunity for the personal trainer to establish professional credibility, determine client-trainer compatibility, and develop rapport and trust with the client. A personal trainer establishes credibility by "debunking" fitness myths and explaining the scientific rationale and programming necessary to reach their goals. Rapport and trust are developed when the personal trainer asks the "right" questions and demonstrates active listening to the client's responses; thereby, increasing the likelihood that a client will discuss the underlying motivational factors driving them to achieve their goals. These factors lay the foundation for open communication between the personal trainer and client, and increase the likelihood that their goals will be attained.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: During the initial consultation, personal trainers should ask questions pertaining to training history, resources, and other obstacles (e.g., time constraints, equipment access, family commitments etc.), as well as begin the initial discussion of training goals. This information provides the "road map" to designing effective programs; it tells the trainer where the client wants to go and identifies where they are starting from. It is important to note that goals should be discussed in general terms during this initial consultation. S.M.A.R.T. goals (see below) can only be accurately set following the evaluation of health history and fitness assessment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Refer to Appendix A for sample questions to ask during the initial consultation.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 2. Evaluate Health History Forms and Perform a Fitness Assessment

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The results of the health history forms and fitness assessments are used to design a client's individual training program. This data includes a baseline for future comparison, identification of current fitness level, clarification of goal setting, and assistance in prescribing initial exercise frequency, volume, and intensity.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 3. Establish S.M.A.R.T. Goals

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Successful programs train clients at a level that matches their needs and abilities to meet their specific goals. Following the initial consultation, health history evaluation, and fitness assessment, the personal trainer and the client should work together to develop specific, measurable, action-oriented, realistic, and timely (S.M.A.R.T.) goals. Tips for effectively establishing goals include:

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING | NSCA.COM/PROGRAM-DESIGN-ESSENTIALS Copyright © 2015 National Strength and Conditioning Association. All Rights Reserved.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: a. Agree Upon the Goals

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The personal trainer and client should develop and agree upon the goals together. The client provides the "why" (i.e., their motivation for achieving these goals), while the personal trainer determines whether the goals are realistic, including time frame to achieve goals, and develops and explains the overall plan for achieving those goals.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: b. Define Roles and Responsibilities

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The personal trainer should explain his/her role in helping the client achieve the goals as well as the client's role and responsibility in achieving the goals, and address the clients expectations of the personal trainer.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: c. Identify and Address Roadblocks

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The personal trainer and client should identify any potential issues that may impede progress and develop alternative options if, or when, these issues arise.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 4. Develop the Training Program

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At this point, the personal trainer has all the necessary information to develop a specific training plan that matches the needs and abilities of a client to reach the agreed upon goals. This plan should include frequency of training, exercise selection, and training variables.

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING | NSCA.COM/PROGRAM-DESIGN-ESSENTIALS Copyright © 2015 National Strength and Conditioning Association. All Rights Reserved.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: IMPLEMENTING THE FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING: INSTRUCTIONS AND APPLICATION

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: While there are many ways to organize an individual training session, the FFP provides recommendations that cover the following training components:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Mobility, movement preparation, and flexibility training

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Resistance training

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Basic nutrition

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Cardiovascular training

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Core/stability training

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is assumed that at this point, the personal trainer has taken the client through and completed the initial consultation, health history evaluation, fitness assessment, and goal setting process. The following sections identify key points related to the application of key training components.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There are program design templates available for download. These templates are formatted for the personal trainer to design periodized training programs with his/her clients.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In addition, a list of other example exercises can be found in the appendix. These exercises are linked to short exercise technique videos with key points and coaching cues.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The templates and videos can be found on the Program Design Essentials page.

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING | NSCA.COM/PROGRAM-DESIGN-ESSENTIALS Copyright © 2015 National Strength and Conditioning Association. All Rights Reserved.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: MOBILITY, MOVEMENT PREPARATION, AND FLEXIBILITY TRAINING

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: WARM-UP BENEFITS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The term "warm-up" refers to preparatory exercises performed prior to engaging in activities that are more vigorous and includes three types: passive, general, and specific. Regardless of the type selected, the overall purpose remains the same: to prepare the body for the demands of the upcoming workout, in particular to increase temperature-dependent physiological responses. These responses:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. increase muscle temperature causing more forceful contractions and quicker relaxations,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. increase blood temperature to working muscles, unloading more oxygen to working muscles, and

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. increase range of motion around joints (Hedrick, 2012).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is important to note that dynamic warm-up/stretching is not the same as flexibility (e.g., static stretching) training. Flexibility refers to the range of motion at a specific joint or series of joints, and is typically assessed in non-weight bearing situations. Conversely, dynamic stretching refers to performing movements specific to a sport or movement pattern (Hedrick, 2012). Within the context of dynamic stretching are the terms mobility and movement preparation (prep). Mobility refers to a client's ability to achieve a posture or position, is more global in nature, and emphasizes multi-joint movements and stabilization (Brooks & Cressey, 2013). Movement prep is an even broader term used to describe all of the various methods used to improve mobility during a warm-up. Performing a dynamic-based warm-up prior to physical activity appears to improve performance and may provide increased resistance to muscle injury (Hedrick, 2012).

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING | NSCA.COM/PROGRAM-DESIGN-ESSENTIALS Copyright © 2015 National Strength and Conditioning Association. All Rights Reserved.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: DYNAMIC WARM-UP RECOMMENDATIONS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A dynamic warm-up routine starts with about 5 min of cardiovascular activity, starting at a low intensity and progressing to a moderate intensity (i.e., to the point of developing a light sweat). This cardiovascular warm-up is followed by 5 - 15 min of movement prep that progresses from general exercises to ones that are more specific. Each movement prep exercise is performed for approximately 20 - 25 yards, or 5 - 10 reps. A list of dynamic warm-up exercises can be found in Appendix B; the exercises listed are linked to videos that provide exercise technique tips and coaching cues.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In addition to the dynamic warm-up exercises included in the appendix, some clients may benefit from additional movement preparation techniques, such as self-myofascial release. This technique may improve range of motion without subsequent performance detriments (MacDonald, et al., 2013).

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: DYNAMIC WARM-UP PROGRAMMING CONSIDERATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Personal trainers should have a conscious reason for prescribing exercises for their clients and can support their recommendations with scientifically sound research. This statement applies to all phases of a workout, including the dynamic warm-up routine. When designing a warm-up routine, personal trainers should ask themselves:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. What cardiovascular activity is most appropriate for the client and involves the most amount of muscle mass?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. What exercises are planned in the upcoming workout?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: a. What joints and muscles will be involved?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: b. What is the overall level of mobility required to perform the exercise?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: c. What planes of motion will be involved?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: d. What speed of movement will be involved?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Does the client have any specific mobility restrictions or exercise contraindications?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Recommendations:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Start with general movements that mobilize joints that will be used in the upcoming workout or need consistent work, such as the ankle, hip, and thoracic spine (Myer, et al., 2014).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Select additional mobility drills based on the individual needs of the client.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Progress to specific warm-up movements/exercises that meet the physical and physiological demands of the upcoming workout.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Consider the following warm-up example for a client with limited mobility who will be performing the barbell back squat in the upcoming workout. After a 5-min warm-up (walk to jog to run), a sample mobility routine may include the following:

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: FLEXIBILITY TRAINING

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Research suggests that although static stretching and proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) are viable options for increasing range of motion, they may decrease force production and subsequent performance (Mojock, Kim, Eccles, & Panton, 2011). This decrease in performance is attributed to musculotendinous unit (MTU) stiffness and decreased neural activation of the skeletal muscles (Mojock, Kim, Eccles, & Panton, 2011). For this reason, flexibility training via static stretching and PNF are recommended when the muscles are already warmed up, either at the end of a workout session or during a separate flexibility focused session.

layout_dets.text: CLASSIFYING TRAINING STATUS AND TRAINING FREQUENCY RECOMMENDATIONS

layout_dets.label: 段落

The following table provides a means of classifying clients based on the duration and frequency of their current training program and their overall training experience.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: SEQUENCING OF TRAINING

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Periodization is the systematic process of planned variation in a training program and is commonly used in athletic populations, where peaking for an event is critical. Consider a football team who just ended their fall season. After a short time off, their periodicized training program will begin with a general preparation phase in the off-season and progress toward a peaking/competitive phase. This general preparation phase will begin shifting from high volume/low intensity to low volume/high intensity as the football season nears. How does a personal trainer apply this concept to a client who wants to lose weight, build muscle, or "get in shape?"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Before answering that question, it is important to understand that the purpose of periodization is to improve physical performance progressively towards a training goal through the manipulation of training variables. This purpose adheres to the general training principles of overload, progression, and variation previously discussed. The personal trainer should understand that different training goals have complementary effects, and that by sequencing different phases of training those same principles are adhered to. For example, a client whose primary training goal is strength would benefit from completing a hypertrophy phase prior to completing a strength phase. The hypertrophy phase will result in an increased cross-sectional area (e.g., more muscle mass) which can increase total force production potential (Haff G. H., 2012).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is generally accepted that all clients should begin a resistance training plan based on either muscular endurance or hypertrophy to establish a training base for the development of other specific goals. Intermediate and advanced clients who have already developed this training base may perform a shorter muscular endurance or hypertrophy phase or move directly into training for their specific goals.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The following provides an example linear periodization sequence, each lasting 2 - 4 weeks (Haff G. H., 2012):

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Muscular endurance phase

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Hypertrophy phase

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Strength phase

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Power phase (intermediate and advanced clients only)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is important to note that many different methods of periodization/sequencing can produce significant results; however, there is no "one best way" (Cissik, Hedrick, & Barnes, 2008). After completing the initial training sequence of 3 - 4 months, the personal trainer should sequence the training phases to meet the specific needs/goals of the client, and then manipulate training variables every 2 - 4 weeks to prevent stagnation and encourage continuous adaptation.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: EXERCISE SELECTION, REGRESSION, AND PROGRESSION

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Becoming proficient at an exercise requires coaching (from the personal trainer) and practice (from the client). Clients must be able to perform movements that challenge their ability without putting them at risk of injury and still provide them with an appropriate training stimulus in order to adapt.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As an example, consider Mari, a 45-year-old female who just signed up for an eight-week personal training program. She will be getting married in eight weeks and her goal is to look great in her wedding dress. In training terms, she wants to decrease her percentage of body fat. Mari's training age is 0, meaning she has never stepped foot in a weight room and describes herself as "clumsy." Her personal trainer thinks that one of the best overall exercises is the barbell back squat, which requires a moderate level of technical skill to be performed safely with an adequate load to elicit a training effect. The personal trainer also knows that most lumbar disk injuries occur when the spine is flexed (Durall & Manske, 2005), especially when loaded. If the personal trainer were to spend 15 minutes a session, twice a week working on barbell back squat technique, it would be using about \(25\%\) of her training time on learning exercise technique.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Instead of getting stuck on the process, the personal trainer should focus on the product (or outcome of performing the exercise). If the personal trainer thinks about the product of the exercise (incorporating a multi-joint movement involving the majority of muscles in the body) he/she may choose to "regress" the exercise. Regression refers to selecting a less complicated exercise using the same movement pattern. In this case, the trainer may choose to select a goblet squat, assisted squat, or even a wall sit. Progression is the opposite; it involves selecting an exercise of a similar movement pattern with a higher technical degree. For example, a progression from the back squat may include the front squat or overhead squat. Going back to Mari, performing a less technical exercise, like the goblet squat, would be a more effective exercise (given her eight-week time frame) in building muscle and/or burning calories.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: TRAINING VARIABLES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The next sections provide descriptions of each training phase. These training phases include muscular endurance, hypertrophy, muscular strength, and muscular power. Training variables are included within each phase. These training variables include:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Sets per exercise

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Reps per exercise

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Rest between sets

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Load, which is expressed as a percentage of one-repetition maximum (IRM)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Note that these exercise variables apply to the primary exercises (multi-joint/compound). Assistance exercises (single-joint/ isolated) are typically performed with lower intensity and higher repetition ranges (primarily in the strength and power phases). For example, during the strength phase, the primary lifts (e.g., squats, bench press, etc.) utilize high intensity/low reps, but the assistance exercises (e.g., leg extension, biceps curl, etc.) utilize low intensity/ high reps.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: ASSIGNING LOAD

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Load is commonly expressed as a percentage of 1RM (one-repetition maximum), which is the heaviest load that can be lifted once while maintaining correct form/technique during a given exercise. Load and the number of reps performed have been shown to be highly associated to specific training goals. For example, heavier loads \((>80\%)\) of 1RM with lower reps are associated with gains in strength, while lighter loads \((<70\%)\) of 1RM with higher reps are associated with gains in muscular endurance (Haff G. H., 2012).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Before assigning load, the personal trainer must determine the IRM of the desired lift. This can be attained by performing a true IRM test or by using a multiple repetition maximum (RM) test to estimate the IRM.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The advantage of performing a 1RM test is that a true 1RM test will provide the most accurate result; however, this method does have some disadvantages. Novice clients may lack the technique necessary to allow a safe 1RM test. Some clients may have the necessary technical competence to complete a lift safely, but lack confidence to complete the test safely. It is essential that the personal trainer take the client's training age, technical competency, and confidence into consideration when deciding which method they will use to determine a 1RM. It is also important to note that 1RM tests should be reserved for compound/multi-joint lifts because these lifts are typically better suited for use with large loads. Testing assistance exercises (e.g., single-joint exercises such as the biceps curl) for a 1RM should be avoided. (Haff G. H., 2012)

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING | NSCA.COM/PROGRAM-DESIGN-ESSENTIALS Copyright © 2015 National Strength and Conditioning Association. All Rights Reserved.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: An alternative to 1RM testing is multiple RM testing, which can be used to estimate a client's 1RM. While a 1RM test directly measures the maximal amount of weight a client can lift, multiple RM testing determines a 6RM - 10RM load that can be used to indirectly estimate a client's 1RM using the Training Load Chart found on the Program Design Essentials page.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PROGRAM DESIGN METHODS AND DESCRIPTIONS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The following are program design terms used in subsequent sections with brief explanations:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Single-set system: performing one set of a given exercise (as opposed to performing multiple sets of an exercise)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Multiple-set systems (standard exercise order): performing multiple sets of an exercise before moving on to subsequent exercises

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Complex set: combining a strength exercise followed by a power exercise (e.g., squats followed by depth jumps)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Compound set: performing 2 - 3 exercises for similar muscle groups

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Circuit training: performing one set of multiple exercises before repeating

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Supersets: performing alternating exercises for opposing muscle groups

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Pyramid loading: increasing training load progressively and then decreasing

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Drop sets: performing a set to muscular failure with a given load and continuing immediately with additional sets at a lighter load

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Heavy negatives: performing eccentric-only work with a load greater than concentric 1RM

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Forced reps: performing additional reps past volitional fatigue with the help of a spotter

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Cluster sets: also known as rest-pause sets, utilize inter-repetition rest intervals of 10 - 30 s

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Accommodating resistance: incorporating bands and chains to free weight exercises to exert isokinetic resistance throughout the full range of motion

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Partial range of motion: performing an exercise in partial ranges of motion to increase strength at a particular joint angle

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING | NSCA.COM/PROGRAM-DESIGN-ESSENTIALS Copyright © 2015 National Strength and Conditioning Association. All Rights Reserved.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PROGRAM DESIGN: PHASES OF TRAINING

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The FFP and the corresponding training templates follow the linear periodization method. It should be noted, however, that there are numerous valid and effective periodization methods that can be implemented when working with clients.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: MUSCULAR ENDURANCE

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Muscular endurance is defined as the ability to maintain submaximal muscle actions (Willardson, 2008). Training for muscular endurance combines high repetition ranges with short rest periods, bringing about high levels of metabolic stress thereby requiring lighter loads to complete the prescribed number of repetitions. These lighter loads are not as effective in stimulating muscle hypertrophy as moderate loads with slightly longer rest periods (as recommended in the hypertrophy phase) (Schoenfeld, 2010).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Muscular endurance training is most commonly performed with either standard exercise order (completing all sets of an exercise before moving on to another exercise) or through circuit training.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Resistance exercise performed through circuit training has been shown to improve \(\mathrm{VO}_2\max\), lactate threshold, body composition, and strength endurance in untrained populations (Waller, Miller, & Hannon, 2011). An essential component to successful implementation of circuit training is the rest period. While there are no specific rules for assigning the work-to-rest period, the FFP recommends that the personal trainer start novice clients with a 1:1 ratio then progress to a 2:1 ratio as the client's fitness level improves.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: HYPERTROPHY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Muscle hypertrophy refers to an increase in cross-sectional area (CSA) brought about from a net increase or growth of the contractile proteins actin and myosin (myofibrillar hypertrophy), as well as glycogen and intracellular fluids (sarcoplasmic hypertrophy). To accomplish this increase in CSA, the hypertrophy phase combines moderate loads, repetitions, and rest intervals to elicit muscular tension, metabolic stress, and muscle damage, all of which act as stimuli for adaptations. This combination of moderate loads, higher relative volume, and rest intervals can also cause an increase in circulating testosterone and growth hormones, which lead to increased protein synthesis and decreased protein degradation (Schoenfeld, 2010).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When training for hypertrophy, the personal trainer should pay particular attention to rest intervals, as too much rest (over about 2.5 min) may decrease the magnitude of the endocrine response (i.e., the amount of testosterone and growth hormones released). Subsequent sets of a given exercise must begin before complete recovery has been reached, which causes increased metabolic stress (Buresh, Berg, & French, 2009). It is important to adjust the load and/or rest periods to assure that exercise technique is not compromised.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hypertrophy training is often performed in body part "splits" or upper/lower body alternating routines, whereby exercises that focus on the upper body are performed on one day and exercises for the lower body the next day. Typical splits include chest, shoulders, and triceps; back and biceps; and legs. Other programming techniques used for hypertrophy may include forced reps, drop sets, superset, compound sets, and heavy negatives.

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FOUNDATIONS OF FITNESS PROGRAMMING | NSCA.COM/PROGRAM-DESIGN-ESSENTIALS Copyright ? 2015 National Strength and Conditioning Association. All Rights Reserved.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Regardless of the method employed, the goal of hypertrophy workouts is to induce metabolic stress, muscle tension, and appropriate levels of muscle damage.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: MUSCULAR STRENGTH

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Maximum strength represents the maximal amount of force that can be generated by a muscle or group of muscles, regardless of the amount of time it takes (Tan, 1999). The muscular strength phase employs heavy loads (e.g., 1-6RM) and longer rest periods to increase the maximal level of force a muscle (or group of muscles) can generate, regardless of time.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Training with heavier loads and longer rest periods can result in positive neural and physiological adaptations. The neural improvements have been shown to occur earlier in the training phase, typically the first two months for novice clients. The physiological adaptations (primarily increased CSA) occur later in the training. Training for maximum strength improves the ability to recruit fast-twitch muscle fibers, which typically are not recruited when training with lighter loads, especially among novice clients (Weir & Brown, 2012).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: From a physiological standpoint, the heavy loads and longer rest periods can result in a greater increase in circulating testosterone, while the use of moderate loads and intensity combined with short rest periods employed during hypertrophy training can lead to greater increases in growth hormones (comparatively) (Willardson, 2008).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As mentioned earlier, sequencing of training has a complementary effect. This means that initially increasing the CSA of muscle fibers may promote greater increases in strength with subsequent training. Similarly, the neural improvements that result from increasing maximum strength may improve the hypertrophic effect (Haff G. H., 2012).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Existing strength training guidelines suggest that primary exercises (complex multi-joint movements) be performed first, followed by assistance exercises (smaller muscles/muscle groups and single-joint movements). Standard exercise order seems to be the most effective for optimal strength gains because it allows greater recovery between sets compared to muscular endurance or hypertrophy training. Max strength training is typically performed by movement groups (as opposed to training individual body parts), such as push (e.g., squat, lunge, bench press, etc.), pull (e.g., deadlift, bent-over row, etc.), and press (e.g., military press, etc.). Clients with more experience who are more advanced may further break down the movements into lower-body push, lower-body pull, upper-body push, upper-body pull, and press (Haff G. H., 2012).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: An example strength workout might include 1 - 3 strength exercises, such as the back squat and bench press (3 - 6 sets of 3 - 6 reps with 3 min of rest) followed by assistance/complementary movements using hypertrophy variables, such as walking lunges, leg extensions, dumbbell flies, and triceps extensions (3 sets of 8 - 12 reps with 1 min of rest).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Other program design techniques commonly used to increase maximum strength include cluster sets, the use of accommodating resistance, partial range of motion, and isometric work (Schoenfeld, 2011).

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: MUSCULAR POWER

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: While more often thought of for use with athletes, fitness clients can also benefit from power training. In fact, power training has been shown to increase older adults' ability to perform activities of daily living (ADL) more than standard strength training (Haff G. H., 2012).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The emphasis of this phase is on explosive movements, developing force as quickly as possible, and is accomplished by moving loads as quickly as possible. Exercises traditionally utilized in the power phase include traditional barbell Olympic-style lifts (the snatch and the clean and jerk) and plyometrics. However, the Olympic-style lifts require a high degree of technical experience along with a high degree of mobility and stability; it is not always realistic to expect the everyday client to be able to perform Olympic-style lifts. However, power training can still be performed safely and effectively using explosive exercises and various implements, such as medicine balls, dumbbells, kettlebells, and bodyweight (plyometrics).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Training for power is typically performed with standard exercise order described earlier. Two other methods that require more research, but appear to improve the development of power, are complex sets and cluster sets.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Complex sets can be used to improve both strength and power by performing biomechanically similar exercises in pairs (two similar exercises) or triads (three similar exercises). Complex sets typically begin with a strength exercise followed by a power exercise. In theory, training using cluster sets is thought to stimulate motor unit excitability, increase phosphorylation of the myosin light chain, and decrease presynaptic inhibition. This response is thought to augment power output and is collectively termed postactivation potentiation (PAP). Training with complex sets seems to be more beneficial in clients with higher levels of strength and is not typically recommended for novice clients. Prior to implementing complex sets into training, a client should have a solid strength base and be proficient in plyometric training (Carter & Greenwood, 2014).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cluster sets manipulate the configuration of reps performed within a set and may also be referred to as a rest-pause set. This manipulation involves programming short rest periods between each rep and/or manipulating the load within each rep performed within a set. The short rest period (15 - 30 s

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: between each rep) is thought to allow some phosphocreatine (PCr) replenishment and overall higher quality successive reps. Load manipulation within a set is typically performed in an undulating (using a pyramid loading scheme) fashion. Theoretically, the undulating cluster training elicits a potentiation effect allowing for greater overall power outputs and barbell velocities. Undulating cluster training should be reserved for highly experienced clients (Haff, et al., 2008).

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Chemistry is a discipline based on observation (as are all sciences). In lecture, you will learn the principles and theories that, to date, best explain the observations that have accumulated. The problem is that, if all you have is lecture, then it is all too easy to forget that these theories apply to the "real world." The laboratory experience is, by design, your opportunity to see these principles and theories in practice.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This laboratory manual has been written not only to enhance your understanding of chemistry, but also to utilize the computing device that yow, as a student at Dakota State University. You will be required to bring it to lab so that you can use it to capture data and take observations. You are also strongly encouraged to bring it to class. In addition, you will be required to purchase a copy of Hyper Chem for students (available at http://www.hyper.com for download) which will be used both in lecture and lab.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This project is possible thanks to a generous grant from Dakota State University. It is free for non-commercial use. All rights reserved. This is brought to you by the College of Arts and Sciences at the Dakota State University. It is the user's responsibility to ensure that proper supervision is maintained at all times by an appropriately trained person or persons to ensure the softly of all people using any of the experiments contained in this manual. It is the users own responsibility to follow all appropriate safety procedures and modify any part of this manual that they are not comfortable with. Use of this manual, in whole or in part, does not imply liability in any way on the part of the author, the college of arts and sciences, or Dakota State University.

layout_dets.text: Legal Notice: These safety guidelines are just that; guidelines. To the best of the author's knowledge, this is as complete a document as can be reasonably expected, however, following these guidelines does not guarantee that an individual may not be harmed in a lab, and because situations can arise that are not expected and there may be guidelines that have been overlooked by simple mistake, the College of Arts and Sciences, Dakota State University, and the author claim no responsibility for any reason whatsoever by those who choose to use this document. This document is provided to the general public as a courtesy; any individual, institution, or organization who chooses to use this document, either in its original or in a modified form, do so at their own risk, assume all responsibilities and, by use of this document, implicitly agree that they shall not hold the aforementioned College of Arts and Sciences, Dakota State University or Dr. Richard E. Bleil liable for injuries or accidents that occur in any lab.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Very rarely will an injury or accident occur in a well-supervised laboratory. When an injury or accident does occur, it is generally brought about by complacency. In this laboratory, you will hear a LOT about lab safety; you will be given safety instructions at the start of each lab, you will be told of the major hazards of each chemical you will be using, and you will be quizzed on safety. Sometimes, such an emphasis makes a student nervous about what may be a new learning environment for them. This is an unfortunate and unintentional side effect, but it is important to give such emphasis on safety to reduce the odds of injuries in the lab by being sure that students know what hazards exist, how to avoid them and how to respond if something does go wrong. Knowledge is the best defense against injury in a chemistry lab.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The best way to prevent accidents is for you to know the possible hazards of the laboratory. Any experiment, no matter how often it has been performed in the past, has the potential to fail with hazardous results. By knowing the hazards, you will develop a healthy respect for what is happening around you, and with this respect, heightened levels of observation are sure to follow. This implies that potential accidents can be spotted before they can occur. If there is ever anything that does not seem right to you, it is not only your right, but also your obligation to point them out to me, your instructor. I will do my part to keep you safe, but I will need your help.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The following sections present some general guidelines. These are not arbitrary rules set down to make your life less enjoyable. Each and every one of them has a specific purpose, which will hopefully be made clear to you. If not, ask! There will be a safety exam which you will be required to pass (90% or greater) before the fourth lab day. Even though this grade will not be a part of your final grade, you must pass this exam to continue in the lab, so take it seriously. On the other hand, it is not designed to trick you or to be particularly difficult. If you understand the following guidelines and the reasons behind each point, you will pass the exam.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Most of laboratory safety is common sense. Remember that this is a general guideline, and therefore may be incomplete. If you are ever unsure about safety, please ask.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Laboratory Apparel

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (1) Safety goggles are required in the laboratory AT ALL TIMES! Splash hazards are perhaps the most significant danger present in the lab, and eyes are extremely sensitive.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (2) Contact lenses are not permitted in the lab. Your goggles will protect your eyes from spill hazards, but do nothing to protect you from fumes, which can dry your contacts out and may result in the necessity of an operation for their removal. Contact lenses can also absorb chemicals from the air (especially the new "breathable" lenses), concentrate and hold them against the eye, and prevent proper flushing of the eye should a chemical be splashed into the eyes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (3) Laboratory aprons must be donned at all times. In the event of a spill, these aprons are chemical and flame resistant, and could save you from scar tissue!

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (4) Sandals, open-toed shoes and high heels are not permitted in the lab. This is to protect your feet from splashes and spills. The restriction on high heels is for balance.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (5) Shorts or skirts cut above the knee are not permitted in the lab. Again, should a spill occur, it will be your clothing that will be your protection from direct exposure of the skin to that chemical. The idea is to put as many layers of clothing as possible between you and a chemical spill. The more clothing, the more diffuse the chemical will be by the time it reaches the skin, and the greater the chance to remove the chemical before it reaches your skin.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (6) Careful consideration should be given before wearing any jewelry into the lab. Some chemicals evaporate very quickly and therefore pose relatively little danger should they get onto your skin. However, if they get beneath a ring, watch or some other form of jewelry, they can be prevented from evaporating, held against the skin longer and greatly increase the risk of injury. Should you decide to wear jewelry to the lb (as I will be wearing my watch), be particularly mindful of itching, burning or any other irritation under or around your jewelry. (By the way, NEVER wear opals, pearls, or other "soft gems" in the lab. The harsh laboratory environment may dry them out or otherwise damage them, and neither your instructor nor DSU will replace or repair such items.)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (7) Never wear clothes that hang, such as loose sleeves. Be sure ties and scarves are tucked well inside your laboratory apron. These pose fire hazards (if you are reaching or bending down near an open flame) as well as chemical hazards (if they accidentally get dragged through a chemical, they can transport that chemical directly to your skin). In fact, you may want to give very serious consideration to wearing only very old clothes. Some of my students have, in the

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (8) Long hair is to be constrained. Like hanging clothes, long hair is subject to fire and contact with chemicals. A rubber band will be used to constrain particularly long hair if necessary.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (9) No radios, tape players, CD players or any other devices of this type will be permitted in the laboratory at any time. Loud music is distracting, and headphones prevent you from hearing announcements or verbal warnings given in the lab.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Safety Equipment

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (1) Take the time to identify all of the laboratory safety equipment, and keep their location in your mind at all times. You should be able to close your eyes any time during a lab and point to such safety equipment as the fire extinguisher, the emergency eyewash stations, the fire blankets, the safety shower, etc. If you were to splash a chemical in your eyes, you'd better be able to find that eyewash station without your eyes well before permanent damage can occur (which can be seconds depending on the nature of the chemical).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (2) Check all safety equipment. I'll keep as close an eye on it as possible, but I need your help as well. Is the fire extinguisher charged? Does it have the plastic "seal"? Is there enough sodium bicarbonate in case there is a chemical spill? If anything does not look right to you, report it to your lab instructor IMMEDIATELY!

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (3) Material Data Safety Sheets (MSDS's) are available to you on request only. Basic safety information will be given during the safety lecture before each lab. Yow can also find links for MSDS's on my homepage at http://www.homepages.dsu.edu/bleilr/ if you are interested.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: General Behavior

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (1) ABSOLUTELY NO HORSEPLAY WILL BE TOLERATED IN THE LABORATORY! Offenders of this one will be unceremoniously cast out with a zero resulting for that day's work. I realize that at times it is awfully tempting to grab that water bottle and squirt your friends, but many hazardous chemicals look like water. The humor will be lost if something other than water is in that bottle.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (2) Always read the upcoming experiments carefully and thoroughly, being sure to understand all of the directions before entering the lab. This will help you to be prepared to handle any hazards of the experiment, and will also help you to perform the experiment more quickly resulting in less "fumbling around" and reckless work as you rush to finish on time. To ensure that you have read the upcoming experiment, you are required to complete the pre-lab
