layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: II. Ways of Thinking About Data

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Data is...

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The 1973 Webster's New Collegiate Dictionary defines data as "factual information (as measurements or statistics) used as a basis for reasoning, discussion, or calculation." The 1996 Webster's II New Riverside Dictionary Revised Edition defines data as "information, especially information organized for analysis." Merriam Webster Online Dictionary defines data" as the following (http://www.m-w.com):

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1: factual information (as measurements or statistics) used as a basis for reasoning, discussion, or calculation. E.g., the data is plentiful and easily available -- H. A. Gleason, Jr., e.g., comprehensive data on economic growth have been published -- N. H. Jacoby.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2: information output by a sensing device or organ that includes both useful and irrelevant or redundant information and must be processed to be meaningful.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3: information in numerical form that can be digitally transmitted or processed.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Taking from the above definitions, a practical approach to defining data is that data is numbers, characters, images, or other method of recording, in a form which can be assessed to make a determination or decision about a specific action. Many believe that data on its own has no meaning, only when interpreted does it take on meaning and become information. By closely examining data we can find patterns to perceive information, and then information can be used to enhance knowledge (The Free On-line Dictionary of Computing, 1993-2005 Denis Howe).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The number 1,099 is one example of data.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - "The number of children who were determined to have a disability prior to enrollment in Migrant and Seasonal Head Start for the 2004 enrollment year is 1,099" is information.

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: © AED/Tac-12 Spring 2006. Permission granted to copy for non-commercial uses only.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: What has been evident in disciplines such as education, public health, nutrition, nursing, and management, is now becoming evident in early care and education, including Head Start. Programs now recognize that the quality and quantity of data, be it statistical or descriptive, is needed to set baselines, identify effective actions, set goals and targets, monitor progress and evaluate impacts (World Bank Website http://www.worldbank.org/data/aboutdata/aboutdata.html).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One thing that Migrant and Seasonal Head Start programs can do well is gather data. Using an upstream program as an example, in late May the data gathering process is swift and fast during enrollment. If the data relates to a child or family it is shared among appropriate Head Start staff. When the program ends, the data is stored, and next thing you know it is March and the program is preparing for pre-service. The question that one is always left with is: what do we do with all this data and or information? One of the goals of this handbook is to help you answer this question.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Before you can present and interpret information, there must be a process for gathering and sorting data. Once again, 1,099 is a number - and this number is, in fact, data. The number 1,099 is a raw number - on its own it has no meaning. Just like many of the crops that our families pick are raw from which food is prepared, so too, can data be viewed as the raw material from which information is obtained.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Head Start requires the collection of data in a variety of areas. We collect data in all of the content service areas. Thus, data collection is something that is not just limited to children and families, but if the purpose and the questions relate to children and families it is definitely not good practice to collect data when the children and families are not available. The data you collect in Head Start can take many forms. The data could be in the form of numbers, words, pictures, maps, and even newspaper articles. When collecting data, we are faced with the inevitable question of which is better. The concept of which is better has the potential to lead to the qualitative versus quantitative debate, which although exhilarating to some, could cause havoc in program planning and implementation. These debates fail to achieve an honest understanding of how qualitative and quantitative data differ, because in many people's mind the difference between the two is underscored by the notion that one is better than the other.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Why the Soliloquy? Types of Data

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In research circles there has been a long-term debate over the merits of Quantitative versus Qualitative data. Key influences in this debate are based upon how researchers were taught, compounded by differences among individuals and their preference in relating to numbers or to words.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In reality, this debate is largely irrelevant in Head Start. In order to have a high quality program, we must collect both types of data. There are times when a quantitative

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: © AED/TAC-12 Spring 2006. Permission granted to copy for non-commercial uses only.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: approach will be better suited to the situation and vice versa. "Qualitative and quantitative methods are not simply different ways of doing the same thing. Instead, they have different strengths and logics and are often best used to address different questions and purposes (Maxwell, 1996,2005)." That being said, there are other times when it makes sense to "have the best of both worlds," and to use a combination of some quantitative and some qualitative data in order to credibly address a particular question and make well informed decisions.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Qualitative data

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Data that is represented either in a verbal or narrative format is qualitative data. These types of data are collected through focus groups, interviews, opened ended questionnaire items, and other less structured situations. A simple way to look at qualitative data is to think of qualitative data in the form of words. Later on, we will explore how the transcript below can be used as a source of data.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Quantitative data is data that is expressed in numerical terms, in which the numeric values could be large or small. Numerical values may correspond to a specific category or label.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Data Strategies

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There are a variety of strategies for quantitative and qualitative analyses, many of which go well beyond the scope of an introductory Handbook. Different strategies provide data analysts with an organized approach to working with data; they enable the analyst to create a "logical sequence" for the use of different procedures. In the boxes below, we offer four examples of strategies for quantitative analysis that you may consider as you work with and develop your skills in data analysis as well as reasons why you may consider using the strategy. Some of these strategies are used in Section V when looking at particular content area data.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Strategy: Visualizing the Data

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Involves: Creating a visual "picture" or graphic display of the data.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Reason(s): a way to begin the analysis process; or as an aid to the reporting/presentation of findings.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Strategy: Exploratory Analyses

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Involves: Looking at data to identify or describe "what's going on"? - creating an initial starting point (baseline) for future analysis.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Reason(s): Like you have a choice?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Strategy: Trend Analysis

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Involves: Looking at data collected at different periods of time.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Reason(s): to identify and interpret (and, potentially, estimate) change.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Strategy: Estimation

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Involves: Using actual data values to predict a future value.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Reason(s): to combat boredom after you have mastered all the previous strategies.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Also to answer PIR and Community Assessment items and tasks.

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: © AED/Tac-12 Spring 2006. Permission granted to copy for non-commercial uses only.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Visualizing Data

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Visualizing data is to literally create and then consider a visual display of data. Technically, it is not analysis, nor is it a substitute for analysis. However, visualizing data can be a useful starting point prior to the analysis of data.

layout_dets.text: Consider, for example, someone who is interested in understanding Migrant and Seasonal Head Start from a national perspective. Specifically, someone might be interested in the differences in funded enrollment across all MSHS grantees. layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Exploratory Analysis

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Exploratory analysis entails looking at data when there is a low level of knowledge about a particular indicator (teacher qualifications, first and second language acquisition, etc.) It could also include the relationship between indicators and/or what is the cause of a particular indicator.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Trend Analysis

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The most general goal of trend analysis is to look at data over time. For example, to discern whether a given indicator such as the number of children with disabilities has increased or decreased over time, and if it has, how quickly or slowly the increase or decrease has occurred. One aspect of trend analysis that is discussed in this Handbook and encouraged is that of comparing one time period to another time period. This form of trend analysis is carried out in order to assess the level of an indicator before and after an event.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Estimation

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Estimation procedures may occur when working with either quantitative or qualitative data. The use of both quantitative data such as poverty level data, can be combined with interviews from providers serving low income families to help determine the proportion of families in the area that are income eligible. Estimation is one of many tools used to assist planning for the future. Estimation works well for forecasting quantities that are closely related to demographic characteristics, eligible children and families, and social services. Estimation is the combination of information from different data sources to project information not available in any one source by itself.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: III. Conceptualizing Data Analysis as a Process

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: The "Problem" with Data Analysis

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: What does 'data analysis' mean? Does it refer to one method or many? A collection of different procedures? Is it a process? If so, what does that mean? More important, can MSHS program staff - without a background in math or statistics - learn to identify and use data analysis in their work? (P.S. - the answer to the last question is Yes! - assuming a minimum investment of time, effort, and practice).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Data analysis can refer to a variety of specific procedures and methods. However, before programs can effectively use these procedures and methods, we believe it is important to see data analysis as part of a process. By this, we mean that data analysis involves goals; relationships; decision making; and ideas, in addition to working with the actual data itself. Simply put, data analysis includes ways of working with information (data) to support the work, goals and plans of your program or agency.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: From this perspective, we present a data analysis process that includes the following key components:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Robotics technology increase drastically following the demand of intelligent robotics that able to help human kind. For robots to be intelligent in the way people are intelligent, they will have to learn about their world, and their own ability to interact with it, much like people do. Robot vision is a branch of robotics that learns about acquisition and image processing for intelligent robotics. At 2030, it is predicted that almost home duty task accomplished by service robot that use vision sensors such as camera, it is a big challenge for us to develop that robot. A robot is a mechanical or virtual agent, usually an electro-mechanical machine that is guided by a computer program or electronic circuitry. Intelligent robotics is a system that contains sensors, camera, control systems, manipulators, power supplies and software all working together to perform a task. That's why the ability to develop intelligent robotics using computer vision is a must to for the future.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The term Artificial Intelligence or AI stirs emotions. In 1955, John McCarthy, one of the pioneers of AI, was the first to define the term Artificial intelligence, roughly as follows:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The goal of AI is to develop machines that behave as though they were intelligent.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: According to McCarthy's definition the aforementioned robots can be described as intelligent. The word of robot is very familiar with us today [1]. The term robot was first used to denote fictional automata in a 1921 play R.U.R. Rossum's Universal Robots by the Czech writer, Karel Čapek. According to Čapek, the word was created by his brother, Josef from the Czech "robota",

In 1927, Fritz Lang's Metropolis was released; the Maschinenmensch ("machine-human"), a gynoid humanoid robot, also called "Parody", "Robotrix", or the "Maria impersonator" (played by German actress Brigitte Helm), was the first robot ever to be depicted on film [2].

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The history of robots has its origins in the ancient world. The modern concept began to be developed with the onset of the industrial revolution which allowed for the use of complex mechanics and the subsequent introduction of electricity. This made it possible to power machines with small compact motors. In the early 20th century, the modern formulation of a humanoid robot was developed. Today, it is now possible to envisage human sized robots with the capacity for near human thoughts and movement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At \(\sim 270\mathrm{BC}\) an ancient Greek engineer named Ctesibus made organs and water clocks with movable figures. Al-Jazari (1136-1206), a Muslim inventor during the Artuqid dynasty, designed and constructed a number of automatic machines, including kitchen appliances, musical automata powered by water, and the first programmable humanoid robot in 1206. Al-Jazari's robot was a boat with four automatic musicians that floated on a lake to entertain guests at royal drinking parties. His mechanism had a programmable drum machine with pegs (cams) that bump into little levers that operate the percussion. The drummer could be made to play different rhythms and different drum patterns by moving the pegs to different locations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A robot has these essential characteristics:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1) Sensing, First of all your robot would have to be able to sense its surroundings. It would do this in ways that are not unsimilar to the way that you sense your surroundings. Giving your robot sensors: light sensors (eyes), touch and pressure sensors (hands), chemical sensors (nose), hearing and sonar sensors (ears), and taste sensors (tongue) will give your robot awareness of its environment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2) Movement. A robot needs to be able to move around its environment. Whether rolling on wheels, walking on legs or propelling by thrusters a robot needs to be able to move. To count as a robot either the whole robot moves, like the Sojourner or just parts of the robot moves, like the Canada Arm.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3) Energy. A robot needs to be able to power itself. A robot might be solar powered, electrically powered, battery powered. The way your robot gets its energy will depend on what your robot needs to do.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4) Programmability, it can be programmed to accomplish a large variety of tasks. After being programmed, it operates automatically.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5) Mechanical capability, Enabling it to act on its environment rather than merely function as a data processing or computational device (a robot is a machine).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6) Intelligence, A robot needs to be smart. This is where programming enters the pictures. A programmer is the person who gives the robot its 'smarts.' The robot will have to have some way to receive the program so that it knows what it is to do.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A manipulator is a device used to manipulate materials without direct contact. The applications were originally for dealing with radioactive or biohazardous materials, using robotic arms, or they were used in inaccessible places. In more recent developments they have been used in applications such as robotically-assisted surgery and in space. It is an arm-like mechanism that consists of a series of segments, usually sliding or jointed, which grasp and move objects with a number of degrees of freedom.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Robot manipulators are created from a sequence of link and joint combinations. The links are the rigid members connecting the joints, or axes. The axes are the movable components of the robotic manipulator that cause relative motion between adjoining links. The mechanical joints used to

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The arm-and-body section of robotic manipulators is based on one of four configurations. Each of these anatomies provides a different work envelope and is suited for different applications.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1) Gantry - These robots have linear joints and are mounted overhead. They are also called Cartesian and rectilinear robots.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2) Cylindrical - Named for the shape of its work envelope, cylindrical anatomy robots are fashioned from linear joints that connect to a rotary base joint.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3) Polar - The base joint of a polar robot allows for twisting and the joints are a combination of rotary and linear types. The work space created by this configuration is spherical.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4) Jointed-Arm - This is the most popular industrial robotic configuration. The arm connects with a twisting joint, and the links within it are connected with rotary joints. It is also called an articulated robot [3].

layout_dets.text: Robot Vision

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There are several important terms in the robot vision interconnected, including computer vision, machine vision and robot vision. Computer vision is the most important technology in the future in the development of interactive robots. Computer Vision is a field of knowledge that focuses on the field of artificial intelligence and systems associated with acquisition and image processing. Machine vision is implemented process technology for image-based automatic inspection, process control, and guiding robots in various industrial and domestic applications. Robot vision is the knowledge about the application of computer vision in the robot. The robot needs vision information to decide what action is to be performed. layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: WHAT ARE FLORIDA-FRIENDLY LANDSCAPES?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Florida-Friendly Landscapes protect Florida's unique natural resources by conserving water, reducing waste and pollution, creating wildlife habitat, and preventing erosion. Any landscape can be Florida-Friendly if it is designed and cared for according to the nine Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ principles, which encourage individual expression of landscape beauty. In 2009, the Florida Legislature found that the use of Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ and other water use and pollution prevention measures to conserve or protect the state's water resources serves a compelling public interest and that the participation of homeowners' associations and local governments is essential to the state's efforts in water conservation and water quality protection and restoration. Make your landscape a Florida-Friendly Landscape — do your part to create a more sustainable Florida!

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: WHAT IS A FLORIDA-FRIENDLY LANDSCAPE?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A Florida-Friendly Landscape is a quality landscape that is designed, installed, and maintained according to the nine Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ principles. The nine principles seek to reduce environmental impact from landscaping by properly applying water, fertilizer, and pesticides, creating wildlife habitat, preventing erosion, recycling yard waste, and employing other practices based on University of Florida research.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Not all Florida-Friendly Landscapes look alike. A wide variety of forms, styles, and types are available to the designer. Florida-Friendly Landscapes may incorporate both native and non-native plants. One Florida-Friendly yard may use a rain garden to filter stormwater runoff, while another may attract pollinators with specific nectar plants. But if cared for according to the nine principles, a Florida-Friendly Landscape can produce aesthetically pleasing, low-maintenance results that may add value to your property while helping to protect the state's natural resources.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: THE FLORIDA-FRIENDLY LANDSCAPING? PROGRAM

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Preserving and protecting Florida's water resources is the focus of the Florida-Friendly LandscapingTM (FFL) Program, which promotes the nine principles with public outreach and education statewide. The FFL Program is a joint venture of the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) and the University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences (UF/IFAS). The FFL Program works in cooperation with the state's five water management districts and other agencies and organizations to achieve the common goals of water conservation and water quality protection.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: LANDSCAPE DESIGN & PLANT SELECTION

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: So, how do plant selection and landscape design contribute to saving water and preventing pollution? The first Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ principle—"Right Plant, Right Place"—involves designing a landscape efficiently and choosing plants that fit the site. This helps reduce maintenance inputs, including irrigation, fertilization, mowing, and application of pesticides, which in turn lowers the risk of pollutants finding their way into ground or surface waters. Keeping excess nitrogen and phosphorous out of the water improves the health of water bodies and by extension the whole ecosystem. This guide will help you to create a landscape that works with the natural environment, rather than against it. Such a landscape, if maintained correctly, will require less money, time, and effort on your part, while still looking healthy and beautiful.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: HOW TO USE THIS BOOK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Florida-Friendly LandscapingTM Guide to Plant Selection and Landscape Design is intended as a companion to The Florida Yards & Neighborhoods Handbook (4th ed., 2009). The Handbook is available through your county Extension office or online at http://fyn.ifas.ufl.edu/. The Handbook describes in detail the nine Florida-Friendly LandscapingTM (FFL) principles that are the bedrock of the FFL Program. This guide is intended for homeowners who want to take the next step and design their own Florida-Friendly Landscapes. Included in this book is information on landscape design strategies, a landscape planning worksheet, and the FFL Plant List containing many of the UF/IFAS-recommended Florida-Friendly plants for each region of the state.

layout_dets.label: 页脚
layout_dets.text: FLORIDA-FRIENDLY LANDSCAPING? GUIDE TO PLANT SELECTION AND LANDSCAPE DESIGN ? 2010

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: The Nine Florida-Friendly Landscaping? Principles

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The nine Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ principles are the cornerstone of the Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ Program. Based on UF/IFAS science, the principles teach homeowners, builders and developers, landscape maintenance professionals, and other Florida citizens how to implement environmentally sound design and maintenance techniques in their landscapes. The principles are outlined briefly here. For more detailed information, please refer to the FFL state office Web site (http://fyn.ifas.ufl.edu) or to The Florida Yards & Neighborhoods Handbook.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #1: RIGHT PLANT, RIGHT PLACE

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Plants well-suited to their site need less irrigation and fertilizer and are more resistant to pest infestation. Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ principles encourage the selection of the right plant for the right place, helping you create a healthy, attractive landscape that works with the natural ecosystem rather than against it. Match plants with site conditions based on USDA zone, water and light requirements, soil conditions, salt and wind tolerance, and other factors. The FFL Plant List can help you make the right plant selections for your landscape.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #2: WATER EFFICIENTLY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Overwatering not only depletes water supplies, it raises your water bill and makes landscapes more prone to pest infestation. If needed, irrigate plants according to UF/IFAS-recommended rates and application schedules, taking into account local restrictions issued by your water management district. Water only when plants show signs of wilt, preferably in the early morning. Check your irrigation system regularly for leaks and clogs. Do not water if it has rained in the past 24 hours, or if rain is forecast in the next 24 hours. By law you must install, maintain, and operate a device such as a rain sensor that prevents operation of your automatic irrigation system during periods of sufficient moisture.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #3: FERTILIZE APPROPRIATELY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If fertilization is needed, use UF/IFAS-recommended rates and application schedules to get a healthier lawn and garden. Fertilizing at the correct times and in the correct amounts not only supplies plants with the nutrients they need, it helps prevent fertilizer runoff and leaching that can get into our water supplies and interfere with ecosystem and human health. Fertilizing at the rates recommended by UF scientists helps avoid the excessive growth, pest problems, and higher water requirements that over-fertilization causes.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #4: MULCH

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ methods recommend using mulch to protect against soil erosion, maintain soil moisture, inhibit weed growth, improve soil structure and aeration, and reduce pesticide use. A Florida-Friendly Landscape will feature one of the types of mulch recommended in The Florida Yards & Neighborhoods Handbook in its planting beds.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #5: ATTRACT WILDLIFE

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Florida-Friendly LandscapingTM encourages Floridians to make their yards attractive to birds, bees, bats, and other creatures displaced by rapid urban development. Supply berry bushes, a bird bath, or a bat house; increase vertical layering to provide habitat; manage household pets and reduce insecticide use—all these tricks can welcome wild visitors in need of refuge. Many of these will return the favor by eating pest insects and helping to pollinate your garden!

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #6: MANAGE YARD PESTS RESPONSIBLY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ Program advocates a more holistic approach to pest control than merely spraying chemicals. Integrated Pest Management (IPM) creates an effective defense against yard pests while minimizing environmental impact. IPM emphasizes smart planning, proper maintenance, and natural or low-toxicity controls to ensure that plants stay healthy and resist disease and insect infestation. Chemical treatments may still be necessary in some cases, but use of toxic materials will be minimized by this approach.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #7: RECYCLE

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A Florida-Friendly Landscape recycles yard waste generated by activities like mowing, pruning, and raking. Use these leftovers as mulch or compost, returning valuable nutrients to your landscape. Save money and enrich your soil by composting grass clippings, weeds, and plant trimmings and using the compost as an amendment.

layout_dets.label: 图片选项
layout_dets.text: A Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ Publication

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #8: MANAGE STORMWATER RUNOFF

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A Florida-Friendly Landscape uses porous pavers, rain barrels or cisterns, rain gardens, and swales and berms to keep rainwater on site and allow it to percolate into the ground or be captured for later use. Reducing the amount of runoff and the chance for rainwater to wash quickly into storm drains—carrying yard clippings, fertilizer, pesticide, dirt, oil, and other toxins—is the goal of managing stormwater runoff.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: PRINCIPLE #9: PROTECT THE WATERFRONT

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Implementing Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ design and maintenance methods helps protect water bodies from pollution. If you live on a lake, bay, river, or other water body, keep fertilizers, pesticides, and other toxins away from the water by preserving a 10-foot maintenance-free zone between your landscape and the water. Do not mow, fertilize, or apply pesticides in that area. Even if you do not live immediately on the waterfront, the pesticides and fertilizers you apply in your landscape affect the health of local water bodies through a drainage system called the watershed. The choices you make at home have much farther-reaching consequences than you might imagine.

layout_dets.label: 页脚

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Designing Your Florida-Friendly Landscape

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Florida-Friendly Landscapes are all based on the same nine principles. But Florida-Friendly LandscapingTM encourages individual expression of beauty. As long as you apply the principles described in The Florida Yards & Neighborhoods Handbook, your landscape can be Florida-Friendly and as individual as you want.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: WHAT IF I LIVE IN A PLANNED COMMUNITY?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Check with your homeowner association before you make changes to your landscape. HOAs, usually have a landscape review board and can regulate the appearance and types of plantings in your yard, as long as they do not prohibit you from installing and maintaining Florida-Friendly Landscapes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If you live in a community with codes, covenants and restrictions that could be more Florida-Friendly, encourage your association to adopt all or part of the model Florida-Friendly Landscaping™ restrictions, found at http://fyn.ifas.ufl.edu/.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Florida-Friendly LandscapingTM Program has a number of "success stories" which highlight water and costs savings for communities that adopt Florida-Friendly LandscapingTM and maintenance practices. Visit the Web site at \underline{http://fyn.ifas.ufl.edu/.}

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Before Reading:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. In this story, Marcella will find something special. Do you have something you found? What is it? Where did you find it?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Where is Marcella in the first picture? What can you see in the room?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. What do you think Marcella will find in this room?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella liked to visit her Grandma's old house. When she was at her Grandma's house, she played up in the attic. Marcella found many old toys and things there.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One day, Marcella was up in the attic as usual. She was tired because she was playing for a long time, so she sat down to rest.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: She looked around and saw a box in the back of the room. "What could be in that box over there?" she thought. She stood up and climbed over some old chairs and tables. Finally, she got to the box.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: She opened it, but it was too dark to see. Marcella brought the box over to the window where she could see better in the sunshine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: She found a little white hat and put it on her head. In an old bag, she found some dolls wearing old clothes. And there was a picture of a very pretty little girl with long hair. Then Marcella pulled out an old rag doll with only one button eye, a painted nose, and a smiling mouth. Her dress was made out of soft cloth. It was blue with pretty little flowers all over it.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Stories

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella was so happy. She picked up the rag doll and ran downstairs to show it to her Grandma.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Well! Well! Where did you find her?" Grandma asked. "It's old Raggedy Ann!" Grandma gave the doll a hug. "I forgot about her. She has been in the attic for fifty years! Well! Well! Dear old Raggedy Ann! She needs her other eye right away!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella watched Grandma sew the button on Raggedy Ann. Grandma told Marcella how she played with Raggedy Ann when she was a little girl.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Now," Grandma laughed, "Raggedy Ann, you have two new button eyes. Now you can see the changes in the world! And, Raggedy Ann, you have a new friend. I hope you and Marcella will have as much happiness together as you and I did!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then Grandma gave Raggedy Ann to Marcella. She said, "Marcella, this is my very good friend, Raggedy Ann. Raggedy, this is my granddaughter, Marcella!" And Grandma helped Raggedy Ann shake Marcella's hand.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Oh, Grandma! Thank you so much!" Marcella said as she gave Grandma a hug and kiss. "Raggedy Ann and I will have so much fun."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And that was how Raggedy Ann became part of the doll family at Marcella's house. This book is about Raggedy Ann's stories.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: After Reading:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Who is Raggedy Ann? What does Raggedy Ann look like?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. What was Raggedy Ann missing?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. You are a grandparent. You want to share something from your childhood with your grandchild. What would you give him or her?

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Learns a Lesson

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 2. Raggedy Ann Learns a Lesson

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Before Reading:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Raggedy Ann learns an important lesson in this story. What are three important lessons that children should learn?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Take a look at all of the pictures in this story. What do you think is going to happen?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Do you think the dolls will talk and do things on their own? Why do you think so?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella's dolls were always very good and did not move while she was in the room. One day Marcella put her dolls against the wall. She told them to be good little children while she was away. When Marcella left the room, the Tin Soldier smiled at Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When the dolls heard the front gate close, they knew that they were alone in the house. "Now let's have some fun," said the Tin Soldier. They all stood up. "Let's find something to eat."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Yes, let's find something to eat," said all the other dolls.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "When Marcella took me to play outside today, we went to a door at the back of the house. I smelled something very good," said Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Then you must take us there," said Lisa.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I think it would be a good idea to make Raggedy Ann our leader for this trip," Uncle Clem said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: All the other dolls smiled and shouted, "Yes, Raggedy Ann is our leader!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann felt happy and said she would be their leader.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Follow me," she said and started walking across the room.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Stories

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The other dolls ran after her. They went through the house until they came to the kitchen door. "This is the door," said Raggedy Ann. Now all the other dolls could smell something good. They knew it would be very nice to eat.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But none of the dolls were tall enough to open the door. They pulled. They pushed. But the door stayed closed.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The dolls were talking and pulling and pushing. At times one doll would fall down. Then other dolls would climb on her to open the door. But the door wouldn't open. Finally, Raggedy Ann sat down on the floor.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When the other dolls saw Raggedy Ann sitting with her hands on her head, they knew she was thinking.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Shh, Shh!" they said to each other. They sat quietly in front of her.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "There must be a way to get in the kitchen," said Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Raggedy says there must be a way to get inside," said all the dolls.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I can't think clearly today," said Raggedy Ann. "It feels like I have a hole in my head."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Lisa ran to Raggedy Ann and took off her cap. "Yes, there is a hole in your head, Raggedy!" she said. Then she took a needle from her dress and used it to sew shut the hole in Raggedy's head. "It does not look very good, but I think I closed it!" she said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I feel so much better!" said Raggedy Ann happily. "Now I can think clearly."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Now Raggedy can think clearly!" shouted all the dolls.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "My thoughts were running out of the hole before!" said Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "They were running out, Raggedy!" shouted all the other dolls.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Now that I can think clearly," said Raggedy Ann, "I think the door must be locked and to get in we must unlock it with the key. See, there is a key in the door!"

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Learns a Lesson

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "But the lock is too high for us!" said Helen. "What can we do?"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Yes, what can we do?" the Tin Soldier said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: No one had any idea.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After thinking for a minute more, Raggedy Ann said, "I know what we'll do." She asked Jumping Jack to try to open the door. Jack had a stick that was good for jumping. He jumped higher and higher on his stick. He jumped up to the key, turned it, and unlocked the door.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then the dolls all pushed. The door opened.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The dolls ran into the kitchen. They all wanted to be the first to get to the food.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They quickly climbed up on the kitchen cupboard. They ran quickly and they pushed each other. One of the dolls pushed over a bottle of milk. The bottle fell on Lisa. The milk spilled out and made Lisa's dress wet.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Uncle Clem found some bread. He sat down and started to eat it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A jar of raspberry jam fell over, and the dolls began eating the jam. They ate so much jam that their faces became purple.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Tin Soldier fell off the cupboard three times. But he climbed up again and again.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The dolls had so much fun. They ate as much as they could. Suddenly, they heard the front gate open.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Stories

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They jumped to the floor and ran back to their room as fast as they could.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But they were too late. Just as Marcella came into the room, the dolls stopped moving.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "This is funny!" said Marcella. "They were all sitting in a line when I left! Why are they in different places now? Did my dog Fido move them?"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then she saw Raggedy Ann's face and picked her up. "Oh Raggedy Ann, you are covered with jam!" Marcella put Raggedy Ann's hand in her mouth. "Yes! It's jam! Oh, Raggedy Ann! You've been to

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: the kitchen! The other dolls were with you, too!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then Marcella dropped Raggedy Ann on the floor and left the room.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When she came back, she picked up all the dolls and put them in a basket. Then she took them outside.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There, she washed all the dolls until they were clean. Then she hung them on the clothesline in the sunshine to dry. The dolls hung there all day.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I think she washed my face so hard that my smile's almost gone!" said Raggedy Ann, after an hour of silence.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "No, it's still there," said the Tin Soldier.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Just then the wind blew strongly and Helen fell to the grass below.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Learns a Lesson

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Late in the afternoon Marcella came out with a table and chairs. Then she took all the dolls from the clothesline and sat them on chairs around the table.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They all drank lemonade and ate small cookies with sugar on them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When they finished eating, the dolls were taken into the house. Marcella combed their hair and dressed them in pajamas.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella placed them in their beds and kissed each one good night. Then she walked

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: quietly out of the room.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The dolls did not talk for a few minutes. Then Raggedy Ann said, "I've been thinking!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Listen!" said all the other dolls, "Raggedy's been thinking."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Yes," said Raggedy Ann, "I've been thinking. Marcella gave us nice things to eat under the trees to teach us something. I think she wanted to teach us that we must never take without asking. So let's remember this. We'll try never to do anything that makes the people who love us unhappy."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Yes, let us all remember," cried all the other dolls.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And Raggedy Ann, with a happy look in her button eyes, lay back in her little bed. Her cotton head was filled with thoughts of love and happiness.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: After Reading:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. What did Raggedy Ann and her doll friends do?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. What did Marcella do with the dolls?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. What lesson did Raggedy Ann learn? Do you think it's a good lesson? Do you know someone who took something without asking? What happened?

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Stories

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 3. Raggedy Ann and the Washing

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Before Reading:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Who does the work around your house (washing dishes, washing clothes, cleaning up, and so on)? Do you help around the house? What do you do?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. What is something different about Raggedy Ann's face in the first picture?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. In this story, Raggedy Ann was washed. Guess what happened to her during and after the wash.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dinah was the housekeeper for Marcella's family.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One day, Marcella's Mamma looked out of the window and saw Marcella run up to Dinah and take something out of Dinah's hand.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Oh, Dinah! I can't believe you did that!" Mamma heard Marcella say to Dinah.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then Marcella sat on the ground and put her head in her arm. She started crying.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: So Mamma went outside and sat down next to Marcella. "What's wrong, my love?" Mamma asked.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella held up Raggedy Ann to show her mamma. Raggedy Ann looked so funny! Mamma had to smile when she looked at the doll.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dinah could not understand why Marcella cried. She loved Marcella and did not want to make Marcella sad.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But Raggedy Ann was not sad at all. She knew that she looked funny, but she continued to smile. Her smile was wider than ever.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This is because Raggedy Ann knew what happened.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann and the Washing

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: She remembered that morning when Marcella came to take off the pajamas from the dolls and dress them for the day. Marcella was already upset. She was not happy as she dressed each of the dolls.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann thought at the time, "Perhaps she got up on the wrong side of the bed!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And when it was Raggedy Ann's time to be dressed, Marcella was not careful. She was upset because she had hurt her finger when dressing Lisa.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then Marcella heard her friend calling her name from outside. She threw Raggedy Ann on the floor and she ran quickly out of the room.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: She didn't know that Raggedy had landed in the laundry basket.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A few minutes later, Dinah came into the room with some dirty clothes to be washed. She put them all on top of Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then Dinah carried the basket out to the back of the house and washed them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dinah put all the clothes into a big pot and poured water on them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then she put the pot on the stove.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When the water began to get warm, Raggedy Ann climbed on top of the clothes and looked out of the pot. There was so much steam that she couldn't see anything. Dinah could not see Raggedy Ann, either.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dinah used a big stick to move the clothes around in the big pot. The clothes and Raggedy Ann moved around while the water boiled.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then Dinah took the clothes out of the big pot one at a time and washed them. She finally got to Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Of course Dinah did not know that Marcella had thrown Raggedy into the laundry basket by mistake. She thought Marcella really wanted Raggedy Ann to be washed. So she put soap on Raggedy and washed her on the washboard.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Two buttons from the back of Raggedy's dress and one of Raggedy Ann's

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: button eyes fell off. After washing Raggedy and all the clothes, Dinah tried to dry Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Stories

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It was just then that Marcella came back and saw Raggedy.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Oh, Dinah! I can't believe you did that!" Marcella cried and quickly took the wet Raggedy Ann from Dinah's hand.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That was when Mamma heard Marcella and saw her cry. Mamma held Marcella's hand and talked to her softly. Soon, Marcella stopped crying.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dinah told everyone that she didn't know that Raggedy was in the wash until she took Raggedy from the big pot. When Marcella heard that, she began crying again.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It was all my fault, Mamma!" she cried. "I remember now. I threw Raggedy Ann as I ran out the door. She fell in the laundry basket! Oh! Oh!" and she hugged Raggedy Ann tight.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Mamma was not angry with Marcella. Mamma knew Marcella already felt very sorry. So Mamma just put her arms around Marcella and said, "But just look at Raggedy Ann. She doesn't seem to be unhappy!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella wiped her tears away and looked at Raggedy Ann. Raggedy was all wet, but she had a funny smile on her face. Marcella laughed. And Mamma and Dinah had to laugh, too, because Raggedy Ann's smile was bigger than it had been before.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Let me hang Raggedy Ann on the line in the bright sunshine for half an hour," said Dinah, "and she'll be fine again!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: So Raggedy Ann was put on the clothesline, out in the bright sunshine. There, she enjoyed the breeze and listened to the birds in a nearby tree.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann and the Washing

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Every once in a while, Dinah went out to turn and pat Raggedy. Finally, Raggedy became soft and dry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then Dinah took Raggedy Ann into the house. She showed Marcella and Mamma how clean and sweet she was.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella took Raggedy Ann up to her room. She told all the dolls what had happened to Raggedy. She also said that she was very sorry about being upset in the morning when she dressed them. Of course the dolls couldn't say anything, so they only looked at Marcella with love in their eyes. Marcella sat in her little red chair and hugged Raggedy Ann tightly in her arms.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann looked up at Marcella sweetly with her one button eye. On her face was the same old smile of happiness and love.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: After Reading:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Why was Raggedy Ann washed?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Did Raggedy Ann enjoy the washing? How do you know?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Do you think it was okay for Marcella to be mad at Dinah? Why do you think so?

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Stories

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 4. Raggedy Ann and the Kite

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Before Reading:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. What activities do you enjoy doing outside with your friends?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. In this story, Raggedy Ann flies high up in the air. What do you think might happen to her?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Look at the picture of Raggedy Ann and the birds. What do you think the birds are doing to Raggedy Ann?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One day Marcella was playing with her friends. Raggedy Ann was with her. The children were making a kite. They used sticks and cloth to make the kite.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They made a tail for the kite. Then they tied a large ball of string to the kite.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The kite was ready to fly now. One boy held the kite. A second boy held the string.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There was a nice wind, and the kite needed the wind to fly in the sky. The boy with the string said, "Let it go." The other boy held the

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: kite up in the air. Then he let the

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: kite go. The boy with the string started to run.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The kite flew very high in the sky. Raggedy Ann was happy to see it fly so high. But then something happened to the kite. It began flying this way and that way. The kite made four or five circles in the air. Then it fell to the ground.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It needs a longer tail!" one boy said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The children asked each other where they could get more cloth to make a longer tail for the kite.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Let's tie Raggedy Ann to the tail," said Marcella. "I know she'll like to fly in the sky!"

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann and the Kite

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The boys thought this was a good idea. So, they tied Raggedy Ann to the tail of the kite.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This time the kite flew straight up into the air. It flew very high. Raggedy Ann enjoyed being up in the sky. She could see very far. The children looked very small from the sky.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Suddenly, a strong wind came. She heard the wind singing as it pulled the kite faster and higher.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then, Raggedy Ann felt something tear. It was the cloth that tied her to the kite. As the wind blew harder, the tear became bigger.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella saw Raggedy Ann fly high above the ground. She thought that Raggedy Ann was having a lot of fun. She also wanted to fly in the sky with Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After some time, Marcella grew tired of looking at the kite. She wanted to go home.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Can you please pull down the kite now?" she asked the boy with the string. "I want Raggedy Ann."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Let her fly some more," the boy said. "We'll bring her down later. We want to make the kite go higher!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella didn't want to leave Raggedy Ann with the boys, so she sat down to wait.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: From the ground, Marcella couldn't see the wind tearing the cloth that held Raggedy Ann to the kite. Raggedy Ann could feel that she was not tied tightly any more. She was getting looser and looser.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Suddenly, the cloth tore all the way. Raggedy was not tied to the kite tail anymore! But she did not fall. The wind blew into Raggedy's skirt. She went flying away from the kite.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella jumped up when she saw Raggedy Ann flying away from the kite. Without Raggedy Ann, the kite couldn't fly straight any longer. Finally, it fell to the ground.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We'll get Raggedy Ann for you!" the boys said to Marcella. All the children ran to where the kite had fallen. They ran and ran. At last, they found the kite on the ground. But they could not find Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Maybe she fell in your garden!" a boy said to Marcella. "The kite was above your garden when she fell!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: All the children went to Marcella's garden. But they did not find Raggedy Ann there.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella was very sad. She went into her house and told Mamma what happened. Then Marcella went to her room and lay on her bed.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann Stories

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Her Mamma went out to look for Raggedy Ann. But she couldn't find Raggedy Ann either. When Daddy came home in the evening he also looked for Raggedy Ann. But he could not find her. Marcella didn't want to do anything. She didn't want to play with any of her other dolls. And she cried for a long time that night.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Finally, she fell asleep. She dreamed that Raggedy Ann came back to her. She woke up crying. Mamma heard her and came to her bed. She told Marcella that in the morning Daddy would look for Raggedy Ann again.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I shouldn't have given Raggedy Ann to the boys to tie to the kite!" Marcella cried, "I want her to come back to me."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Mamma took Marcella in her arms and said sweet things to her. But Mama thought that Raggedy Ann was lost and would never be found again.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Now, where do you think Raggedy Ann was?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When Raggedy Ann fell from the kite, the wind took her a long way. It took her to Marcella's garden. She fell into the top of a big tree in the garden. In the tree, two birds had a nest. They heard Raggedy Ann fall into the tree.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They were angry with Raggedy Ann for falling so close to their nest.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann did not move for a long time. The birds stopped being angry and became curious. They asked her who she was. But Raggedy Ann did not say anything to them. She did not move. She only smiled at them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Soon Mamma Bird told Daddy Bird, "See her hair! We can use it in our nest."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: So the birds jumped closer to Raggedy Ann. They asked her if they could take some of her hair for their nest. Raggedy Ann did not say anything to them. She only smiled at them. So, the two birds pulled at Raggedy Ann's hair until they had some for their nest.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Raggedy Ann and the Kite

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Evening came and the birds sang their lullabies. Raggedy Ann saw the stars come out in the sky.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The next morning, the birds pulled more hair from Raggedy Ann's head. They also moved her. Now, she could see the ground. She saw that she was in a tree in her own garden.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: She saw Marcella looking for her again. Soon Marcella found Raggedy. And this is how she did it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Mamma Bird had seen Marcella with Raggedy Ann in the garden many times. So she started singing, "Chirp! Chirp!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Daddy Bird also started singing, "Chirp! Chirp! Chirp!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marcella looked up into the tree when she heard the birds singing. Then she saw Raggedy Ann in the tree.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: She felt very happy. "Here is Raggedy Ann," she shouted.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Mamma and Daddy came out and saw Raggedy Ann. Daddy climbed up the tree and brought Raggedy Ann down. He put her in Marcella's arms.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "You'll never fly on a kite again, Raggedy Ann!" said Marcella, "I'll never let you leave me again."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: So Raggedy Ann went into the house and had breakfast with Marcella. Mamma and Daddy were very happy when they saw Marcella playing with Raggedy Ann.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: After Reading:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. What happened to Raggedy Ann after she was untied from the kite?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Who had the idea to put Raggedy Ann on the kite? Do you think it was a good idea?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Think of three things that are very special to you. What are some ways you can make sure you won't lose them?

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Organization and management of the district hospital surgical service

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1.1 THE DISTRICT HOSPITAL

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: You, your staff, systems and site

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The hospital plays a unique role in any community:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - It is the focus of many health care services

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - It can provide a significant amount of local employment

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - It is a point of intersection for members of different communities

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - It may be a community in its own right

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - It must be involved in community public health education and political solutions to common health problems.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Organizations grow and change; hospitals are no different.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As a doctor or senior health care provider, you may be the most highly trained person in a district hospital. In this capacity, other hospital staff will expect leadership to be a part of your job.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As a leader (especially if you are newly arrived), other members of the health care team or the community may turn to you with frustrations or with hopes for solutions to problems. These tasks may not be directly related to your work on the wards or in the operating room, but they will become part of your job.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When assuming a new role or advanced leadership responsibilities, one of the challenges is to see what is familiar as if you were seeing it for the first time. It is difficult but important to avoid bringing old ideas or grudges to a new position. Use your past experiences, but also begin a new role with a broader view and an attitude unbiased by prejudgements. When you arrive in a new place or take on a new job or role at a familiar place, be alert to the physical and human resources and try to learn as much as possible about the work and culture of the place.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Familiarize yourself with the people, hospital and its resources. Try to get an overview of the organizational and communications systems that are used (not just those that are supposed to be used, but what is really happening).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Approach a new work environment or job as you would approach a patient by taking a full history and examination. Be observant and attentive to all aspects of the encounter. Asking questions is important; be a good listener.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: KEY POINTS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Leadership is a part of your job

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Apply the medical skills of evaluation and planning to your work as a manager

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Respect the knowledge and expertise of senior hospital staff

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Every institution has a history and the legacy of what has happened and why things have worked or not worked is held in the memory of the employees

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The pride people feel in their workplace and the services they offer is a valuable commodity and is the greatest resource of any health care facility.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Surgical Care at the District Hospital

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hear what people have to say. Try to understand what works well, where the problems lie and what the hopes of your co-workers are.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It will not be possible to understand everything at once or to fix all problems, but a full history and examination of the site provides the starting point for understanding and improvement. Any efforts to change practices or introduce new ones should include consultation with representatives of all interested parties; this is part of taking the "history" of the place and is equivalent to talking to the family members of a patient. As with patients, any management plan needs to be worked out with the people involved and carried out as a partnership.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As a health care provider, you will be entering into the lives of others who will have worked hard to create and maintain the place in which they work. Being sensitive to this will help you to fit in. The pride people feel in their workplace and the services they offer is a valuable commodity and is the greatest resource of any health care facility.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Community partners

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The district hospital is part of a wider community of people and agencies, all of whom are working to improve the health of individuals, communities and society. Remember that these people and groups are your friends and allies. In discouraging times you can help one another and, by working together, can make things better. Find out who the other individuals and groups are and reach out and work with them – you have much to teach and learn from each other.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In addition to identifying the opinion leaders, you must be sensitive to any groups or subgroups whose voices are unlikely to be heard. You must find ways of reaching out and listening to them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Health is a concern for all people and can provide an opportunity to bring people together across divisions. In areas of conflict, when the district hospital and other parts of the health care system are accessible to all members of society without prejudice, it can provide an example of cooperation and develop the feeling of belonging to a broader and more inclusive group which respects and meets common needs.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: KEY POINTS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The leader is not expected to make all the decisions or do all the work, but must encourage others and co-ordinate efforts; the final responsibility for any endeavour rests with the leader

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Leadership requires a set of skills that can be learned and developed over time.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1.2 LEADERSHIP, TEAM SKILLS AND MANAGEMENT

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A leader is best when people barely know he exists. Not so good when people obey and acclaim him. Worse when they despise him. Fail to honour people, they fail to honour you. But of a good leader, who talks little When his work is done, his aim fulfilled, The people will say "We did this ourselves".

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Lao-tse

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Organization and management of the district hospital surgical service

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: ROLE OF THE LEADER WITHIN A HEALTH CARE TEAM

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Health care providers are only a part of the health team which includes support staff, administrative staff and those at satellite locations. The team consists of a group of people who share a common health goal and common objectives, as determined by community needs. Each member contributes according to his or her competence and skills and in coordination with the others.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The health care team exists to serve the community. Even if working for a manager or other employer, you are ultimately responsible to the people you serve clinically: the community and users of your service. It is from these people and groups that you must seek direction. Observing, listening and learning, discussing and deciding, organizing, participating and informing are the foundation of the relationship between the community and the team.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The leader is not expected to make all the decisions or do all the work, but must encourage others and coordinate efforts. Final responsibility for any endeavour rests with the leader.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Responsibility is the essence of leadership.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Leaders can be given authority by the group or by an outside power, they can assume authority or earn authority and responsibility. They can be appointed, elected or chosen by a group. Leadership can be shared by two or more people or rotated within a group. In an informal situation, different members of a group may take leadership roles with respect to different issues or tasks. It is important that all members of a group share the same idea of what the leader's role will be.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some people adopt leadership roles with greater ease than others, but there are no born leaders. Leadership requires a set of skills that can be learned and developed over time. They include:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Listening

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Observing

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Organizing

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Making decisions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Communicating effectively and working well with others

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Encouraging and facilitating others

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Fostering enthusiasm and vision

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Goal setting and evaluation

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Giving and receiving feedback

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Coordinating the efforts of others

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Chairing a meeting

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Being willing to accept responsibility.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Surgical Care at the District Hospital

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: LEADERSHIP STYLES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There are many different leadership styles.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Democratic

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The leader is chosen by the group and is expected to act with the wishes of the group in mind. The leader follows a course of action that represents the will of the group. Not everyone may agree, but most people mostly agree.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Autocratic

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The decisions are made by the leader and the other members of the group are expected to follow. In this situation, one person makes the decisions and tells the others what to do.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Laissez-faire

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The laissez-faire leader allows the members of the group unconstrained freedoms.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Anarchic

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: No leadership is shown and individuals or groups of people do what they want and resist efforts to organize or coordinate.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Consensus

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Members of the group attempt to find a mutually agreeable solution or course of action. This is not so much a leadership style as a group style where all members agree on a course of action

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Situational

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: No single style of leadership will work in all situations; different situations will demand different styles of leadership. A leader who is responsive to the group and the situation is practising situational leadership.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In times of crisis, an autocratic leader can make sure that things get done quickly and efficiently. When time and situation permit, democratic and consensus based leadership can be very effective and make people feel more involved and can even increase satisfaction and morale within groups.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: COMMUNICATION

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: An effective communicator:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Listens

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Speaks clearly so that others will understand

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Confirms understanding and asks others to do the same

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Does not use jargon

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Asks for questions and encourages others to speak

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Is patient

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Presents information in small amounts

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Does not overwhelm others.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Organization and management of the district hospital surgical service

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Think about how people communicate in your hospital:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - What works and what does not work?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - How could you do more of what works and less of what does not?

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Listening

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Listening is a culturally based activity and skill. In some situations, eye contact is appropriate and avoiding eye contact can be seen to be evasive whereas, in others, eye contact is seen as being very aggressive and diverting one's eyes is a sign of respect. No matter what the cultural norms, effective listening is active, not passive. Active listeners are attentive – they communicate interest and concern with their words and body language. Effective listeners summarize what they have heard and how they understand what has been said. This allows for clarification and early correction of misunderstandings. Everyone likes to be heard and listening is a way of showing respect and concern.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: WORKING WITH OTHERS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A skilled leader recognizes the expertise and input of others. Different things motivate different people, but everyone likes to do work of value, to do it well and to be recognized for it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The effective leader can help people stay motivated and interested:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Achievement: help people achieve work related and personal goals

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Recognition: give praise when it is due

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Responsibility: help others take responsibility

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Advancement: help others train for promotion and learn new skills

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Self-improvement: provide opportunities for personal development

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - The work itself: explain the value of work, make work meaningful; if possible, allow people to do work which appeals to them, or allow people to pursue special projects or ideas they may have

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Involvement: when people work hard for an organization or cause they are investing in it, not financially but personally and emotionally; this leads to feelings of pride and responsibility – a sense of ownership.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Just as there are ways of motivating people, recognize the factors that may discourage them and create dissatisfaction:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Poor personal relations

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Poor leadership

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ● Low pay

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Unsafe or unpleasant working conditions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Inefficient administration

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Incompetent supervision.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Remember that healthy organizations:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Orient new members to the group and the ways the group works

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Have ways of dealing with challenges, questions, discussions and disagreements

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: KEY POINTS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Active listeners are attentive - they communicate interest and concern with their words and body language

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Effective listeners summarize - what they have heard and how they understand what has been said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: KEY POINTS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Help people and groups find common ground in times of difference and conflict

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Be a role model: in the way you work, demonstrate the behaviours you value.

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: Surgical Care at the District Hospital

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Encourage new ideas and efforts

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Are places that people want to join and to stay.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The staff may have representation from groups in society which may have a history of conflict or be actively engaged in conflict.
