layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1 EUROPE

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Russian and US officials hold talks in Saudi Arabia

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Leading Russian and US officials met in Saudi Arabia this week for high-stakes talks aimed at ending Moscow's nearly three-year war in Ukraine, with Kyiv and Europe excluded from the negotiations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The swift push to organise the talks came after last week's call between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, where the two leaders discussed opening negotiations on the war. The meeting in Riyadh marked the first in-person discussions between top officials from the countries in years, after a sharp downturn in relations following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. It was expected the talks could lay the groundwork for a Trump-Putin summit.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The talks followed a tumultuous week for European officials in which Trump revealed he had held a 90-minute conversation with his Russian counterpart, Putin. Then, in a speech at the Munich security conference last Friday, the US vice-president, JD Vance, launched a brutal ideological assault on Europe, accusing its leaders of suppressing free speech, failing to halt illegal migration and running in fear from voters' true beliefs.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The big story Page 10→

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 2 GERMANY

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Two dead and 37 injured after Munich car attack

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A two-year-old girl and her mother died from injuries suffered in the car-ramming attack in Munich last Thursday that left 37 others injured, police said. An Afghan man was arrested on suspicion of deliberately driving a car into a trade union demonstration. Police said the 24-year-old asylum seeker, identified by German media as Farhad N, may have had Islamist extremist motives for the attack. After the incident, the suspect uttered the words "Allahu Akbar" (God is greatest) to police officers and also prayed, prosecutor Gabriele Tilmann said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The attack came shortly before the 23 February election in which immigration is a key issue, following several attacks blamed on migrants.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Spotlight Page 17→

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 3 UNITED STATES

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Approval of supreme court sought for watchdog firing

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Donald Trump's administration has asked the supreme court to approve the firing of the head of a federal agency dedicated to protecting whistleblowers in the first appeal of Trump's new term.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hampton Dellinger, the head of the office of the special counsel (OSC), is among the fired watchdogs who have sued the administration, arguing their dismissals were illegal and that they should be reinstated.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The OSC is "a secure channel for federal employees to blow the whistle by disclosing wrongdoing".

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Spotlight Page 32 \(\rightarrow\)

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 4 AUSTRIA

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Man who rammed knife attacker hailed as hero

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A Syrian migrant living in Austria has been hailed as a hero after he rammed his car into an attacker, bringing down a radicalised assailant who had killed one teenager and left five injured.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The stabbing, described by Austria's interior minister as having been carried out by a Syrian man who was legally living in the country and who had become radicalised by the Islamic State group, happened last Saturday in the southern city of Villach.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As the country mourned, many hailed the bravery of Alaaeddin al-Halabi, a delivery driver who left Syria in 2015 and who had been driving past the area when he noticed a commotion. He slowed down, he said, "because there were many people, some running, some scared, and some were shouting for help".

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It was then that he noticed that one of the people at the scene had a knife. "I immediately understood what was happening - there were people on the ground bleeding, and this person was waving the knife in a threatening manner."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 5 VATICAN CITY

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Pope Francis in hospital for tests after infection

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Pope Francis was to remain in hospital for as long as required after tests undertaken this week showed a "complex clinical picture", the Vatican has said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The pontiff, 88, was admitted to Gemelli hospital in Rome last Friday with worsening bronchitis and was diagnosed and treated for a respiratory tract infection.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The results of the tests carried out in recent days and today have demonstrated a polymicrobial infection [caused by two or more microbes] of the respiratory tract, which has led to a further modification of the therapy; the Vatican said in a statement.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 6 CANADA

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: At least 18 injured after plane crash lands in Toronto

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A plane carrying 80 people crash landed at Toronto Pearson airport on Monday, flipping upside down and leaving at least 18 people injured. Video from the scene showed a Delta Air Lines plane belly-up on snow-covered tarmac and people walking away.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Two people in a critical condition were airlifted to a nearby trauma centre and one child was taken to a hospital in downtown Toronto. Twelve others sustained minor injuries.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The flight - operated by the Delta subsidiary Endeavor Air - had flown from Minneapolis in the US. The US Federal Aviation Authority said all 80 people onboard had been evacuated.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 7 BRAZIL

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Brasilia asks UN to ditch carbon levy on shipping

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The government asked the UN to throw out plans for a new levy on global shipping that would raise funds to fight the climate crisis, despite playing host to the next UN climate summit.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The proposed levy on \(\mathrm{CO}_{2}\) emissions from shipping was due to be discussed at a meeting of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) this week. Brazil, China, Saudi Arabia and 12 other countries oppose the plans. They argued last month that a levy could reduce exports from the developing world, raise food prices and increase inequalities.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 9 FRANCE

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Language test for residence could stump some locals

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The government has been accused of making some of its language tests for foreigners seeking to stay in the country so hard even its own citizens would fail them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: An impact report on a new immigration law expected to come into force later this year, suggested the requirement for applicants to have at least the level of French of a secondary school pupil, aged 11-15 years, could lead to 60,000 people being refused permission to remain in France.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The tests, which cost around €100 ($105), are part of a bill passed a year ago that includes tighter border controls and tougher measures to expel foreign migrants.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 8 ENVIRONMENT

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: UN aviation meetings remain clouded in secrecy

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Aviation industry delegates outnumbered those from green groups by 10 to one at the previous conference of the UN's committee on aviation environmental protection (CAEP), an analysis has found. Other recent meetings held by CAEP's parent body, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), were sponsored by large fossil fuel companies and airlines, including Saudi Aramco and Etihad. Critics accuse the ICAO of having been captured by the industry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A meeting of CAEP was held this week but there was no public information on its agenda or the people who will be running the conference. The ICAO has been criticised for a lack of transparency.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 10 CULTURE

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Conclave celebrates a divine night at the Baftas

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Conclave, Edward Berger's Vatican-set thriller starring Ralph Fiennes as a cardinal overseeing the election of a new pope, was the big winner at this year's Baftas with four awards: for best picture, outstanding British film, adapted screenplay and editing.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Brutalist, Brady Corbet's epic drama about a Hungarian modernist architect working in post-war America, went home with best director, leading actor (for Adrien Brody), cinematography and score.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Anora's Mikey Madison took the best actress prize over frontrunner Demi Moore for The Substance.

layout_dets.text: 21 February 2025 The Guardian Weekly

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 11 MALI

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Collapse of illegally run goldmine kills 48 people

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At least 48 people were killed in the collapse of an illegally operated goldmine in the west of Mali, authorities and local sources have said. Mali is one of Africa's leading gold producers, and mining sites are regularly the scene of deadly landslides and accidents. Authorities have struggled to control unregulated mining of the precious metal in the country, which is among the world's poorest.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Some of the victims fell into the water," a police spokesperson said. "Among them was a woman with her baby on her back."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The accident took place at an abandoned site formerly operated by a Chinese company.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 13 DR CONGO

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: M23 rebels take Bukavu in latest seizure of territory

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: M23 rebels have captured and occupied Bukavu, the capital of South Kivu, the Congolese government confirmed, days after the Rwanda-backed militia entered the city.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In a statement posted on X, the DRC communications ministry said it was "doing everything possible to restore order, security and territorial integrity".

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: M23 fighters entered Bukavu last Friday, after advancing south following the group's capture of Goma, the capital of North Kivu, last month. The militia faced little resistance.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 12 SOUTH AFRICA

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: First 'openly gay imam' shot to death in his car

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Muhsin Hendricks, considered the world's "first openly gay imam", was shot dead near the southern city of Gqeberha, South African police have said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The imam, who ran a mosque intended as a safe haven for gay and other marginalised Muslims, was in a car with another person last Saturday when a vehicle stopped in front of them and blocked their exit, police said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A police spokesperson said: "Two unknown suspects got out of the vehicle and started firing. The motive for the murder is unknown and forms part of the ongoing investigation."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 14 SUDAN

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Plan for first Russian naval base in Africa agreed

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A plan for Russia to establish its first naval base in Africa will go ahead, Sudan's foreign minister confirmed, after years of delays over the Red Sea military port. If the agreement is implemented, Russia would join the US and China in the region; they have bases to the south in Djibouti.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The announcement came during a visit by the foreign minister, Ali Youssef Ahmed al-Sharif, to Moscow where he met his Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After their meeting, Sharif said the two countries were in "complete agreement" on establishing a Russian base "and there are no obstacles".

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The lunch-hour rush in Copley Square has cooled.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dozens of delivery drivers in dark balacavas and the occasional helmet sit back on their mopeds lining both sides of Boyston Street, waiting for their phones to chirp. At last, an Uber Eats notification pops up on one driver's screen with an order from a noodle shop in Chinatown. It's a 23-minute delivery to Dorchester. The pay: $3.52.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This area outside Chick-fil is one of many hot spots around the Boston region where drivers have started gathering, often grouped by their home countries - Dominicans in one area, Haitians in another - to satisfy residents' seemingly insatiable appetite for takeout.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Food delivery by two-wheeled motorized vehicles is a growing phenomenon in Boston and other cities like New York and Washington, D.C., largely carried out by a growing migrant population. The faster drivers go, the more money they stand to make, and it's led to a rising tide of complaints: mopseds going the wrong way in bike lanes, running red lights, weaving between cars, narrowly avoiding pedestri

layout_dets.text: Fake electors are among GOP delegates

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Convention includes at least 17 who falsely asserted Trump won in 2020

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: By Sam Brodey GLOBE STAFF

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: WASHINGTON - Nearly four years ago, 84 Republicans across seven states where Joe Biden won signed official-looking documents falsely attesting that then-President Donald Trump was actually the rightful winner in their states.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: These so-called fake electors - so named because they came forward pretending to be official Electoral College votes for Trump - became emblems of Trump's effort to remain in power.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Now, some of them are playing a role in something else: Trump's effort to return to the White House in 2024.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When Republicans converge for their convention in Milwaukee next month to again nominate Trump for president, at least 17 people who participated in fake elector schemes will be present as official GOP delegates or alternate delegates, according to publicly available records and a Globe review of the delegate selection process.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In total, five fake electors from Nevada, three from Arizona, three from Pennsylvania, two from Michigan, two from Wisconsin, one from Georgia, and one from New Mexico are headed to the convention.

layout_dets.text: MIDDLEBOROUGH - There's no single reason why 11-year-old Hunter Scanlon repeats to go to school.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Crushed in war, more are willing to speak out

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
By Raja Abdulrahim
and Iyad Abuheweila
NEW YORK TIMES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: JERUSALEM - On Oct. 7, as the Hamas-led attack on Israel was unfolding, many Palestinians took to the streets of the Gaza Strip to celebrate what they likened to a prison break and saw as the sudden humiliation of an occupier.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But it was just a temporary boost for Hamas, whose support among Palestinians in Gaza has been low for some time. And as the Israeli onslaught has brought widespread devastation and tens of thousands of deaths, the group and its leaders have remained broadly unpopular in many parts of the world. More Gaza residents have even been willing to speak out against Hamas, risking retribution.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In interviews with nearly a dozen people in Gaza in recent months, a number of them said they held Hamas responsible for starting the war and helping to bring death and destruction upon them, even as they blame Israel first and foremost.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One Gaza resident, Raed al-Kelani, 47, said Hamas always acts in its own interests.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “It started Oct. 7, and it wants to end it on its own terms,” said al-Kelani, who worked as a civil servant for the former Palestinian Authority government in Gaza, which was run by a rival faction to Hamas before Hamas seized control of the territory in 2007.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But time is ticking with no potential hope of ending this," he added. Al-Kelani now makes meals and distributes food aid in shelters for displaced Palestinians in Gaza. "Hamas is still seeking its slice of power, he said. Hamas does not know how to get down from the tree it climbed.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some of the Gaza residents who spoke to The New York Times said that Hamas knew it would be starting a devastating war with Israel that would cause heavy civilian casualties, but that it did not provide any food, water, or shelter to help people survive it. Hamas leaders have said they wanted to ignite a permanent state of war with Israel on all fronts as a way to revive the Palestinian cause and knew that the Israeli response would be big.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Throughout the war, hints of dissent have broken through, sometimes even as Gaza residents were mourning loved ones killed by Israeli attacks. Others waited until they left the enclave to condemn Hamas - and even then were at times reluctant in case the group survives the war and continues to govern Gaza.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In March, well-known Gaza photojournalist Motaz Azaiza caused a brief social media firestorm when he obliquely criticized Hamas after he left the territory. He was one of a handful of young local journalists who had been exposed to national prominence early in the war for documenting the death and destruction on social media.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “If the death and hunger of their people do not make any difference to them,” he wrote in an apparent reference to Hamas, “they do not need to make any difference to us. Cursed be everyone who trafficked in our blood, burned our hearts and homes, and ruined our lives.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some Palestinians attacked him over the comments, and Azaiza felt compelled to defend himself publicly. But inside Gaza, many agreed that he was giving voice to a sentiment that had grown over the course of the war.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gauging public opinion in Gaza was difficult even before the war began. For one, Hamas, which long controlled the territory, perpetuated a culture of fear with its oppressive system of torture and exacted repression against those who criticized it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Now, polling has become even more difficult, with most of the 2.2 million Palestinians in Gaza displaced multiple times by the war, constant breakdowns in communications, and

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: constant Israeli military offensives.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Still, some recent surveys reflect the weak or mixed support in Gaza for Hamas and its leaders. In some cases, contradictory results underline the complications in surveying a transient population during the fog of war.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In March, a survey by the West Bank-based Institute for Social and Economic Progress asked Gaza residents how they felt about Hamas leaders. About three-quarters opposed Yahya Sinwar, the group's Gaza-based leader, and a similar share opposed Ismail Haniyeh, the movement's political leader in exile.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “When you realize six months in or seven months in that Gaza is completely destroyed, your life as a Gazan is completely destroyed, that’s where people are coming from when they are not supportive of Sinwar or Haniyeh,” said Obada Shtaya, a Palestinian and a founder of the Institute for Social and Economic Progress.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Other polls painted a more mixed picture. A poll conducted by the Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research in Gaza and published this past week showed that support in Gaza for Hamas leaders is slightly higher, but the share who are satisfied with Hamas leadership in the territory has risen since December.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But it also showed that support for Hamas continuing to govern the territory had decreased slightly in the past three months.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Basem Naim, a Hamas spokesman, said that public support for Hamas in Gaza was no less than 50 percent. That includes Hamas members in Gaza - which he said numbered more than 100,000 - and their families.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “Are there people in Gaza who blame Hamas? Of course,” he told the Times. “We aren’t saying that 100 percent of Gaza residents are Hamas supporters or are happy with what happened,” he added.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "In the end," he said, "this is a natural thing in societies that some people are for and some who are against. And we welcome this position."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some of the nearly one dozen people in Gaza the Times spoke about Hamas say this war has lasted longer than any previous conflict between Israel and an armed Palestinian faction in Gaza in part because Hamas seeks not only to survive, but to cling to a certain fate if it does, there is no guarantee that future wars with Israel will not plunge Palestinians in Gaza back into the same misery.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hamas says it will not agree to any cease-fire deal with Israel that leads only to a temporary truce, wary that the war would restart once the Israeli hostages are freed. The group says it wants a permanent cease-fire.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Naim said that if Hamas had such low popularity numbers as

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: a result of the war, then it should be left to elections that allow Palestinians to choose their representatives. But over the past decades, Palestinians in Gaza and the Israeli-occupied West Bank have made few opportunities to express their voice in democratic elections.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The two territories are separated geographically, and while Hamas has governed Gaza for more than a decade, the more moderate Palestinian Authority administers some parts of the West Bank.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Fatah party, a rival to Hamas, lost a legislative election to Hamas in 2006. The next year, Hamas fighters routed Fatah

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: forces from Gaza and forcibly seized control of the territory. The political chasm between Hamas and Fatah has, in large part, hindered elections then.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Naim blamed Israel and the United States for disrupting past Palestinian elections.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One Gaza resident who in recent months fled to Egypt with her family said that she hears regularly from friends and family that they do not want the war to end before Hamas is defeated in 2014. She said Hamas had prioritized its own aims over the well-being of the Palestinians they purport to defend and represent.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Vehicle explosion kills 8 Israeli soldiers, official says

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
By Aaron Boxerman  
NEW YORK TIMES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: JERUSALEM - Eight Israeli soldiers were killed while riding in an armored vehicle in the southern Gaza Strip on Saturday, the Israeli military said, as the Israeli offensive in Gaza had been a casualty of Rafak continued to exact a toll among its troops.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The deaths occurred around 5:15 a.m. as Israeli troops operated in the northwest part of Tel al-Sultan, a neighborhood in western Rafah, the Israeli military said. The eight soldiers, who belonged to the military's engineering corps, were riding in an armored vehicle when the blast occurred, the military said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hamas, the Palestinian armed group, said in a statement that its militants fired anti-tank missiles at Israeli military vehicles in western Rafah, killing some soldiers. It was not immediately clear whether it was an explosive device that damaged the vehicle or anti-tank missile fire, Rear Admiral Daniel Hagari, the Israeli military spokesperson, told reporters.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The explosion damaged the vehicle but might have also ignited munitions inside, Israeli military officials said, adding that the blast was severe enough to make finding and identifying the bodies difficult.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Israel has fought for more than eight months in Gaza in the wake of the Hamas-led attack on Oct. 7, which killed roughly 1,200 in Israel - mostly civilians - and took about 250 others hostage. More than 36,000 people have been killed in Gaza since the beginning of the war, according to Palestinian health officials, who do not distinguish between combatants and civilians.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hamas has fought a dogged guerrilla war, resisting Israel's efforts to decisive

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ly defeat the organization, take down its leaders, and bring back many of those abducted during the surprise Oct. 7 attack. According to the Israeli military, the campaign has killed an estimated 13,000 to 14,000 militants in the Israeli officials have not provided evidence for the calculation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: More than 300 Israeli soldiers have been killed since the Israeli ground invasion of Gaza began in late October. At the end of January, about 20 Israeli soldiers were killed as a result of demolishing buildings inside Gaza near the border with Israel.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu publicly mourned the soldiers' deaths and called for Israel to remain committed to its military's goals of destroying Hamas, bringing home the hostages, and “ensuring Gaza can no longer threaten Israel.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "There is no substitute for victory,"奈廷yah said, adding, "Do not let anyone distract you from the simple and clear fact: We must remain dedicated to the war aims, despite the heavy and agonizing price."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Netanayahu has been criticized by parts of the Israeli public, the families of hostages held in Gaza, and former security officials. Some argue that only a settlement with Hamas will return the remaining 120 living and dead captives; others have argued that his failure to articulate a clear postwar alternative to Hamas has left the country trapped in a holding pattern in Gaza.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Israeli forces rescued four hostages in a rescue operation in central Gaza last weekend that also left scores of Palestinians dead, according to local health officials. Hagari applauded the mission but added, "We must be honest - we cannot bring home everyone in this manner."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "They could have surrendered a long time ago and saved us from all this suffering," said the woman, who asked not to be interviewed. "I fear of possible retribution if her criticism were made public.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Even for Palestinians who chided under Hamas's iron grip on Gaza for more than a decade, Oct. 7 gave them a feeling, at least initially, that this was a battle of liberation from Israeli occupation. Much of Gaza's population are either refugees or descendants of refugees who fled to Gaza in previous-day Israel after the government declared or forced to flee during the war surrounding the establishment of the Israeli state. They have never been allowed to return.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When Hamas attacked Israel, most people in Gaza supported that “form of resistance,” said a 26-year-old lawyer from Gaza who also asked not to be named.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “But what we don’t support is them continuing with this war when they have not accomplished any of the goals they set out to accomplish,” the lawyer said. “This isn’t resistance. This is insanity.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hamas's stated goals for the attack touched mostly on broader Palestinian aspirations beyond Gaza's borders. And some residents of the territory have long felt that during each new round of war between Hamas and Israel, the group is seeking to raise its global profile and champion more universal Palestinian causes at the expense of ordinary Gaza residents.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One of Hamas's aims was to free Palestinian prisoners held by Israel, some of them from Gaza, but others from the West Bank and east Jerusalem. It also wanted to stop Israel from exerting increased control over Al-Aqsa Mosque in the Old City of Jerusalem – one of Islam's holdest sites – and to stop the expansion of Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The more that Hamas pushed those objectives rather than ending the war quickly, Gaza residents said they felt other Palestinians were winning their freedom at their expense.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I do not want to sacrifice my life, my home, and house for anyone," Ameen Abed, a resident of Jabalia in northern Gaza, said at the time of one of the prisoner releases.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Who are you to impose this kind of life on me? My home has gone because someone's imprisonment will end after four months, why?" he said, "What did I benefit from?"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: While Hamas and even the Israeli hostages were in the underground tunnels, he said, Gaza residents were above ground with no protection from Israeli and US-made bombs dropped over their heads every day. That is an oft-heard complaint by Hamas’s critics in Gaza.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "There is uncontrolled anger against Hamas," he said. "It threw the Palestinian people into the bottom of the well."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
DUBAL, United Arab Emirates  
— Iran and Sweden carried out a prisoner swap Saturday that saw Tehran release a European Union diplomat and another man in exchange for an Iranian convicted in Stockholm of committing war crimes over his part in 1988 mass executions in the Islamic Republic. The arrest of Hajnal Nouri by Sweden in 2019 as he traveled to a hotel in the Netherlands demonstrated the detentions of the two Swedes, part of a long-running strategy by Iran since its 1979 Islamic Revolution to use those with ties abroad as bargaining chips in negotiations with the West. While Iranian state television claimed without evidence that Nouri had been "illegally detained," Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristerson said diplomat Johan Pledorus and a second Swedish citizen, Saeed Azizi, had been facing a "hell on Iran." Iran has already given Swedes a new criminal negotiation game with the aim of getting the Iranian citizen Hajnal Nouri released from Sweden, Kristerson said Saturday. "It has been clear all along that this operation would require difficult decisions." (AP)

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text:
ITALY  
Activist held in Budapest freed

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ROME - Italian anti fascist activist Ilaria Salvis returned to her parents' house in the northern Italian city of Monza on Saturday evening, after being freed from house arrest in Budapest the day before. "A nightmare is over," her father Roberto Salis told journalists. "Now we must ensure that this accusation for which Ilaria believes she is innocent is dropped," he added. Ilaria Salis was released after being elected as a new member of the European Parliament for the Italian Green and Left Alliance earlier this month. The 39-year-old activist was elected during the 1980s when he was arrested in Hungary, where she is on trial and faces charges for allegedly assaulting far-right demonstrators. European Parliament lawmakers enjoy substantial legal immunity from prosecution, even if the allegations relate to crimes committed prior to their election. More than 170,000 voters in Italy wrote Salis' name onto the ballot in a bid to bring her home from Hungary, where she has been detained for more than a year. (AP)

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text:
ENGLAND
Answers sought on police hitting cow

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: LONDON - Britain's interior minister on Saturday demanded an "urgent explanation" after police officers were filmed ramming a runaway cow with their car. The Surrey Police force said it had referred itself to the police ethics watchdog over the incident. The force said officers responded on Friday evening to reports of a loose cow "running at members of the public" in Staines-upon-Thames, just outside London, and damaging a car. It said officers spent several hours trying to catch the animal, and eventually "a decision was made to stop it using a police car." Footage published on social media showed a cow running in a residential road being hit by a police car, getting up, and then being hit again. The cow sustained a large cut to its leg and was being treated by a vet, police said. (AP)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Vice President Kamala Harris and Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelinsky (foreign) were among the attendees.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Swiss conference lacks Russian cooperation

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
By Jamey Keaten and Aamer Madhani  
ASSOCIATED PRESS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: OBBURGEN, Switzerland — Dozens of world leaders converged on a Swiss resort Saturday to discuss how to bring peace to war-ravaged Ukraine, though any hopes of a real breakthrough were muted by the absence of Russia.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: More than two years into the war, the combatants remain as far apart as they've ever been, with Kyiv sticking to its demands that Russia leave all Ukrainian territory it has seized and Moscow pressing on Russia for a binding offensive that has already taken large swaths of eastern and southern Ukraine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Despite Russia's absence from the conference at the Birgenstock resort overlooking Lake Lucerne, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky suggested that one measure of the two-day event's success was "bringing back to the world the

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: idea that joint efforts can stop war and establish a just peace.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Attendees faced a tricky balancing act, with many chastising Russia for breaking international law while hedging their positions to leave the door open for Moscow to join future peace talks that might bring about an end to the conflict one day.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “Here, there are representatives from Latin America, Africa, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, the Pacific, North America, and religious leaders,” Zel

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ensky said. "Now, there is no Russia here. Why? Because if Russia was interested in peace, there would be no war."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “We must decide together what a just peace means for the world and how it can be achieved in a truly lasting way,” he said. “At the first peace summit, we must determine how to achieve a just peace, so that at the second, we can already settle on a real end to the war.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: About half of the roughly 100 delegations were led by

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: heads of state and government. Analysts said turnout would be a key indicator about how much pull Ukraine and its staunch Western bankers have had in the broader international community.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday sought to cast a shadow over the Swiss-Ukrainian initiative for the conference. Some countries such as India, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia that have retained ties, at times lured into conflict – unlike Western powers that have sanctioned Russia over the war – were also on hand.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Saudi Arabia's foreign minister, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, told the conference that credible peace talks will need Russia's participation and require "difficult compromise."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Turkey’s foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, acknowledged the mistrust between Russia and Ukraine, stating “each side regards the other party’s steps (in floating proposals) as an extension of broader war efforts.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “Excellencies, I must also note that this summit could have been more results-oriented if the other party to the conflict Russia was present in

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: the room," he added.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Entering the venue, President Gitanas Nauseda of Lithuania, a NATO member country that has been one of the most stalwart supporters of fellow former Soviet republic Ukraine, said Russian troops must leave the region. The warshaw must be held accountable for crimes there and pay reparations for the war damage.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Right now it seems unrealistic, but I think we have to stay united, and if international society will push the Russian Federation, everything is possible," he told The Associated Press. "I don't think that assimilation is very clear. Ukraine has to seek territorial integrity."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Vice President Kamala Harris, representing the United States while President Biden attended a fund-raiser in California, reiterated America's full backing for Ukraine and announced \(1.5 billion in new US assistance for an array of projects such as energy infrastructure and civilian security.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: China, which backs Russia, joined the scores of countries that sat out the event. Beijing has stated that any peace process would require the participation of

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Russia and Ukraine, and has floated its own ideas for peace.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In a separate initiative last month, China and Brazil agreed to six "common understandings" toward a political settlement of the Ukraine crisis, asking other countries to play a role in promoting peace talks to be held "at a proper time" with both Russia and Ukraine involved.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The standoff over Ukraine is steeped in security implications for Europe it is the continent’s deadliest conflict since World War II and major-power geopolitics.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: US intelligence officials say China has increased sales of machine tools, microelectronics, and other technology to Russia that Moscow is using to produce missiles, tanks, aircraft, and other weaponry to fuel its war effort.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “What is clear is that China is not here, and I presume they’re not here because Putin asked them not to come and they obliged Putin,” said Biden’s top foreign policy advisor, Jake Sullivan. “And I think that says something about where China stands with respect to Russia’s war in Ukraine. I think countries should take notice of that.”

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Haiti replaces police chief as gang violence claims officers' lives

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
By Evens Sanon and Dánia Coto  
ASSOCIATED PRESS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: PORT-AU-PRINCE, Haiti - Haitian leaders have ousted Frantz Elbe, the beleaguered director of Haiti's National Police, following months of criticism that he wasn't doing enough to protect officers under assault by gangs.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A government official not authorized to speak to the media told the Associated Press on Saturday that former Haitian police chief Normil Rameau will once again take the helm of an underfunded and ill-equipped department that a UN report notes has only around 4,000 officers on duty at a time in a country of more than 1 million inhabitants. Rameau had been dismissed from the past nearly four years ago under a different administration.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: More than 2,500 people were killed or injured across Haiti in the first three months of the year, and gang violence has continued to surge.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Among those killed are nearly two dozen police officers, overwhelmed by gangs that control 80 percent of Port-au-Prince and are better equipped and have more powerful weapons. The most recent killings targeted three officers from a newly formed anti-gang tactical unit who were on patrol in an armored vehicle. A fourth remains missing.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Since 2015, more than 320 police officers have been killed, with 120 of them slain under Elbe's administration, according to a survey released this week by the local nonprofit group National Network for the Defense of Human Rights.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rameau's appointment comes as a newly selected prime minister and Cabinet take the reins of Haiti's government with a transitional presidential council at their side.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rameau previously served as police director-general under slain former President Jovenel Moise, who appointed him in

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: August 2019. Prior to that, he oversaw the detective division. He was ousted as police chief in November 2020 after Prime Minister Joseph Jouthe accused him of being incompetent and failed to find results at a time when gangs were seizing control of more territory.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Neither Rameau nor Elbe returned messages for comment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Haiti's Office of Citizen Protection praised the selection of Rameau as police chief and demanded that he act swiftly to stop gang activity and establish a security plan to curb violence.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It also urged police to push judicial authorities to open investigations into the killings of citizens, including journalists, and into what it called the "spectacular" escape of more than 4,500 prisoners in March after gangs stormed Haiti's two biggest cities. It said that the attack took place with the complete indifference of Elbe and the former ministers of justice and public security.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Haiti’s police unions had repeatedly called for Elbé’s resignation and arrest, noting that gangs have raided and burned at least 30 police stations and substations in recent months as part of a series of attacks that began on Feb. 29 and targeted critical state infrastructure, leading to the eventual resignation of former Prime Minister Ariel Henry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On Wednesday, a police union known as SPNH-17 held a news conference to condemn the state of the department and deplore the deaths of the officers.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Look at these young men, hacked to death," spokesman Garry Jean-Baptiste said as he pointed to rows of pictures behind him that depicted officers killed on duty.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Meanwhile, another police union known as SYNAPOHA called on newly installed Prime Minister Garry Conille this week to make strengthening the department a priority.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “The prime minister must see the need to have another team at the top,” the union said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Divers find parts of Finnish WWII plane

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Soviet shot down Kaleva with US diplomat aboard

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
By Jari Tanner  
ASSOCIATED PRESS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: HELSINKI — The World War II mystery of what happened to a Finnish passenger plane after it was shot down over the Baltic Sea by Soviet bombers appears to finally be solved more than eight decades later.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The plane was carrying American and French diplomatic couriers in June 1940 when it was downed just days before Moscow annexed the Baltic states. All nine people on board the plane were killed, including the two-member Finnish crew and the seven passengers - an American diplomat, two French, two Germans, a Swede, and a dual Estonian-Finnish national.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A diving and salvage team in Estonia said this week that it had located well-preserved parts and debris from the Junkers Ju 52 plane operated by Finnish airline Aero, which is now Finnair. It was found off the tiny island of Keri near Estonia's capital, Tallinn, at a depth of around 230 feet.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “Basically, we started from scratch. We took a whole different approach to the search,” said Kaido Peremees, spokesman for the Estonian diving and underwater survey company Tuukri-toode OU, as he explained the group’s success in finding the plane’s remains.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The downing of the civilian plane, named Kaleva, en route from Tallinn to Helsinki happened on June 14, 1940 - just three months after Finland had signed a peace treaty with Moscow following the 1939-40 Winter War.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The news about the fate of

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The plane was met with disbelief and anger by authorities in Helsinki who were informed that it was shot down by two Soviet DB-3 bombers 10 minutes after taking off from Tallinn's ?lemiste airport.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “It was unique that a passenger plane was shot down during peacetime on a normal scheduled flight,” said Finnish aviation historian Carl-Fredrik Geust, who has investigated Kal‐eva's case since the 1980s.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Finland officially kept silent for years about the details of the aircraft's destruction, saying publicly only that a "mysterious crash" had taken place over the Baltic Sea, because it didn't want to provoke Moscow.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Though well documented by books, research, and television documentaries, the 84-year-old mystery has intrigued Finns. The case is an essential part of the Nordic country's complex history and sheds light into its troubled ties with Moscow.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But perhaps more importantly, the downing of the plane happened at a critical time just days before Josef Stalin's Soviet Union was preparing to annex the three Baltic states, sealing the fate of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania for the next half-century before they eventually regained independence in 1991.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Moscow occupied Estonia on June 17, 1940, and Kaleva's doomed journey was the last flight out of Tallinn, though Soviets had already started enforcing a tight transport embargo around the Estonian capital.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: American diplomat Henry W. Antheil Jr., who is now considered one of the first U.S. casualties of World War II, was aboard the plane when it went down.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The 27-year-old Antheil, the younger brother of the acclaimed composer and pianist

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: George Antheil, was on a rushed government mission evacuating sensitive diplomatic pouches from US missions in Tallinn and Riga, Latvia, as it had become clear that Moscow was preparing to swallow the small Baltic nations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: An Associated Press wire item dated June 15, 1940 noted that "Henry W. Antheil Jr. of Trenton, N.J., attached to the United States Legation in Helsinki, was killed in the mysterious explosion of a Finnish airliner yesterday." In the US media, Antheil's death was overshadowed by much bigger news from

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
'It was unique that a passenger plane was shot down during peacetime on a normal scheduled flight.'  
CARL-FREDRIK GEUST, Finnish aviation historian

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Europe at the time: the Nazi occupation of Paris.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The US Embassy in Tallinn has thoroughly documented and researched the case over the years.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Embassy spokesman Mike Snyder told the AP that "news of the AP location of the wreck of the Kaleva passenger plane is of great interest to the United States, especially since one of the first US casualties of the Second World War, Diplomat Henry Antheil, occurred as a result of the plane being downed."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Earlier this month, the U.S. ambassador in Estonia, George P. Kent, shared a post on X that included photos of Antheil, Kaleva, and a memorial plaque by

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: the American Foreign Service Association in Washington with Antheil's name engraved in it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Kaleva was carrying 500 pounds of diplomatic post, including Anthell's pouches and material from French diplomatic couriers - identified as Paul Longuet and Frederic Marty.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Estonian fishermen and the lighthouse operator on Keri told Finnish media decades after the downing of the plane that a Soviet submarine surfaced close to Kaleva's crash site and retrieved floating debris, including document pouches, that had been collected by fishermen from the site.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This has led to conspiracy theories regarding the contents of the pouches and Moscow's decision to shoot down the plane. It still remains unclear why precisely the Soviet Union decided to down a civilian Finnish passenger plane during peacetime.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: New video taken by underwater robots from Peremee's company show clear images of the three-engine Junkers' landing gear, one of the motors, and parts of the wings.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Peremees and his group are "absolutely" convinced the parts belong to Kaleva because of the distinctive and recognizable design of the German-made Junkers Ju 52.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Peremees said his company would now focus on creating 3-D images of Kaleva's debris and discuss with Estonian authorities the possibility of raising some of the items and, if found, cargo and human remains.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Snyder from the U.S. Embassy said Washington is closely monitoring the diving group's efforts.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We are following the investigation of the site and will be happy to discuss with our Finnish and Estonian (NATO) allies any developments . . . from recovery efforts," Snyder said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Tribal members reclaiming ‘land of the flowing water’

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: 'To me, the [Three Creeks property] is sacred.'

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: TERI RED OWL (far left, with Kjeldall Noek), executive director of the Owens Valley Indian Water Commission

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: PHOTOS BY MIKE KAI CHEN/NEW YORK TIMES

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Land in California's Owens Valley has recently been returned to Indigenous stewardship.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
By Jill Cowan  
NEW YORK TIMES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The vast territory known as the Owens Valley was home for centuries to Native Americans who lived along its rivers and creeks fed by snowmelt that cascaded down the eastern slopes of the Sierra Nevada.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then came European settlers, and over time, tribe members lost access to nearly all of that land. Eventually, the water was lost, too: In the early 20th century, the developers of Los Angeles famously built a 226-mile-long aqueduct from Owens County to the city; this was their project, the story goes, that allowed Los Angeles to become the booming metropolis that it is today.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Less familiar is what happened to the Owens Valley, and the people who lived there, after most of the water was sent south. Owens Lake is now a patchwork of saline pools covered in pink crystals and wetlands studded with gravel mounds designed to catch dust. And today, the four recognized tribes in the area have less than 2,000 acres of reservation land, estimated Teri Red Owl, a local Native American leader.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But things are changing, tribal members say. They have recently reclaimed corners of the valley, buoyed by growing momentum across the country to return land to Indigenous stewardship, also known as the "Land Back" movement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In recent years, Native American tribes have reclaimed hundreds of acres of ancestral land, often after decades of advocacy. Members of the Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation have repurchased 130 acres in Illinois, which will become a federally recognized reservation for the tribe. And about 850 acres of land along the Mattaponi River in Virginia were returned to Indigenous stewardship and preservation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In California, state and local leaders have acknowledged a dark history of brutality toward Native Americans, and tribes have reclaimed territory up and

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: down the state.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Early this year, the state transferred ownership of the Mount Whitney Fish Hatchery - a European-style stone hall built in 1917 and manicured grounds - to the Fort Independence Indian Community of Paiute Indians, in the first return of its kind under a new state directive.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And last year, the owners of a healing retreat called Three Creeks sold their 5-acre property to a water advocacy group representing three local tribes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Along Highway 395, the desolate road running along the base of the Sierra Nevada, the landscape is rocky and covered in scrub brush. But the approach to Three Creeks is like a portal into a different world, opening onto a lush green expanse and a pond reflecting the clear, blue sky. On the property itself, apple, watermelon, and apricot trees bloomed on a recent afternoon while the sounds of trickling water and laughter floated through the air.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This is not what tribal members’ ancestors would have seen. But Red Owl, executive director of the Owens Valley Indian Water Commission—the group that purchased Three Creeks—said it is no less significant.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "To me, it is sacred," she said as she took a break in the cool air of what is known as the Heron Hut, a circular building on the property used for gatherings and ceremonies.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The former owners of Three Creeks had established the place about 25 years ago for visitors from around the world to stay, tend to the gardens, walk through the nearby mountains, and learn about the area's history as a tribe members. In the process, they built relationships with the Native American community.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gigi Coyle and her partners were told they could have sold the property for $1.5 million on the open market. Instead, they accepted the commission's proposal to buy it for $900,000 as a gesture to the people whose ancestors were there first. Dona

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: tions to fund the commission's purchase had come from people around the world who were moved by the community's call.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Coyle, 74, said she hoped the land return would inspire others to challenge beliefs that land is a sacred property to be passed down to heirs.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “Maybe think twice about that,” she said. “Recognize how important a relationship to place is and that these places have destinies, as well as these people.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The area’s Native American community members, who make up a relatively large share of the area’s overall population, have carried the legacy of brutal

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: displacements and broken promises by the federal government. (According to census data, 13.8 percent of the roughly 19,000 residents of Inyo County, which includes the valley, identified as a "residential area," compared with 1.7 percent in California overall.)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At the Owens Valley Paiute-Shoshone Cultural Center, maps show where the local tribes once lived near water sources. Their name for their home, Payahuunadü, translates to “land of the flowing water.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Other exhibitions trace how, in the 1850s, white miners and ranchers discovered that water,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: and agreements were made with a US government that continuously shrank their territory.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Today, the four recognized tribes in the area struggle to provide enough housing for members, many of whom have left as a result. On the Bishop Pauite Tribe's reservation, trailers are parked in the front yards of worn ranch houses and duplexes. Looming overhead are the craggy, towering peaks of the mountains - this spring, capped with blinding white.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Although many land returns involve sites that have historic or ceremonial significance, tribal leaders in the Owens Valley say

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: they also want to recover property that community members can use for housing and jobs that can sustain their lives.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We take care of our roads, we take care of our water, we take care of housing - the state doesn't do that for us," said Carl Dahlberg, chair of the Fort Independence tribe, whose reservation is about 40 miles south of the Bishop Painte Tribe.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Fort Independence tribe, which is not part of the group that purchased Three Creeks, took ownership of the Mount Whitney Fish Hatchery thanks to a recent rule change giving the tribe the right to first refusal when the state dispenses with excess property.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marilyn Bracken, 85, a longtime member of the Friends of Mount Whitney Fish Hatchery, and has helped preserve the site, recalled visiting there for field trips and birthday parties as a girl growing up on the Fort Independence reservation. She said it was meaningful that her community now controlled the site.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's encouraging, because this was once our land here," she said as she helped prepare a tribe member's wedding on the hatchery grounds. "Do we feel like we were the ones that should get it back? No, it should have been my grandparents and my great-grandparents. But it's happening now."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Environmental groups are working with Indigenous leaders in hopes of keeping more water in the Owens Valley, and in particular, Owens Lake. Los Angeles' demand for water, they say, has left the region's ecosystems barely hanging on. They hope that after two rainy winters, Los Angeles water officials will be able to think about how much water they really need and to rely more on conservation and recapture measures in Southern California.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We have a moment here. There is water in the lake. People are ecstatic," said Wendy Schneider, executive director of Friends of the Iyo, an environmental nonprofit.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Iowa takes lead in fighting potential stem cell scams

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: CHARLIE NEIBERGALL/ASSOCIATED PRESS

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: A court exhibit from a lawsuit filed by Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
By Heather Hollingsworth  
ASSOCIATED PRESS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The mailings promised "Life Without Pain!" via stem cell injections or IVs administered in a patient's own home. The allure as obvious: More than 20 percent of US adults endure chronic pain.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The flyers invited Iowans to free dinners across the state. Afterward, sales people traveled to potential customers' homes for high-pressure pitches disguised as pre-screenings, according to prosecutors. More than 250 people signed up, paying \(3,200 to \)20,000 each for a total of $1.5 million. For this, a nurse practitioner came to their homes to administer injections and IVs filled with stem cells derived from umbilical cords.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yet experts and regulators have alternately labeled such treatments as ripoffs, scams, or simply unproven. In some cases, studies have documented real harm.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Last fall, Iowa's attorney general sued two proprietors responsible for the mailings in her state, naming a Minnesota man who hosts a Christian entrepreneurship podcast and his Floridian partner for allegedly deceiving consumers, many of them elderly.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In bringing the lawsuit, Iowa joined attorneys general in New York, North Dakota, Georgia, Nebraska, Arkansas, and Washington state who have sued businesses alleging they fraudulently promoted unproven stem cell treatments.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Stem cells have long fascinated researchers because of their ability to reproduce and, in some cases, transform into other cell types. Because of this, they are thought to hold the potential for treating many diseases and injuries.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the FDA has approved only a handful of such therapies, and only for certain forms of blood cancer and immune system disorders. Stem cells are

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: considered experimental for most uses, despite being marketed as a treatment for everything from autism and emphysema to sports injuries.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The FDA has repeatedly warned Americans to be wary of businesses hawking unapproved, unproven, and costly stem cell therapies, which occasionally have caused blindness, bacterial infections, and tumors.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In a 2020 notice, the agency expressed concern about patients being misled about products that are "illegally marketed, have not been shown to be safe or effective, and, in some cases, may have significant safety issues."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dr. Jeffrey Goldberg, chair of ophthalmology at the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford University, whose work has documented vision loss in some patients treated with cells removed from patients' own bodies, processed, and reinjected, lamented that there are as desperately willing to take the huge sums of money for unproven and in some cases, explicitly sort of sham, so-called therapeutics."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Since August 2017, the FDA has issued about 30 warning letters regarding the unproven treatments.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Experts, including Dr. Paul Knoepfer, a stem cell researcher at the University of California at

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Davis, and Leigh Turner, a bioethicist at the University of California, Irvine, are among those who have raised alarm that such federal action is too little to regulate a US industry which Turner estimated in 2021 topped 2,700 clinics.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Because states can seek substantial fines against wayward operators, Turner said their legal actions offer promise.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “If you look at them collectively, they might over time start to have an impact,” he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The FDA offers training to attorneys general pursuing such cases. Dr. Peter Marks, director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, said federal regulators partner with state law enforcers in a "shared mission."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That puts people like Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird on the front lines.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Last year, Bird brought the case over mailers offering lowwans a pain-free life, naming the now dissolved Biologics Health and Summit Partners Group, which operated under the name Summit Health Centers, as defendants. The state also sued the companies' proprietors: Rylee Meek, of Prior Lake, Minn., and Scott Thomas, of Thonotosassa, Fla.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Iowa case is still in the discovery stage, with the trial set for March 2025.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.text: CHICAGO - Warning of a difficult fight ahead, former President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama on Tuesday called on the nation to embrace Kamala Harris in urgent messages to the Democratic National Convention that were at times both hopeful and foreboding.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: CHICAGO - At first glance, Donna Gholson looks like any one of the thousands of Democratic convention attendees decked out with all manner of Kamala Harris apparel.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Amtrak stumbles along with century-old system

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: BRYAN ANSELM/NEW YORK TIMES

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Virtually every episode that caused a significant delay happened between New York City and in Newark, N.J.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Outdated parts, technology make for long delays

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
By Patrick McGeehan
and James Glanz  
NEW YORK TIMES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It was just before rush hour on a Thursday afternoon, and all of the trains between Philadelphia and New Haven were at a standstill. The alert Amtrak sent out did little to calm seething commuters:All itsaid wassuspended because of an "overhead power outage."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: What it did not mention was that a giant circuit breaker - a critical piece of Amtrak's system for powering trains along the nation's busiest stretch of passenger railroad tracks - had blown up a few miles from Midtown Manhattan,causing catastrophic damage to an electrical substation and wreaking havoc across the Northeast Corridor.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The June 20 disruption was

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: just one in a series of delays this summer that exasperated commuters. But more than any of the other failures, the explosion that day showed that many of Amtrak's vulnerabilities along the corridor can be traced back to the system's astonishing age and long-outdated technology.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Long stretches of that system are unchanged from when the defunct Pennsylvania Railroad first electrified it a century ago, The New York Times has found. And any wholesale modernization effort could come at tremendous cost and take more than a decade.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's staggering; it's just staggering that we're still having antique technology controlling our rails," said John Goglia, a former member of the National Transportation Safety Board whose duties included overseeing railroad investigations. "That's last century's technology."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On that June afternoon, as the railroads were gearing up for the homeward rush, the substa

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: tion suddenly stopped transmitting data to monitors in operations centers in New York and other cities, the official said. Amtrak had lost power on about 10 miles of tracks.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That disruption halted service for several hours, leaving some travelers stranded as trains as trains were halted and canceled as far away as Boston.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The location of all the trouble was no mystery: Virtually every episode that caused a significant delay for New York area riders happened between two Penn Stations, the infamous one in New York City and the lesser-known one in Newark, N.J.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: About 9 miles long, that segment of tracks serves the most passengers of any in the country

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - by far. But it is a vestige of the early days of American train travel, when it was owned by the Pennsylvania Railroad which was known as the Pennsy.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When Amtrak was created in the 1970s, it inherited the Pennsy's original infrastructure,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: including the electrical system and the structures that suspend the wires above the tracks to provide power to locomotives.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And the heart of the operation Amtrak inherited relies on electrical standards that are a

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: centurv old.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Between Washington and New York City, rather than adopting the modern, nearly universal standard of 60 cycles per second, or 60 hertz, Amtrak has patched together an eletr

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: cal network that runs on the outdated standard of 25 cycles per second, or 25 hertz.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Amtrak maintains equipment that dates to when the Penny first electrified the line in the 1920s and '30s.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The antiquated system has forced Amtrak to cannibalize old substations for parts or have them custom-made, slowing down repairs. The replacement parts for the substation that blew up in June were not expected to arrive until late August.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Madison Feinberg, who has studied Amtrak's infrastructure as director of electric traction and technical planning for the Effective Transit Alliance, an advocacy group, said: "They've upgraded bits and pieces of the system - fundamentally making minor fixes to a design that's from the '30s. It's just effectively playing Whac-a-Mole, which Amtrak's team is very good at."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Amtrak officials said there were no immediate plans to update the electrical system.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Greenpeace tries a novel tactic in lawsuit over Dakota Access Pipeline

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Greenpeace recently unveiled a new strategy for fighting a costly lawsuit by an energy company that the group contends is designed to silence critics of the oil industry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The suit, first filed in federal court in 2017, alleges that Greenepeace had incited the protests against the Dakota Access Pipeline near the Standing Rock Sioux Reservation in North Da

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: kota in 2016 and 2017, and it seeks $300 million in damages.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Greenpeace disputes the claims. It says the lawsuit is designed to force the environmental group to go out of business with an expensive legal fight.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Its new tactic, led by Greenpeace International in Amsterdam, would use the European legal system to try to minimize the financial consequences of a

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: potential loss in US courts. In a letter to the company last month, lawyers for the group cited a new European Union directive aimed at curbing SLAPP suits, or Strategic Litigation Against Public Participation. Those are defined as meritless suits that seek to shut down civil society groups.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The letter called on the company suing it, Dallas-based En

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ergy Transfer, to drop its suit against Greenpeace International, and to pay damages for its legal costs, or risk a countersuit under the new European rules.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: S.D. bridge collapse cleanup begins

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: NORTH SIOUX CITY, S.D. Half of a collapsed rail bridge connecting South Dakota and Iowa was blasted in a controlled demolition, part of which was to remove the bridge months after it fell into the river, swollen from severe flooding.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The steel bridge over the Big Sioux River connected North Sioux City, S.D., with Sioux City, Iowa.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The bridge was partially underwater after heavy rains in late June brought record high river crests in the two states, along with Minnesota and Nebraska.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The blast on the South

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dakota side of the bridge, owned by BNSF Railway, occurred Monday morning, according to reports from broadcast station KTIV in Sioux City, Iowa.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "At 9 a.m. local time, charg-es were successfully used to cut the bridge span into sections, allowing it to fall into the river for removal," Kendall Sloan, BNSF communications director, said in a statement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sloan said crews will use a crane to remove the fallen pieces over the next week, and a second controlled blast will target the Iowa side of the bridge, likely in September.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Ill. bans corporal punishment in schools

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: SPRINGFIELD, Ill.-This school year, Illinois will become just the fifth state in the nation to prohibit corporal punishment in all schools.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Legislation that Governor JB Pritzker signed into law this month bans physical punishment in private schools while reiterating a prohibition on the practice in public schools implemented 30 years ago.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When the ban takes effect in January, Illinois will join New Jersey, Iowa, Maryland, and New York in prohibiting paddling, spanking, or hitting in every school.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: State Representative Margaret Croke, a Chicago Democrat,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: was inspired to take up the is-sue after an updated call by the American Association of Pediatrics to end the practice, which it says can increase behavioral or mental health problems and impair cognitive development.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It was an easy thing to do," Croke said. "I don't want a child, whether they are in private school or public school, to have a situation in which corporal punishment is being used."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The World Health Organiza-tion has decreed the practice "a violation of children's rights to respect for physical integrity and human dignity."

layout_dets.text: Former officer in Floyd killing moved to Texas prison

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: MINNEPOLIS - Derek Chauvin, former the former Minneapolis police officer convicted of killing George Floyd, was transferred to a federal prison in Texas almost nine months after he was released in a different facility, the federal Bureau of Prisons said Tuesday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Chaevin, 47, is now housed at the Federal Correctional Institution in Big Spring, a low-security prison. He was previously

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: held in Arizona at FCI Tucson in August 2022 to simultaneously serve a 21-year federal sentence for violating Floyd's civil rights and a 22 1/2-year state sentence for second-degree murder.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The transfer comes nearly nine months after Chauvin was stabbed 22 times in prison by a former gang leader and onetime FBI informant. Another former Minneapolis officer, Thomas Lane, who held down

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Floyd's legs as the man struggled to breathe, was released from federal prison in Colorado on Tuesday, the Bureau of Prisons said. Lane, 41, was serving a three-year sentence for aiding and abetting manslaughter.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When Lane pleaded guilty, he admitted that he intentionally helped restrain Floyd in a way that created an unreasonable risk.
