layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: New images capture their gravitational 'shimmy'

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Claire Thornton USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Scientists now have a better view than ever of a certain penguin’s tail feathers—only the bird in question is not what you may expect.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: NASA scientists running the James Webb Space Telescope have unveiled new photos of two galaxies dubbed the Penguin and the Egg for their shape and proximity to each other. Images of the galaxies already had been gathered by the Hubble Space Telescope, but the photos released Friday show stars, gas and space dust in greater clarity, NASA says.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The photos of the Penguin and the Egg also mark two years since the first groundbreaking photos from the Webb telescope were released.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “Astronomers often give cute names to the objects they study because it helps us remember and maintain a mental catalog of interacting galaxies,” said Eric Smith, program scientist for the James Webb Space Telescope at NASA headquarters in Washington. “The Penguin and the Egg are a great example.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Penguin galaxy, otherwise known as NGC 2936, is a spiral galaxy resembling the stout arctic bird, complete with a beak, a face with a bright eyeball, and a sloping, feathery-looking tail. The orbital radius of NGC 2936 is perched nearby (in astronomical terms) and is elliptical, or oval-shaped, galaxy, thus the name.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The two galaxies are locked together in a gravitational "dance," the space agency says, and despite their different sizes, they have about the same mass.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "They will go on to shimmy and sway, completing several additional loops before merging into a single galaxy hundreds of millions of years from now," NASA said in a statement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The stunning images show gas shining more brightly, shown as a blue hue, and the Webb telescope is able to see beyond dust that has partially disappeared. The Penguin's "eye" in past images, Smith said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Studying stuff in space is just beautiful and fun," Smith told USA TODAY. "It's certainly one of my top favorite images."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Two years after its first light, the James Webb Space Telescope has revealed the distorted spiral galaxy and the compact elliptical galaxy that make up the gravitationally bonded Penguin and Egg. 
PROVIDED BY THE SPACE SCIENCE SCIENCE INSTITUTE OFFICE OF PUBLIC OUTREACH, NASA, ESA, CSA, M. MARIN (STSCI)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sheriff, school district have 20 days to do so

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Hogan Gore  
Austin American-Statesman  
USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: AUSTIN, Texas - A Texas judge ruled that the school district and sheriff's office in Uvalade must release records within the next 20 days detailing the mishandled law enforcement response to the 2022 deadly mass shooting at  Robb Elementary School.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Laura Prather, the media litigation chair for Haynes Boone who is representing the media outlets, announced the ruling from the 38th Judicial District Court of Uvalde County on Monday. Prather said that the school district and sheriff's office must release "all responsive documents" to the news agencies - a pivotal step towards ensuring transparency and accountability.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A consortium of media outlets including the Austin American-Statesman, part of the USA TODAY Network, filed a lawsuit in 2022 after officials in Uvalde repeatedly refused to publicly release records related to the shooting. The news agencies are seeking records detailing Texas' deadliest school shooting, including police body camera footage, emails, 911 calls and additional communications tied to the mass casualty and its investigation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: An 18-year-old gunman killed 19 children and two teachers after entering Robb Elementary on May 24, 2022. Law enforcement response to the shooting has been sharply criticized after responding to a gunshot in minutes before confronting the shooter.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The public deserves to know the full details of the response to this tragic event, and the information could be critical in preventing future tragicacies," Prather said in a statement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Uvalde County Sheriff Ruben Nolasco declined to comment on Monday’s ruling. The Uvalde school district did not respond to the American-Statesman’s requests for comment.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Decision follows a similar 2023 ruling

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Last year, a judge made a similar ruling in favor of 14 news organizations, including the American-Statesman's parent company, Gannett, requiring the Texas Department of Public Safety to release its Uvalde school shooting

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: records, which the outlets were seeking.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In addition to Gannett, the other media outlets listed as plaintiffs in the lawsuit included the Texas Tribune, the New York Times Co., the Washington Post, NBC News, ABC News, CBS News and CNN.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Despite the ruling in the news organizations' favor in March, the Department of Public Safety has not released the records, citing objections from Uvalde County District Attorney Christina Mitchell. In a news brief Monday, attorneys representing the shooting victims' families seeking those records referenced an ongoing appeal by the Department of Public Safety to delay the release of "more than two terabytes of data related to the investigation."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Texas law enforcement criticized for delayed response to shooting

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Texas Department of Public

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Safety has faced intense scrutiny after video footage revealed that the agency's officers, and all other law enforcement agencies that responded to the massacre, waited more than an hour before confronting and killing the shooter.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The gunman had remained inside two classrooms where terrified kids who survived the shooting had called 911 pleading for help.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Earlier this year, the U.S. Department of Justice released a scathing report detailing law enforcement's "significant failure" in the shooting. The report described a chaotic, unorganized scene in which officers was no command and control by officers.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It also blamed the school’s police chief for attempting to negotiate with the gunman, who had already shot his way into the classroom, while having his officers search for keys to unlock rooms.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The report also noted officials provided misleading and inaccurate

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: information after the incident.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In May, days before the second anniversary of the massacre, the victims' families filed a lawsuit against the Department of Public Safety and 92 troopers who responded to the mass shooting, calling the response a derelicting conduct. The duty for not employing proper active shooter response training techniques.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The lawsuit states that while the officers had received active shooter training, those tactics and practices were not included in their response to the mass casualty.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In presenting the lawsuit, the Uvalde families also announced a $2 million settlement agreement had been reached with the city, which includes provisions on better training for police officers.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Contributing: Niki Griswoold, John C. Moritz, Tony Piohetski and Bayliss Wagner, Austin American-Statesman; Thao Nguyen, USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Outdated 911

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: state and local governments also tap general funds or other resources.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Now there are haves and have-nots," said Jonathan Gilad, vice president of government affairs at the National Emergency Number Association, which represents 91st first responders. "Next-generation 91h shouldn't be for people who happen to have an emergency in a good location."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Meanwhile, federal legislation that could steer billions of dollars into modernizing the patchwork 91I system remains waylaid in Congress.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "This is a national security imperative," said George Kelemen, executive director of the Industry Council for Emergency Response Technologies, a trade association that represents companies that provide hardware and software to the emergency response industry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "In a crisis - a school shooting or a house fire or, God forbid, a terrorist attack - people call 91 first," he said. "The system can't go down."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The U.S. debuted a single, universal 911 emergency number in February 1968 to simplify crisis response. But instead of a seamless national program, the 911 response network has evolved into a massive puzzle of many interlocking pieces. There are more than 6,000 911 emergency calls per year, and over 240 million emergency calls each year, according to federal data. More than three-quarters of call centers experienced outages in the prior 12 months, according to a survey in February by the

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: National Emergency Number Association, which sets standards and advocates for 91L and Carbyne, a provider of public safety technology solutions.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In April, widespread 911 outages affected millions in Nebraska, Nevada, South Dakota, and Texas. The shutdown was blamed on workers severing a fiber line while installing a light pole.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In February, tens of thousands of people in areas of California, Georgia, Illinois, Texas, and other states lost cell phone service,including some 911 services, from an outage.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In June, Verizon agreed to pay a \(1.05 million fine to settle a Federal Communications Commission probe into a December 2022 outage that affected 94 calls in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, New Jersey, South Carolina, and Tennessee.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The fires that raced across the Hawaiian island of Maui last August highlighted the critical importance of 911 systems. Dispatchers there fielded more than 4,500 contacts, meaning calls and texts, on Aug. 8, the day the fires broke out, compared with about 400 on a typical day, said Davlyn Racadio, emergency services dispatch coordinator in Maui County.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We're dying out here," one caller told 911 operators.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But some cell towers faltered due to widespread service outages, according to county officials. Maui County in May filed a lawsuit against four telecommunications companies, saying they had failed to inform dispatchers about the outages.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "If 91i calls came in with no voice, we would send text messages," Racadio said. "The state is looking at upgrading our system. Next-generation 91i would

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: take us even further into the future."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Florida, Illinois, Montana, and Oklahoma passed legislation in 2023 to advance or fund modernized 911 systems, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures.The upgrades include replacing analog 9ll infrastructure with digital, internet-based systems.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Instead of just fielding calls, next-generation systems can pinpoint a caller's location, accept texts, and enable residents in a crisis to send videos and images to dispatchers. While outages can still occur, modernized systems often include more redundancy to minimize the odds of a shutdown, Gilad said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Lawmakers have looked at modernizing 91 systems by tapping revenue the FCC gets from auctioning off the rights to transmit signals over speciffic band of the electromagnetic spectrum.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the U.S. Senate, in March 2023, for the first time allowed a lapse of the FCC's authority to auction spectrum bands.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Legislation that would allocate almost $15 billion in grants from auction proceeds to speed deployment of next-generation 9dI in every state unanimously passed the House Energy and Commerce Committee in May 2023. The bill, HR 3565,sponsored by Rep.Cathy McMorris Rodgers, R-Wash., would also extend the FCC's auction authority.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Other bills have been introduced by various lawmakers, including one in March from Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and legislation from Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash, to extend the auction authority. For now, neither effort has advanced. Nine former FCC chairs wrote lawmakers in February, urging them to make 91 upgrades a national priority. They suggested Congress tap unspent

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: federal COVID-19 money.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Whatever the funding source, the need is urgent and the time to act is now," they wrote.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Ajit Pai, who served as chair of the FCC from 2017 to 2021,said outages often occur in older, legacy systems.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The fact that the FCC doesn't have authority to auction spectrum is a real hindrance now," Pai told KFF Health News. "You may never need to call 91I, but it can make the difference between life and death. We need more of an organized effort at the federal level because 91I is so decentralized."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Meanwhile, some safety leaders are making backup plans for 91I outages or conducting investigations into their causes. In Massachusetts, a firewall signed to prevent hacking led to the recent two-hour outage,according to the state 9ll department.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Outages bring to everyone's attention that we rely on 911 and we don't think about how we really rely on it until something happens,”said April Heinze, chief of 911 operations at NENA.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Mass General Brigham, a health system in the Boston area, sent out emergency alerts when the outage happened letting clinics and smaller practices know how to find their 10-digit emergency numbers. In the wake of the outage, it plans to keep the backup numbers next to phones at those facilities.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Two hours can be a long time," said Paul Biddinger, chief preparedness and continuity officer at the health system.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: KFF Health News is a national newsroom that produces in-depth journalism about health issues and is one of the core operating programs at KFF – an independent source for health policy research, polling and journalism.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Climbed ladder to roof before rampage at rally

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
John Bacon and Christopher Cann  
USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A local police officer climbed a ladder to the roof of the building where he encountered a gunman moments before the deadly shooting at former President Donald Trump's campaign rally in Butler County,Pennsylvania, a local law enforcement official says.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Butler County Sheriff Michael Slupe told The Associated Press that the gunman, later identified as Thomas Matthew Crooks, saw the officer and turned toward him just before the officer climbed back down to safety. Slupe, who said the officer was unable to use his own gun under the circumstances, said Crooks quickly opened fire at Trump, who was speaking in the Butler Farm Show grounds about 150 yards away.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Secret Service snipers then shot and killed Crooks, the agency's director has said. The agency issued a statement Tuesday saying it was "deeply grateful" to local police officers for their efforts - and it denied blaming local authorities for failing to prevent the attack.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Three snipers from local tactical teams, deployed to assist the U.S. Secret Service, were stationed inside the building from which Crooks opened fire, a local law enforcement officer with little knowledge of the incident told CBS News.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Trump was wounded, one person in the crowd was killed and two others were critically wounded. Secret Service Director Kimberly Cheadle, in an interview Monday on ABC News, said local police had been in the building and were "responsible for the outer perimeter of the building." The statement drew criticism from Patrick Yoes, national president of the Fraternal Order of Police, who said all officers at the scene acted "heroically."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "This was not a failure of the local, state or federal officers on the ground who responded to the shots fired at former President Trump," Yoes said in a statement. "This is a failure at the management or command level who failed to secure an obvious weakness in the security of this event."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Secret Service, in a statement early Tuesday, appeared to walk back the blame. "We are deeply grateful to the officers who ran toward danger to locate the gunman and to all our local partners for their unwavering commitment," the agency's statement read. "Any news suggesting the Secret Service is blaming local law enforcement for Saturday's incident is simply not true."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cheatle also acknowledged that as Secret Service director, "the buck stops with me."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Secret Service director to testify before Congress

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cheatie is scheduled to testify Monday about the agency's "security lapses" at the rally before the House Committee

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: on Oversight and Accountability, Chair James Comer, R-Ky., said in a statement. "We are grateful to the brave Secret Service agents who acted quickly to protect President Trump after shots were fired and the American patriots who sought to help victims, but questions remain about how a rooftop within proximity to President Trump was left insecure."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In an interview with NBC's Lester Holt on Monday, President Joe Biden said he wants to see the results of an independent analysis he requested before he decides whether the Secret Service did enough to prevent the attempted on Trump's life.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He noted agents around Trump risked their lives to protect the former president.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “The question is: Should they have anticipated what happened? Should they have done what they needed to do to prevent this from happening?” Biden said. “That’s an open question.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas said Monday that Biden's security detail has been adjusted after the attack on Trump, whose Secret Service protection has now also been enhanced. Mayorkas also told reporters that the independent review of the shooting will begin in the coming days and its findings will be made public.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Authorities fear violence could breed violence

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: DHS and the FBI remain "concerned about the potential for follow-on or retaliatory acts of violence," Polito reported Monday. The media outlet cited an internal agency bulletin it said it has

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: viewed. The report added that "some online communities have threatened, encouraged, or referenced acts of violent violence in response to Saturday's shooting.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Meanwhile, Biden rejected accusations that he has engaged in violent rhetoric that could have incited the gunman. During his interview with Holt, Biden was asked about comments he made to campaign donors on July 8 when he said, "It's time to put Trump in the bullseye."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It was a mistake to use the word," Biden said. "I didn't say crosshairs. I meant focus on him, focus on what he's doing.Focus on his polices.Focus on the number of lies he told in the debate."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Slain fireman's widow rejects Biden's call but doesn't blame him

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The widow of Corey Comperatore, the fireman who was killed while protecting his family when the gunfire broke out, said that she rejected a phone call from Biden out of deference to her husband but that she holds no grudges against the president, the New York Post reported Monday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Helen Comperatore told the newspaper she has not heard from Trump but Biden's office reached out, presumably to offer condolences. She described herself as not involved in politics, adding that her husband was a "devout Republican" who would not have wanted her to talk to Biden.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I support Trump. That's who I'm voting for, but I don't have ill will towards Biden," said Helen Comperatore, according to the Post. "He didn't do anything bad to my husband. A 20-year-old

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: despicable kid did."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A memorial for Corey Comperatore will be held Thursday, his family announced.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Crooks reportedly bought ladder before shooting

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hours before the shooting, Crooks stopped at a Home Depot in his hometown of Bethel Park and purchased a ladder, CNN and NBC reported, citing unidentified law enforcement officials. Several rallygoers told officers before the shooting that Crooks was acting suspiciously and was climbing a ladder, according to a law enforcement official who spoke to AP on the condition of anonymity because the person was not authorized to discuss the investigation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In a statement shared with USA TODAY, a Home Depot spokesperson deferred to law enforcement but condemned the shooting.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The best source of information on this is law enforcement. We condemn the violence against former President Trump, and our thoughts are with him, not with them." The victims of Saturday's horrific events, and their families," the statement said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Authorities have yet to reveal a motive for the shooting. Despite scouring Crooks' phone and computer search activity, authorities have been unable to determine why Crooks, a dietary aide at a nursing home with no criminal record, acted as he did. Interviews with family and friends have turned up no obvious motive, law enforcement sources told CNN.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: No-shows

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Utah Sen. Mitt Romney, himself a Republican presidential nominee in 2012, has had a contentious history with former President Donald Trump and is not at this week's GOP convention in Milwaukee. JOE RONDONE/USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The traditional Republicans are not going to be given speaking slots," Douglas Holtz-Eakin, a former top economic adviser to John McCain during his 2008 presidential campaign, told the Washington Post. "There's no reason for them to be there for that, and as a result, there's less pure political attraction to be made."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Planning a write-in vote

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The list of Republicans who aren't coming to Milwaukee includes Sen. Susan Collins. The Maine Republican told reporters last week that she planned to write in former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley on her ballot in November. She said the schedule of events planned in her home state that will keep her far from Wisconsin.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "She will be in Maine with a schedule that includes attending a memorial service, dedicating a new fire station for which she secured funding, and honoring the retiring director of the Maine Poxtate Board," said Annie Clark, a spokesperson for Collins.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some Republican figures, such as Sens. Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Todd Young of Indiana, filled their calendars with other commitments during the convention that will keep them from becoming a candidate for the Senate office. Murkowski is in Alaska for official business, and Young is out of the country on official travel this week.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Changing roles of conventions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This week's RNC comes 48 hours after an assassination attempt against Trump and when safety is top of mind in a period of heightened political rhetoric.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I am so relieved to not have to go," former Rep. Mary Bono, R-Calif., told USA TODAY on Saturday. "I don't know many people who are looking forward to being there."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Political conventions also are changing in ways that don't make attendance necessary, said Holtz-Eakin, president of the American Action Forum, who also is not going to the convention. Advances in technology have simplified some convention procedures, especially after the 2020 national political

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: conventions during the coronavirus pandemic, Holtz-Eakin said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Presidential campaigns also have become "less policy-intensive," which has made national conventions less of a place for lawmakers to discuss their party's policies and future legislation, he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There are also the logistics of attending often massive and national conventions with thousands of like-minded people and swarms of media.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: New Hampshire Gov. Chris Sununu said in an interview with a local television station in late June that the event would be a "logistics nightmare that he wouldn't be attending.The two-term governor backed Haley in the 2024 Republican primary, but he emphasized

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: his absence doesn't signal a defiance of Trump. He said he would be supporting the former president from his home state.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I've had my criticisms with the former president. I stick by all those, actually," he told WMUR 9. "But at the end of the day, it's about choices, and I think it's pretty widely understood that no one really loves both candidates at the top, but people want change."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Passing on the baton

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prominent Republicans who had the spotlight at past GOP conventions are also nowhere to be found in Milwaukee. That list includes 2012 Republican presidential nominee Mitt Romney, now a U.S. senator for Utah, and his former vice president, John Kerry, who stepped down as House speaker during the Trump administration.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Also AWOL from Wisconsin: former President George W. Bush.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I don't think (Bush is) hankerling for the spotlight" Matt Schlapp, a conservative activist who was political director in the George W. Bush White House, told USA TODAY.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Schlapp, whose group organizes the annual Conservative Political Action Conference, added that he isn't surprised some of the old Republican order are opting out of the convention.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "There's always a bridge to the next generation of leadership, and that's true today."

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text:
An undated photo shows Winston, a western lowland gorilla and a popular fixture at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park. Officials said Winston, 52, was euthanized on Saturday after experiencing several age-related health conditions.
PROVIDED BY THE SAN DIEGO ZOO WILDLIFE ALLIANCE

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Winston, 52, was popular animal at San Diego site

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Michael Loria USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Winston, one of the oldest gorillas in the world and a popular fixture at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park, has died after experiencing multiple health problems, officials announced. He was 52.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The western lowland silverback was euthanized Saturday after experiencing several age-related conditions, including heart, kidney and joint diseases, Safari Park officials said on Instagram. Visitors to the Southern California park adored him for his quirky but gentle temperament, and scientists treasured him for his contributions to a critically endangered species, including fathering nine offspring, according to zoo officials.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Winston also raised two unrelated male gorillas, an unknown behavior for silverbacks.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "This gentle giant will be remembered for his quiet strength, easygoing nature and heart of gold," Safari Park officials said. Winston servered as the protector of his family."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Western lowland gorillas are a critically endangered species in several Central African countries, according to the World Wildlife Fund, a leading conservation nongovernmental organization. How many live in the wild is unclear, but scientists estimate their numbers have fallen by \(60\%\) in the past 25 years.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Winston arrived in Southern California in 1984, according to a San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance publication "Wonderful Winston: A truly great ape." He was one of 3,000 animals representing 300 species at the 1,800-acre expanse 30 miles outside San Diego and oversaw a troop of seven gorillas according to the 2018 publication. The park opened in 1972.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The beloved gorilla has had health complications since at least 2017 when zoekkeepers noticed symptoms of heart problems. Most great apes in zoos die from cardiovascular disease.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "After careful consideration stemming from furthering complications

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: from his worsening conditions, and with Winston's quality of life top of mind, wildlife health and care teams made the difficult decision to compassionately euthanize him," zoo spokesperson Emily Senninger said in a statement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: According to the Smithsonian National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute, western lowland gorillas are the smallest subspecies in size and are known for being peaceful. The males can grow up to 6 feet tall and 500 pounds; the females can grow up to \(4\%\) feet tall and 200 pounds, according to the Smithsonian. Gorillas' arms are longer than their legs, and the males have an arm span of 8 feet.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Western lowland gorillas - given the scientific name gorilla gorilla gorilla - live in swampy forests across the Congo Basin, including in Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon, according to the Wildlife Fund.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The number of wild western lowland gorillas worldwide has fallen sharply because of poaching and Ebola. The virus has killed off \(90\%\) of the gorillas and chimpanzees in what were some of the most densely populated ape habitats, according to the fund.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Western lowland gorillas in the wild typically live 30 to 40 years, according to the Smithsonian. They can live into their 50s in captivity.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The first thing zookees noticed about Winston when he arrived in the U.S. from England, where he was raised, was his mean-looking mug, according to a zookeeper publication. The second thing was how gentle he was.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He loved prunes, refused to eat honeyedew melon and had a catlike aversion to getting wet. He would walk around puddles or lie down a piece of cardboard to sit on when the ground was wet, according to zookeepers.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The announcement of his death was met by an outpouring of support from

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: fans on Instagram, who shared stories of seeing him.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Elizabeth Washburn, a San Diego-based artist, told USA TODAY about the time she met him.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Washburn was teaching at an art camp at the Safari Park in the early 2000s when a zookeeper invited her and the kids behind a special gate to watch Winston get a vet check.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "He was cool as all get out," said Washburn, 51, recalling how the full force of his personality was on display in the enclosure. "He came in and made this giant entrance. He ran in and started pounding his chest, and then he immediately came up to the window and looked straight out at us."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The kids, staring back at him across the fence about 10 feet away, were silent, "just gobsmacked," Washburn said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "He had so much intelligence," the artist said. "You could just see it in his eyes, he was just looking at us, trying to see who we were."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: John Dieirdch, Ashley Luthern Jessica Van Egeren, Sophie Carson, Bethany Bruner, Bailey Gallion, Shahid Meighan, David Clarey, Michael Loria and Michael Collins USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: MILWAUKEE - They called him Jehovah.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: An unhoused man whom one acquaintance described as a "beautiful person," he lived in one of Milwaukee's tent encampments and was well known by people in the neighborhood around King Park. They would often see him walking his dog and carrying a Bible.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The man, identified by a cousin as Samuel Sharpe Jr., was shot and killed Tuesday by five police officers from Columbus, Ohio, working as part of the city's security efforts surrounding the publically "National Convention. Both camera video released by authorities showed he was brandishing a knife.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The shooting happened less than a mile from the security perimeter of the convention, which is unfolding amid heightened security following a gunman's attempted assassination of former US president Clinton at a rally in Pennsylvania on Saturday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Authorities said the fatal shooting in Milwaukee is unrelated to the convention. But for some residents of the neighborhood, it raises questions about whether the police force out of-state police officers into the city to help provide policing for the event.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A Milwaukee police officer "would have known, no, no, no this is King Park, this is a known area for homeless to camp out, lots of folks with mental disabilities in here, tread carefully, deescalate," said Milwaukee Alderman Policeman, who represents the district where the shooting happened on Tuesday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Out-of-state officers are “in unfamiliar territory and they don’t know King Park from Central Park,” he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Columbus police are bringing the five officers involved in the shooting back home, but the other 35 officers the city sent are remaining in Milwaukee, Brian Steel, president of the Fatheral Order of Police Capital City Lodge No. 9, said at a news conference in Ohio.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Assistant Chief Ricky Heasley leaned over the hood of a truck on Monday, talking over funeral plans for fellow firefighter Corey Comperatore – the only person killed by a would-be assassin who opened fire Saturday at a Trump rally in the county.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I worked with him for a lot of years," said Heasley of the engineer who lived in a two-story home near the station and was an outgoing family man who officials said died protecting his wife and children from the sniper's bullets.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On Thursday, his friends and family will hold a visitation to pay their respects to Comperatore in Freeport, a small town on the Allegheny River, the family announced. It probably will draw large numbers. Funeral services will be held Friday at his longtime Butler County church.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There are few figures as unifying in America as a firefighter, who shows up when your house is ablaze and your loved ones are in danger. They are revered heroes, ingrained in the national consciousness since rushing into the World Trade Center on 9/11.

layout_dets.text: 'Black Death' killed 50 million people in Europe and still lingers in US today

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Plague infects a handful of people every year

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Eduardo Cuevas

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Plague is no longer the human scourge it was during "The Black Death," when it wiped out entire generations of medieval Europe and Asia.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nor does it pose the same threat it did when dense, unsanitary port cities

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: along the West Coast allowed the plague to fester in the early 1900s.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But still, plague infects a handful of Americans every year and when Colorado officials confirmed last week that a person in Pueblo County had been sickened, they sprang into action with warnings.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They cautioned against exposure to rodents, such as prairie dogs, known to carry fleas with the Yersinia pestis bacterium. that causas plague They also told people to be careful about pets

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: hunting or roaming near where rodents live. And encouraged them to get their pets treated for fleas and not to share a bed with pets.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Times have changed and antibiotics can now treat the plague, but it remains a serious disease,experts said .

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Living conditions were very different than they are now," Rebecca Eisen, a research biologist for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Steel said the victim was waving knives at other people and/or police when Columbus officers shot him. Steel said he didn't know if the officers had tried to use de-escalation measures or a stun gun before shooting the man.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Thirteen Columbus police officers were in the area for a briefing when they saw an altercation between two people, one of whom was holding a knife in each hand, according to preliminary information provided by Milwaukee Police Chief Jeffrey Norman late Tuesday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The officers ordered the man to drop the knives, he said. The man did not, and then suddenly charged at the other individual,which is  when police opened fire, Norman said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Body-camera video footage and still frames released late Tuesday by Columbus police show the man was still armed with the knives, and lunging toward another man,at the time of the shooting. Police shot him multiple times, killing him, the video shows.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Two knives were recovered at the scene, the chief said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Norman strongly defended the outside-state officers involved in the shootin.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Someone's life was in danger," he said. "These officers who are not from this area took upon themselves to act to save someone's life today."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Columbus Mayor Andrew J. Ginther said the body-worn camera footage "shows that Columbus' officers in accordance with their training to prevent physical harm to a potential victim."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Columbus officers were guests in Milwaukee, but they take an oath to protect and serve, wherever and whenever the nation is called to service," the mayor said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Someone's life was in danger. These officers who are not from this area took upon themselves to act to save someone's life today." Jeffrey Norman Milwaukee police chief

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Neighbors critical of out-of-state cops police patrolling area

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Police have yet to identify the victim, but a first cousin, Linda Sharpe, told reporters at the scene that he was Samuel Sharpe Jr,who was known by the nickname "Jehovah."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Eddie Johnson, 55, a friend of the victim, said he was a "beautiful person" who was known to walk his dog and carry a Bible.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I don't understand this," Johnson said. "He didn't deserve that."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sharpe stayed at a tent encampment on 14th and Vliet streets, a block away from a temporary shelter set up by the county for people displaced by the Rehabilitation Commission, said Stephen Bauer, CEO of the Guest House of Milwaukee shelter.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Shelly Sarasin of Street Angels, an outreach group that provides materials for unhoused people staying at the tent encampment,was at a loss for why the Columbus police were in the area.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Our Milwaukee police officers know about this camp and know about the people staging there and understand the issues that go along with experiencing homelessness," she said. "He didn't have to be there by an officer who wasn't from here."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Aurelia Ceja of the Milwaukee Alliance Against Racist and Political Repression criticized that out-of-state po

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: lice were involved. The group had planned a vigil for late Tuesday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Vaun Mayes, a prominent community activist, said he was concerned with the plan to bring non-Milwaukee police from "red states" who may not be familiar with Milwaukee communities. He did not think the shooting would've happened if it had been Milwaukee police. Mayes is familiar with the neighborhood from his work and dealing with its homeless population. He has successfully de-escalated fights in the area, he said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Thousands of additional cops in Milwaukee for convention

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Before the convention, Milwaukee officials estimated about 4,000 officers from law enforcement agencies outside of the city to take part in policing the city this week.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Milwaukee police had said they intended to assign outside officers to positions that are not public-facing - such as traffic control - while Milwaukee officers would have primary contact with members of the community. Any assignments given to outside officers were supposed to include at least one Milwaukee police officer, according to the mutual aid agreement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On Tuesday, Norman said Milwaukee police had provided briefings to visiting officers when they arrived. During the short news conference, he did not provide more details about the duties of the outside officers or any supervision the Milwaukee Police Department had over them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Outside officers in the city providing mutual aid for the convention are required to follow the Milwaukee Police Department's standard operating procedures on the use of force, crowd control and rules of engagement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: According to an agreement signed by partner agencies, any disciplinary

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: matters that arise with an outside officer will be referred to the home agency.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Milwaukee homeless shelter expanded services for convention

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Jehovah was familiar by a different name to Mike Bertram, ministry director for Capuchin Community Services, which runs the St. Ben's Community Meal, a nightly meal for the homeless and hungry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: St. Ben's has expanded its services this week to be open as a day and overnight shelter to give homeless individuals a safe, cool place to stay as the Republican National Convention may displace some people from their usual spot.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Before the convention, Bertram publicly offered St. Ben's staff to defuse any conflicts between homeless individuals and police near the security perimeter. In light of the shooting, he's hoping that more officers reach out.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We're here, we're willing to help in any way that we can," he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Near the park at 14th and Vliet, where aging trees shade the grassy slope of King Park as it rises away from the street,Street Angles has been running a free shower program.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sharpe showered there Monday, the day before the last day of his life.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "He told us he loved us like 10 times before he left," Sarasin recalled. "He had an appreciation for what he had... No one expected it would be like this."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After the shooting, Sarasin watched police take away Sharpe's dog.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: His only companion, she said, no longer has his friend.

layout_dets.text: John Diedrich, Ashley Luthern, Jessica Van Egeren, Sophie Carson, and David Clarey report for the Milwaukee Sentinel Journal; Bethany Bruner, B-aley Gallion and Shahid Meighan report for The Columbus Dispatch; Michael Loria and Michael Collins report for USA TODAY.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Plague

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Colorado, told USA TODAY. "We had high-density urban environments that were often rat-infected. That was a great way of bringing ground for transmission of plague."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: However, a century after the last urban plague outbreak in the U.S., the disease remains a perennial and serious risk in parts of the western U.S. for populations that live near infected rodents. Outbreaks, though contained or rare, become the subject of widespread media coverage when cases pop up.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Plague terrorized the globe, killed millions of people

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The first recorded cases of bubonic plague killed millions of people across the Mediterranean region. They began in the 6th century and endured until the 8th century.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In the 14th century, the Black Death broke out along the Silk Road, the trade route between modern China and Europe, killing about 50 million people in Europe, more than a quarter of the population, according to the Science Museum in London. Some estimates put it higher.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Outbreaks came again in the late 1500s and continued through the 1700s. Historians estimate 2.5 million people have died from the disease in France alone between 1600 and 1670.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Another pandemic began in the mid-1800s in Yunnan, in southwestern China. Several Asian port cities, such as Hong Kong and Bombay (now Mumbai), had outbreaks of bubonic plague in the late 19th century. More than 10 million people died of the disease in India in that era.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After 1900, rats and stowaways aboard ships from countries with outbreaks brought plague to American ports, including Honolulu and San Francisco. Public health officials in the western U.S. seapagoed people in the area, but not Mexican communities, wrongfully blaming them for being carriers of disease.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Honolulu officials began burning homes in the city's Chinatown, resulting in a fire that destroyed nearly all of the neighborhood.

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: A plague warning sign is posted on a prairie dog mound at Dick's Sporting Goods Park in Commerce City, Colo., in 2019. Several cases of plague were confirmed in prairie dogs that year and health officials treated the mounds with insecticide to kill any fleas that could transmit the disease. RON CHENOY/USA TODAY SPORTS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: San Francisco officials attempted to quarantine all of its Chinatown, forcing Chinese people to live in crowded unsanitary conditions in a densely packed area. Officials believed Chinese people carried the disease, but allowed white people to leave the quarantined area.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Los Angeles experienced the country's largest and last urban outbreak of plague in the mid-1920s, which was traced to a dead rat under a home in the city's "Little Mexico"neighborhood just 30 years ago. The response to 30 deaths, the city health department quantitated the area. Thousands of buildings were destroyed.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Plague never went away, still circulating out West

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Plague, which comes in several different forms, has not had the same reach in the past century, though it's considered endemic in parts of Africa and South America, according to the World Health Organization. In the U.S., the disease was first carried by fleas on rats in West Coast cities. It retreated into the interior western U.S., and fleas

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: carrying the bacteria found plentiful reservoirs in rodent populations such as squirrels and prairie dogs in rural and semirural areas.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Plague is now mostly found in semiarid upland forests and grasslands, according to the CDC.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "This wasn't an endemic disease that was already established," Dr. Amesh Adalja, a senior scholar at the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security. "This was something that basically came to the United States in the early 1900s, and is very geographically restricted."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: People don't have the same exposure to fleas as they did in the 1900s, he added.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Most U.S. cases occur in the Southwest and the West. About seven people get plague every year, according to CDC data. Between 1970 and 2022,there have been 500 plague cases in the U.S.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Three people have contracted the plague so far this year, according to the CDC. A New Mexico man died from bubonic plague in March. In February,an Oregon person contracted plage. Officials say the disease was likely transmitted by the person's infected cat.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Colorado case this month is the third.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Bubonic plague, thankfully, does not spread person-to-person

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Symptoms of plague develop within one to seven days after exposure, according to the WHO. It typically causes sudden fever and chills,severe headache, muscle aches, nausea and vomiting.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A common symptom is swollen, painful lymph nodes, called buboes. Buboes give bubonic plague, plague's most common form of disease, its name. It is also the body as swelling in the armpits, groin and neck, according to the Mayo Clinic.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Bubonic plague, along with septicemic plague do not pass from person to person. Direct contact with fleas is required, according to the CDC said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A third type, pneumonic plague, which caused the 1924 Los Angeles outbreak, occurs when bubonic or septicemic plague is left untreated and spreads to the lungs. It can also occur when Y. pestis infects the lungs. In that case, it can spread from person to person when someone inhales the bacteria breathed out by the infected person.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Antibiotics administered early can easily treat plague. Vaccines have been developed, however, they are not available in the U.S.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Take plague seriously, but don't worry too much

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Thanks to public health and sanitation, plague is no longer the threat it was in past centuries.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: However, Colorado health officials took precautions all the same, warning residents to destroy areas where rodents can hide and breed near their homes. Officials also told people to be careful about pets hunting or roaming near where rodents live. Pets must get regular treatment for fleas, officials said. They warned people not to let pets sleep with them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Humans are really accidental hosts," said Dr. Michelle Barron, senior medical director for the UCHealth Infection Prevention and Control and a professor of medicine and adviser to the Colorado School of Public Heath."It's when you come into contact with the animals, or the fleas that are associated with the animals, that they then end up infected.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Trump rally security to be probed

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Former President Donald Trump walks down from the family box during the second day of the Republican National Convention at the Fiserv Forum, MIKE DE SISTI/USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: House, Homeland will investigate

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: John Bacon USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Department of Homeland Security's inspector general's office said Wednesday that it will investigate the Secret Service effort to provide security at Donald Trump's campaign rally in Pennsylvania where the former president was shot and a rallygoer killed.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A notice posted on the office's "ongoing projects" website said the goal is to evaluate the United States Secret Service's (Secret Service) process for securing former President Trump's July 13, 2024 campaign event. The Secret Service falls under Homeland Security.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Secret Service has drawn criticism for failing to keep the shooter, Thomas Matthew Crooks, from gaining access to the roof with an AR-15 semiautomatic rifle, 150 yards from where Trump spoke at the rally. Local police officers had been stationed inside the building but none on the roof.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Also Wednesday, House Speaker Mike Johnson announced a bipartisan task force within the House to investigate the assassination attempt, saying "we need answers for these shocking security failures."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: President Joe Biden previously ordered an "independent review" of the security measures at the event. Secret Service Director Kimberly Cheatele called the shooting "unacceptable" but said she will not resign.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Trump was speaking before throngs of supporters at the Butler Farm Show grounds when the gunman opened fire. Trump, his face bloodied from a bullet that apparently injured his ear, was hustled off the stage by Secret Service personnel. A Trump supporter was killed and two others were critically wounded before a sniper fatally shot the gunman.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Crooks' father, Matthew Crooks,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: called police after the shooting, worried that his son and a gun were missing, three senior law enforcement officials told NBC News. Fox News is reporting that the family called authorities before the shooting took place.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Victim has 'life-altering injuries'

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The family of James Copenhower, one of the two critically injured victims, issued a statement Tuesday thanking first responders and those who have provided him with medical treatment since the shooting.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The statement said Copenhaver, a 74-year-old Pennsylvania resident, sustained "life-altering injuries" in the attack and is in critical but stable condition at Allegheny General Hospital in Pittsburgh. The family also asked for privacy as Copenhaver recovers.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Friends and family of Corey Comperatore, the person killed at Saturday's rally, will gather Thursday in Freeport, a

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: small town on the Allegheny River, to pay their respects.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Funeral services will be Friday at his longtime Butler County church. Comperatore was proclaimed a hero after Gov. Josh Shapiro said the former volunteer firefighter dived onto his family to protect them as the shooting started.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: James Sweetland, a doctor from Dubois, Pennsylvania, who was at the rally, rushed to help Comperatore. But he had suffered a shot to the head above his ear and never regained consciousness.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Iran denies plotting to kill Trump

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Iran rejected "malicious" reports of an alleged plot to assassinate Trump, saying the Islamic nation seeks a "legal path to bring him to justice" for ordering the assassination of an Iranian general in 2020.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The White House confirmed to USA TODAY a report that Trump's security was increased in recent weeks after intelligence showed Iran had been plot

layout_dets.text: Comperatore

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: "For guys like us, we're trained to do this stuff," said former volunteer firefighter Gary Risch Jr., a close friend of Corey Comperatore's. "We're trained to understand it. ... But when it's a brother like this, that's this close, it's pretty much impossible to train to deal with this." BRENDAK MCDERMID/REUTERS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: assassination attempt at the Trump rally he attended, another trauma that has further inflamed one of America's most divisive political moments.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: President Joe Biden called his widow to offer condolences. "He was a father," Biden said later. "He was protecting his family from the bullets that were being fired, and he lost his life. God love him."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Comperatore's wife, Helen, declined to talk to Biden.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I didn't want to talk to him," she told the New York Post. "My husband was a devout Republican and he would not have wanted me to talk to him."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: She added that she didn't have any ill will toward Biden because "he didn't do anything bad to my husband. A 20-year-old despicable kid did."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Decades of service

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Comperatore grew up and went to high school in the same county where he served as a volunteer firefighter. A visitation for family and friends is set for Thursday; his funeral will be held Friday at his longtime church in Butler County, PROVIDED BY BUFFALO TOWNSHIP VOLUNTIRE FIRE COMPANY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Comperatore had recently turned 50 in the same part of the county where he had grown up, a place of forested hills, cornfields, churches and residential communities that have grown in recent decades.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He was also very interested in politics and a Trump supporter.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That's not uncommon in his county, where \(66\%\) voted for Trump in 2020. By contrast, in nearby Allegheny County, anchored by the city of Pittsburgh, that figure was \(41\%\).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: His obituary reflects a man steeped in traditional values. He served a decade in the U.S. Army Reserves after his graduation from Freeport High School in Sarver in 1992. He worked at the same place for decades, according to his LinkedIn page, becoming a project and tooling engineer at JSP International, which makes polymers for industries from autos to construction. He was a member of Cabot Church and served in the Buffalo Township Volunteer Fire Company, including as chief in the early 2000s.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 'God first, his family second'

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Brenda and Jim Disantis called years ago when Helen, who babysat for them as a teenager, introduced them to her boyfriend, the pair wrote on his obituary. "I would see the love between them was forever even at their young age," they said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The couple, who recently celebrated their 22nd anniversary, according to a church bulletin, raised two daughters, Allysson and Kaylee Comperatore. They

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: lived so near the station he could walk his dogs past it. His heart seemed to many to be wrapped up in his family. "Corey was a girl dad," Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro told reporters. "Corey went to church every Sunday. Corey loved his community and, most especially, Corey loved his family."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Johnston said Comperatore put "God first, his family second and everybody third."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Upset by Trump's loss in 2020,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Comparator got more involved in politics in recent years, said Buffalo Fire coalitions were not able to make a

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The coming election meant a lot to him, he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: So when the former president's campaign announced a rally scheduled for Saturday, it was natural that he would make the22-mile drive to the county seat of Butler.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Gunshots, then 'Get down!'

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The gunfire started just as Trump was talking about immigration. Comperatore heard it and yelled, "Get down!"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He piled on top of his family to shield them, according to Shapiro, who said at a news conference that he spoke to Comperatore's wife after the shooting and recounted what she told him.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The shooter, later identified as Thomas Matthew Crooks,20, a health aide from Bethel Park, Pennsylvania, was shot and killed by Secret Service countersnipers, but not before he opened fire from atop a roof outside the venue, piercing Trump’s ear

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Two other rallygoers were critically wounded: David Dutch,57, of New Kensington, Pennsylvania; and James Copenhaver,74, of Moon Township, Pennsylvania. Both remained in the hospital.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: James Sweetland, a doctor from Dubois, Pennsylvania, who was at the rally, rushed to help Comperatore. But the former fire chief had been shot in the head above his ear and didn't regain consciousness.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "He was protecting his daughters, his family," said Sweetland, whose own wife had once been widowed with

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: children. She wasn't at the rally, but she cried when she learned he had died, knowing how painful it could be, he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That Comptatore shielded his family didn't surprise Johnston.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "He always made sure everybody came out safe," he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But that did little to lessen the pain.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Yesterday, time stopped," Allyson Comperatore, his daughter, said on Facebook. "And when it started again my family and I started living a real-life nightmare."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Outpouring of support

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gary Risch Jr., a former volunteer firefighter, hadn't stepped foot in the Buffalo Township Volunteer Fire Company for a year and a half.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But it was the first place he went Sunday morning after the shooting that killed his close friend. Already, black bunting was strewn from the station's sign and across Comperatore's locker.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Firefighters regularly risk their lives. But this was different.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "For guys like us, we're trained to do this stuff. We're trained to understand it," Risch said. "We're trained not to accept it but to deal with it. But when it's a brother like this, that's this close, it's pretty much impossible to train to deal with this."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A day later, Heasley said many are sending checks to the fire station for the family. He said a fundraiser will be set up for the Comperatore family.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Already, a larger fundraiser including Comperatore and others wounded in the shooting had raised nearly $5 million from more than60,000 donations by Tuesday. Elon Musk gave $50,000.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As the nation buzzes with political rhetoric and conspiracy theories amid the search for the shooter's motive, his death is likely to symbolize different things to different people in this complicated political moment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But friends and family in the community of Sarver, ahead of this week's funeral, are focused on the man they lost.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Friends left with memories

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That's especially true for those who are part of the Buffalo fire department, a place of chicken-dinner fundraisers and close friendship. And now, one lost colleague they won't ever forget.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "There's a lot of history with him and a lot of great memories and stuff we'll never forget," Risch said. "I mean, they don't get much better than him."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The nation, too, will never forget.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Contributing: Matthew Rink, Erie Times-News

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Freedom Summer helped change US

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Lessons from era are still resonating

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Deborah Barfield Berry  
USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: WASHINGTON - Charles McLaurin initially disagreed with the plan to bring college students - many of them white, many from the North - to Mississippi 60 years ago to help register Black residents to vote. He thought it would do more harm than good.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Black Mississippians already had to overcome their fear of white superma-cists and violence to register to vote. He doubted it would work to mix educated white students and professionals with local Black residents, many of them sharecroppers who couldn't read.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "But just the opposite happened," recalled the 84-year-old civil rights veteran.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They worked together to set up Freedom Schools in Black communities and take Black residents to courthouses to register to vote. They ate dinner together, talked on porches.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "They melded into the community. It was very successful..." said McLaurin, a veteran of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee. "It created a sense of power."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: During that summer in 1964, Black and white college students and others led by the Council of Federated Organizations, an umbrella group that included SNCC, joined locals in Mississippi to help register Black citizens to vote. Freedom Summer, as it was dubbed, was a continuing fight in the civil rights Movement and helped lead to passage of major legislation, including the 1965 Voting Rights Act.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That summer of activism "helped change the political landscape across the country," said Zikaya Summers, a state representative in Mississippi.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Across the country, veterans of the Civil Rights Movement, community activists, scholars and students are marking the 60th anniversary with a host of events.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On July 17, Rep. John Lewis, a SNCC veteran who worked to register Black voters across the South, will also be remembered with dozens of events marking the fourth anniversary of his death.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The National Civil Rights Museum will hold a symposium on Freedom Summer July 27 in Memphis. In June, veterans hosted a two-day conference in Indianapolis, Mississippi.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Earlier this year, California launched a statewide voter registration campaign commemorating the anniversary. And in May, the African American Policy Forum held a rally at the U.S. Supreme Court kicking off its "Freedom Summer 24" campaign to urge more people to vote.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "People need to remember that a lot of young people from all over the country gave up their summer to come and try to make a difference in a part of the country that needed help, that on its own those people could not make it," said Mississippi Rep. Bennie Thompson, a Democrat whose district was at the heart of the effort. "It was a violent time. It was a time that very idealistic young people (came). Some lost their lives. Others were abused."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Saluting the power of local activists

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: More than 200 people, including civil rights veterans, gathered in Indianaola in June to commemorate the milestone anniversary.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Beyond a reunion, organizers wanted to train younger activists and strategize to protect rights they fought for decades ago. They pointed to recent efforts to ban books, block access to voting and restrict the teaching of Black history.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "There seem to be those in some higher places who are trying to erode some of the changes that we made," said McLaurin, a native Mississippian who helped organize the conference. "So what we want to do is alert our people especially that we need to register and sign off to vote... We need to build economic power as well as political power so that we can protect the gains we've made."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At the conference, veterans shared stories of their experiences during that summer and told how it changed their lives.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At the heart of that effort were local residents, said Charlie Cobb, BI, also an SNCC veteran who worked in Mississippi.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The power of local people at the grassroots, that's the most overlooked aspect of the Southern movement, certainly in Mississippi," said Cobb, author of "This Nonviolent Stuff'll Get You

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Attendees clap while listening to a panel discussion during the Freedom Summer 60 conference at Club Ebony in Indianapolis, Miss., on June 21. The event celebrates the 60th anniversary of the Freedom Summer in 1964. Freedom Summer was a critical turning point in the Civil Rights Movement.

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text:
Dr. C. Sade Turnipseed speaks during the Freedom Summer 60 conference at Club Ebony in Indianaola, Miss., on June 21. "We can make a major difference to the whole landscape of the entire country right here," Turnipseed said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "People need to remember that a lot of young people from all over the country gave up their summer to come and try to make a difference in a part of the country that needed help." Rep. Bennie Thompson Mississippi Democrat

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Killed: How Guns Made the Civil Rights Movement Possible."The whole movement was powered by grassroots community organizing.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: What was Freedom Summer?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Local activists had been working for years in hostile territory to register Black residents.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: For Freedom Summer, they turned to outsiders, namely white college students from the North, to draw national attention to their efforts. Many of the students stayed in the homes of Black students or slept in pews at Black churches.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The project also drew national media attention after the murders of civil rights workers James Chaney, Andrew Goodman and Michael Schwerner that June. Goodman and Schwerner were white. The prior murders of Black activists had not garnered much national attention.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Activists, spurred in part by Cobb, also created Freedom Schools to help educate young and old Black residents. The 40 free schools were staffed by volunteers and included voter education classes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That same year, the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party was also formed to counter the all-white state Democratic Party. The MFDP held a convention, drawing thousands.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Freedom Summer refuted in absolute terms this whole idea, which we ran into frequently with the press, this whole idea that Black people were apathetic, that they didn't want civil rights, that they didn't want the right to vote," C said. "You could no longer say that in the aftermath of the Freedom Summer."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Later that summer, delegates from the MFDP went to the national Democratic Party convention in Atlantic City, New Jersey, where civil rights activist Fannie Lou Hamer gave her impassioned speech about the struggle for democracy. She was for Black Mississippians. Today, there's a statue of Hamer at Atlantic City.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's this groundswell of advocacy and support that comes from within that actually makes these movements a success," said Daphne Chamberlain, a Mississippi civil rights historian. "And it also comes from the bravery of the people at the local level to be able to make these moments of success... Black folks have been so good what the racial climate was like here. The Black folks were also organizing and organizing, particularly around politics and how we insert our voices."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 'Still work to be done'

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Lessons learned from Freedom Summer are still important, said Cobb.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's more relevant because a lot of these lessons from 64 and earlier in the South particularly are forgotten," he said. "They need to be understood in these more complex times when the Black community has really become aware of the issues and more of an urban community and therefore a more complex community."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Mississippi, where the population is nearly40% Black, is now among the states with the highest number of Black elected officials – mostly at the local level. In2022, about72% of Black Mississippians were registered to vote, according to census data.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Following that summer, many activists started organizations back home or joined other civil rights efforts.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "They helped America create the kind of atmosphere at that time that would allow an African American to become a real part of the United States of America," McLaurin said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Activists said the effort 60 years ago to increase Black political power with Freedom Summer isn't finished yet.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The anniversary is "not just about looking back with admiration, but looking forward with the determination to bridge political power and knowledge for liberation," said Kimberly Crenshaw, co-founder and executive director of the African American Policy Forum, a New York-based social justice think-tank, that is hosting a weeklong summer school on civic engagement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's also a time to rededicate ourselves to the same ideals and principles that people came with 60 years ago," said Thompson, who spoke recently at two commemoration events in Mississippi.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Remembering that summer at those events was somber, he said, "but it was also exhilarating in the fact that people were realized that there's still work to be done."
