layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Causes of bird flu outbreak targeted

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Bird flu's risk to the general public remains low, said Dr. Nirav Shah, of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. GINS WANG/GETTY IMAGES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Heat, industrial fans may have put workers at risk

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Eduardo Cuevas  
USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Triple-digit temperatures, industrial fans and carts used to kill millions of sick chickens with gas may have caused the largest bird flu outbreak among U.S. workers to date, federal health officials said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A commercial egg-laying facility in northeast Colorado now has four workers confirmed infected with bird flu and another presumed to have contracted the virus, pending test results. The sickened Colorado workers, announced over the weekend, doubled the number of human cases in the U.S. since agricultural workers began contracting bird flu this year, first from dairy cows.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Workers at the poultry farm in Weld County had been in the process of killing 1.8 million chickens, some of which were infected with the dangerous H5N1 influenza, to prevent it from spreading, federal officials said in a briefing with reporters Tuesday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Their goggles or N95 face masks apparently slipped as industrial fans blew feathers and other infected items through the sweltering barn, exposing them to the virus, said Dr. Nirav Shah, principal deputy director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The workers all suffered some combination of fever, chills, coughing and eye infections, Shah said. They were given the antiviral Tamiflu, and none required hospitalization.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The virus's risk to the general public remains low, Shah said. The workers' illnesses were relatively mild, he said, and Tamiful remains effective. Also, the genetic sequence of the virus has not changed substantially since December as the virus moved from Texas to a dozen other states, including Colorado and from birds to cows and then, apparently, back to chickens, as well as people.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We've not seen severe illness, which is reassuring," Shah said. "The other thing we look at, in addition to severity is whether the virus is able to transmit

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: from animals to humans and/or from humans to humans with greater ease or with greater efficiency. We haven't seen changes, particularly on the human-to-human side."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: The unfolding route of transmission

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Officials said they don't know for sure how the H5N1 virus arrived at the Weld County poultry farm. In early July, Colorado Gov. Jared Polis issued a disaster emergency after the outbreak at the facility, the largest flock of chickens affected in the state and among the largest across the U.S.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Days earlier, a dairy worker, also in northeastern Colorado, contracted bird flu, the state's first case, while working with infected cows.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cattle in the same region of Colorado had been known to be infected with the specific variant of the virus, so it's likely, though not yet confirmed, that the virus was passed from cattle to chickens, said Dr. Eric Deebie, acting senior adviser for the U.S. Department of Agriculture's H5NI Response.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Poultry are very susceptible and easily infected," Deeble said on the call with reporters. "It does not take much in

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: order to introduce this into a flock."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Once any poultry on a farm are infected with H5N1, the only way to contain the virus is to kill the entire flock, the USDA has said. Killing all 1.8 million chickens could take up to two weeks, Deeble said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Sweltering barns, feathers flying

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: About 160 workers inside barns at the facility were tasked with pulling out chickens, placing several at a time in a cart that would then be filled with carbon dioxide, killing them in less than a minute and a half, Dr. Julie Gauthier, the USDA's executive director for field operations in the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, said on the call.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Temperatures in northeast Colorado have hit 104 degrees, though Shah said temperatures inside the barns were even hotter. Workers wore light paper protective suits over their clothes, N95 respirators, goggles, boots and gloves. Industrial fans pushed air through the barns.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The fans made it uncomfortable to wear PPE, all while feathers - a means in which bird flu virus can spread - blew around. That probably caused the infec

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: tions in five workers, officials said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That suggests risks can be better controlled in the future with more systematic use of PPE, in addition to measures to improve ventilation, Shah said. A 10-person CDC team, which includes bilingual speakers and an industrial hygienist, will play in Colorado to monitor and test workers and suggest safety improvements.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In total,60 workers were tested for bird flu, and55 tested negative, though many had symptoms consistent with other respiratory illnesses like rhinovirus, Shah said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sixteen workers who are symptomatic had been tested Monday, AnneMarie Harper, a spokesperson for the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, said in an email. Testing is still being done, and Shah said more infections might come to light.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: What preparedness looks like

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Part of the virus found on its surface remained unchanged from the first person infected in Texas to the first infected in Michigan and the workers sickened recently in Colorado, Shah said, suggesting the virus has not mutated to become more worrisome.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Department of Health and Human Services' Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response is pushing ahead with production of millions of bird flu vaccine doses through July as part of a pre-pandemic stockpile, said David Boucher, director of the agency's infectious disease preparedness and response.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There is no recommendation yet for people to receive the vaccine, which has not been fully tested or approved for use.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The agency also distributed 5,000 goggles, 300,000 gloves, 150,000 N95 masks and 528 courses of Tamiflu to Colorado, Boucher said.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.text: At least 3 dead after severe storms

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 'War zone' in NY, floods in Midwest

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Cybele Mayes-Osterman  
USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Severe weather and several unconfirmed tornadoes across the Midwest and the East Coast wreaked devastation on Tuesday, leaving at least one person dead in upstate New York and an elderly couple dead in Illinois.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: More storms were in the forecast after the National Weather Service issued a severe thunderstorm watch for a wide swath of the East Coast from Philadelphia to Boston and up to Albany, New York.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On Tuesday, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency throughout the state after the storms caused widespread destruction, wrecking buildings and trees and leaving more than100,000 households without power, according to poweroutage.us.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One person died in Canastota, a village about 25 miles east of Syracuse, according to an emergency declaration. The man's wife and his wives were ripped down in the village, and several roads were impassable. Some areas were being evacuated.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Farther east, the storms ripped through Rome, a city of31,000, demolishing houses and uprooting trees.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rome Mayor Jeffrey Lanigan said the storm battered the town's historic downtown, pulling down the steeples of two19th-century churches and permanently changing the city skyline.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The National Weather Service in Binghamton said it would conduct a storm survey in the town to investigate reports of a tornado. The weather service issued a tornado warning for the area on Tuesday afternoon.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Justices halt Gutierrez execution in Texas

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Amaris Encinas USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The U.S. Supreme Court granted a stay of execution less than an hour before a Texas inmate was set to die by lethal injection, a "devastating" development for the family of the victim in the case and a "hopeful" one for the man who got the reprieve.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Ruben Gutierrez, 47, was scheduled to be executed Tuesday just after 6 p.m. CT before the high court issued the stay pending a lower court ruling regarding the inmate's arguments over DNA testing.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Though it wasn't immediately clear how long the delay would be, or even whether it would ever go forward, Texas Department of Criminal Justice spokesperson Hannah Haney told USA TODAY shortly after the ruling: "There will not be an execution tonight."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Shawn Nolan, Gutierrez's attorney, said the stay would get him and his client one step closer to proving something they have known all along.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Mr. Gutierrez has been requesting DNA testing for more than a decade to prove he did not kill the victim in this case," said Juan said in a statement to USA TODAY.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nolan says he and Gutierrez are "hopeful" that now the court has stepped in to stop the execution, they will be able to "ultimately accomplish their task," adding to prove that Mr. Gutierrez should not be executed now or in the future.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Gutierrez's conviction and DNA testing argument

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gutierrez was sentenced to death in the 1998 murder of a 85-year-old Escolastica Harrison, a retired schoolteacher described by her nephew in an interview with USA TODAY as a pillar of the community and someone "everybody loved."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gutierrez acknowledged planning to rob Harrison but has always maintained he was outside her house when the two men he was with went inside.

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text:
Robert Harrison and Escolastica Harrison attend sister Estella Cuellar Perez's 1986 wedding.  
PROVIDED BY ALEX HERNANDEZ

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He says that he never thought things would turn violent and that DNA testing could exonerate him, something he has been repeatedly denied during the appeals process.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Saenz disputed Gutierrez's claims, telling USA TODAY last week that his efforts were merely a "delay tactic." His office wrote in court records this month that "Gutierrez purposefully forewent DNA testing at his trial in 1999."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "And he has leveraged that strategic decision for the last 20 years to delay enforcement of his sentence," they said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Saenz was "very disappointed, very sad and very upset" for the family after Tuesday's delay and told USA TODAY that they are "revictimized" every time Outrezzer has been able to delay the government that was imposed on him legally.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gutierrez has been issued seven death warrants since 2018 and spent more than 575 days on death watch, his attorneys have said. Each time, his execution has been called off, largely over clerical issues.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Here we go again," Saenz said Tuesday. "We did this four years ago and I found that to be very disheartening to the family. And here we are four years later. Deja vu. It's sickening to the family. They get revictimized over and over again. When is it going to stop?"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Saenz says he "will continue to fight" until Gutierrez is held accountable.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "All that does is reinvigorate me," he said. "All that does is motivate me to double down and to do what I have to do to so that someday, in the near future, the Harrison family will see justice for Escolastica, which is what they've been waiting for and wanting now for 25 years."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Gutierrez's execution stay is 'devastating,' nephew says

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Harrison's nephew Alex Hernandez was waiting for the execution to begin when he received a phone call from Saenz about 20 minutes before the lethal injection. Saenz informed him of the last-minute stay.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It was just devastating," Hernandez told USA TDOAY. "It's like: Come on, you know. This is the third time we've jumped through all their hoops and done everything that they've asked. And now you're telling us that it's not going to happen. I mean it's just numbing, devastating, unbelievable.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I feel just defeated. I know it's not over yet, but at this moment I feel defeated."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hernandez thought he was going to be able to lay the case to rest, but instead has continue to live with the memory of what happened to Harrison, who was his beloved "Aunt Peco."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "If it had gone through, I would've gone home, prayed over it, thought about it for a while put it to rest, think about my Aunt Peco and be happy now that all this is done and move on with my life," he said. "But now I have to think about her killer again every day."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hernandez questions why his family has yet to receive justice and wonders whether they ever will.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "When's it going to happen? Why hasn't it happened yet? Is going to happen ever?" he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "He was convicted. How are you telling me 'Look at the case again'? For what? It doesn't make sense."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hernandez believes Gutierrez's pleas for DNA testing are bogus and says he

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: believes Gutierrez is just trying to "buy time."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "He's scared to die. He left crying. He left the room crying in tears, saying 'Thank God,'" he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: How do you think my aunt felt being stabbed 13-14 times with screwdrivers by people she was acquainted with? How do you think she felt?

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Escolastica Harrison was enjoying retirement when attacked

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Harrison was enjoying retirement after decades of juggling her job as a schoolteacher and managing a trailer park that served as a "stepping stone" for struggling residents, Hernandez told USA TODAY.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At the time of her death, another of Harrison's nephews, Avel Cuellar, had been living with her to help her around the trailer park after her husband died. Gutierrez, a friend of Cuellar's, hung out at his trailer in trailer park often, drinking and socializing.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gutierrez, a 21-year-old married father of two at the time, befriended Harrison and would run errands for her, eventually learning that she kept a lot of cash in her home, according to court records.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gutierrez and two other men – Rene and Pedro Garcia – went to Harrison’s home to rob her on Sept.5,1998.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The accounts of what happened in her home that night vary.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gutierrez says he waited outside and had no idea things would get violent.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Regardless, Harrison ended up "face down in a pool of blood" after having been beaten and stabbed about 13 times, court records say.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Though Gutierrez thought Harrison had $600,000 in the home, it's unclear how much money the men made away with.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Prosecutors say it was at least \\(56,000.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hernandez said it was his mother's dying wish that he make sure Gutierrez is executed.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He had been set to be among the witnesses at Tuesday's execution.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: DOJ went too far against Trump case

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Jonathan Turley Opinion contributor

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: From left, U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, former President Donald Trump and special counsel Jack Smith. U.S. DISTRICT COURT, AFP VIA GETTY IMAGES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland," the Mad Hatter asks Alice, "Why is a raven like a writing desk?" It turned out that the Mad Hatter had no better idea than Alice.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In her93-page order, U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon seemed to face the same dilemma when she asked special counsel Jack Smith why a private citizen is like a confirmed U.S. attorney.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On Monday, Judge Cannon dismissed the criminal case against former President Donald Trump over his handling of classified documents, ruling that Smith's appointment as special counsel was unlawful.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The judge has struggled with the assertion of Attorney General Merrick Garland that he may pick private citizens to serve as special counsels and exercise greater authority than a federal prosecutor without any appointment under the Constitution or clear statutory authority.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Biden administration has argued that even asking about its authority is as absurd and frivolous as asking about ravens and writing desks.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It notes that most courts have dismissed these claims with little argument or consideration.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yet, Cannon kept coming back to the question: Why is a private citizen like a confirmed U.S. attorney?

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Justice Thomas raised same issue

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is the same question asked by Justice Clarence Thomas in his recent concurrence in the Trump immunity case.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If this unprecedented prosecution is

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: to proceed, it must be conducted by someone duly authorized to do so by the American people," Thomas wrote. "The lower courts should thus answer these essential questions concerning the Special Counsel's appointment before proceeding."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Someone just did. Cannon found the question neither frivolous nor easy.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After all, we have a demanding constitutional process for the presidential appointment of a U.S. attorney and the Senate confirmation of that nominee.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yet, the Justice Department has argued that Garland can either follow that constitutional process or just grab any private citizen (like former top Justice Department official Jack Smith) to exercise more power than a federal prosecutor. Moreover, the attorney general can make such unilateral appointments by the gross if he wanted.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Judge Cannon also noted that the special counsel is pulling funds from the Treasury (\(12 million by a recent count) and many clear appropriation from Congress.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Article I, Section9, Clause7 of the Constitution states, "No Money shall be drawn from the Treasury, but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law." Yet, Smith is pulling money under a permanent indefinite appropriation reserved for an "independent counsel."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He is not an independent counsel, however, because the Independent Counsel Act expired in 1999. This means Smith must show some "other law" granting him this authority. The court said that he failed to do so.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 'Very little oversight or supervision'

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cannon noted in her ruling that "there does appear to be a 'tradition' of appointing special-attorney-like figures in moments of political scandal throughout the country's history. But very few, if any, of these figures actually resemble the position of Special Counsel (SJC). The SJC is not an advocate citizen exercising the full power of a United States Attorney, and with very little oversight or supervision."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: With that, the judge dismissed the case and, with it, 40 charges stemming from Trump's handling of documents marked classified after leaving office and allegedly obstructing the Justice Department's investigation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: From the outset, I have maintained that the Florida case was the greatest threat to Trump. Where the other cases had serious constitutional, statutory and evidentiary flaws, the Florida case is a case of well-established laws and precedent.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It was not the law but the lawyer who proved to be the problem. Jack Smith was himself the argument that would bring down his case - at least for now.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The special counsel said Monday that he will appeal, but the decision makes any trial in Florida before the election virtually impossible. That in itself is a huge victory for Trump.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Smith still has a second case in Washington, D.C., with an ideal judge and jury pool. However, the Supreme Court recently ripped the wings off that case by first limiting the use of obstruc

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: tion charges (which constitute half of the four counts against Trump) and then declared that the former president is either absolutely immune or presumptively immune on an array of acts and evidence impacting the indictment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan has proved very favorable to Smith in moving away obstacles to try Trump before the election. However, perhaps for that reason, the Supreme Court went out of its way to narrow her range of movement on these questions.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Thus, even if Chutkan refuses to reconsider the constitutional issues on Smith's appointment, she will be hard pressed to hold a trial before the election and even harder pressed to make it stick on appeal.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In the end, the appointment question has good-faith arguments on both sides, which Judge Cannon acknowledged in her detailed opinion. She believes that he is reversed on appeal, but this issue seems likely to go to the Supreme Court.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Immunity case could go up to Inauguration Day

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Convicting Trump either before or after the election seems to be Smith's overriding priority. The Washington Post reported this month that the special counsel is prepared to pursue the conviction of Trump until Jan. 20, when Trump would take the oath of office if reelected in November.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The problem for Smith is now another question worthy of the Mad Hatter: What can crawl and fly with only hands but no legs or wings?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The answer is the one thing that the special counsel no longer has: time.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Jonathan Turley is the Shapiro Professor of Public Interest Law at George Washington University. He is the author of "The Indispensable Right : Free Speech in an Age of Rage".

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Let's look at Trump's judge on documents

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Chris Brennan USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: This image, attached as evidence in the indictment against former President Donald Trump on classified documents, shows stacks of boxes in a buthroom and shower allegedly at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida. PROVIDED BY U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE VIA AFF.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It would be easy to get angry at this point about how law and order is alleged to apply to everyone in America, but former President Donald Trump keeps being issued get-out-of-jail-free cards by judges he appointed.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It happened again Monday when the judge overseeing Trump's federal case for allegedly taking and concealing classified documents after leaving office decided to rule counter to decades of established law  and precedence to just toss the case out of court.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That's frustrating to fair-minded people, no matter what political party you belong to.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: We're told as children that nobody is above the law in America and we hope as adults to see that hold true.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But this would be a good time to press pause on our frustration because U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon, dominated in April 2020 by then-Principles Court法官。 Southern District of Florida, is likely to face some judgment about her judgment.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Judge Aileen Cannon did her part in the Trump document case.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: We've been here before. It didn't go so well for Cannon.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cannon's ruling has nothing to do with the merits of the case. Instead, the judge grabbed hold of a fringe legal argument that Jack Smith, the special counsel appointed in November 2022 by U.S. Attorney General Merrick Garland to oversee the investigation, was improperly selected.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Trump was indicted by a federal grand jury and charged last summer. His entire legal strategy since then has been to delay delay while painting the prosecution as a political vendetta as he seeks another term as president.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In this, Cannon has always seemed

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Cannon

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: more like an eager collaborator than an impartial judge, dragging out the process and leaving legal motions in limbo while sparring with prosecutors. All the while, the clock is ticking down

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: the Nov. 5 general election.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A Trump victory would make the case simply vanish.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Decision to throw out document case started years ago

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One of Trump's opening gambits in the case in 2022, months before charges were filed, was to ask Judge Cannon to prevent prosecutors from examining the thousands of documents it found - some marked confidential or top secret-in boxes strewn across the ex-president's private club in Florida while executing a search warrant.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The judge played along, shutting

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: down the prosecutors and appointing a "special master" to sift through the documents in question.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The special counsel appealed to the Ith Circuit Court of Appeals, known for a certain right-leaning tilt on the political scale, where the case was heard by three judges, including two appointed by Trump.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Those judges, in December 2022, reversed Judge Cannon in a 21-page ruling that ended with what amounted to a scolding for her for what amounted to an attempt at a "radical reordering" to the court. The federal judges act in criminal investigations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The law is clear," the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals judges wrote. "We cannot write a rule that allows any subject of a search warrant to block government investigations after the execution of the warrant. Nor can we write a rule that allows only former presidents to do so."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Let's not forget Supreme Court's role

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That's the way the law is supposed to work. Everyone is equal.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Unless, of course, the U.S. Supreme Court decides otherwise.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The other recent development that has law-and-order fans freaking out was the Supreme Court's July 1 ruling that Trump has immunity for any "official acts" he took as president while attempting to overturn the 2020 presidential election but can still be tried in a separate case in federal court in Washington, D.C., for any "unofficial acts" he took in that attempt.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Justice Clarence Thomas joined the court's other six conservatives, three appointed by Trump, in that 6-3 ruling but couldn't resist helping Trump on a legal point that was not part of the case - writing a concurring opinion that questioned whether Smith's appointment as special counsel was legal.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Thomas opened the door for Cannon to toss the documents charges against trump, And that's just  what she did.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Cannon tucked her ruling Monday into a news cycle already ramped up to

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: full bore, between the attempted assassination of Trump in Pennsylvania on Saturday and his selection of a vice presidential running mate at the Republican National Convention in Milwaukee on Monday evening.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Trump, who briefly called for unity after surviving Saturday, was right back at his usual rhetoric Monday, casting his legal troubles as "Political Attacks". "while celebrating Cannon's ruling on his social media site, calling for dismissal "of ALL the Witch Hunts."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That included the case pending in Washington, a pending criminal case in Georgia on attempts to overturn the 2020 election there, the civil case where he was found liable for sexual assault, the criminal case in New York where he was convicted on 34 felony counts, and a civil case where he was fined \( \\( {454} \) million for running a real estate business rifle with fraud.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: So many cases. And only one Judge Cannon.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 'Future Supreme Court Justice Cannon'?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Trump sees all politics as transactional- if he does something for you,he will expect something from you.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rep. Matt Gaetz, R-Fla., an avid social media troll, said the quiet part out loud Monday in a post on the site previously known as Twitter with Cannon's official portrait, calling her "Future Supreme Court Justice Cannon."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Speaking of the highest court in the land, the justices took a pass in October 2022 when Trump asked them to overturn the llth Circuit, which had just overturned Cannon.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If the special counsel successfully appeals the new Cannon ruling and revives the documents case, Trump will be able to find his luck again with our highest court.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then we'll find out just how many get-out-of-jail-free cards the conservative justices are willing to deal him.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Medora Lee USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If expensive home prices have forced you to rent, you should at least get the best renting experience for your money. About 45 million Americans rent homes with a record high 22.4 million households spending more than \(30\%\) of their income on rent and utilities in 2022, according to a study by Harvard University's Joint Center for Housing Studies. If you're forced to spend money on rent, you may want more than just an affordable roof over your head, housing advocates say. You might also want to know that you have tenant law on your side if there's ever an issue and a great quality of life, including easy public transportation, entertainment and job opportunities. To find the cities that offer the whole package, ApartmentAdvisor researched 98 cities nationwide to determine the best and worst cities for renters. Raleigh, North Carolina, was the most rent-friendly city, while Akron, Ohio, was the least friendly, it said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: What cities are best for renters?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The three most renter-friendly cities, according to ApartmentAdvisor, are:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Raleigh, North Carolina: Raleigh's one of the fastest-growing cities in the U.S., but what makes it remarkable is its pace of building new homes has kept up with demand. It's not the cheapest place to rent, with the median price being 11,263 a month, but rent is falling year over year after hitting a pandemic peak in August 2022. The main drawback is that tenant protections aren't as strong as in some other cities.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Huntsville, Alabama: At $863, Huntsville has one of the lowest monthly median rents for a one-bedroom apartment on the list. Like Raleigh, it has a high number of new residential construction permits and a healthy vacancy rate, but fewer tenant protection laws. Rents are also dropping in Huntsville, making the share of income required to rent well below 30%.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Oakland, California: Rent control laws, high vacancy rates and a high average number of days on the market for apartment listings give this northern California city a boost. However, with the median one-bedroom rent at \(1,941 a month, the median yearly income at \)79,304, a lot of your annual gross income (29%) will be spent on housing.

layout_dets.text: Which cities are the worst for renters?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The least renter-friendly cities are:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Akron, Ohio: Lagging new supply has substantially pushed up rents in the past year. The median cost of a one-bedroom is \(750 a month, which is low when compared to some other cities but is high for Akron. A year ago, the median rent there was \)700.

layout_dets.text: - El Paso, Texas: El Paso has seen some relief in rent prices in the past year, but it's still the Texas city with the least new residential construction on ApartmentAdvisor's list. The monthly median one-bedroom rent is \(831.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Fort Wayne, Indiana: Fort Wayne is another Midwest city that suffers from a lack of new housing supply. The median one-bedroom rent was \(888 in June. That's low when compared to many other cities, but it's up from \)800 a year ago.

layout_dets.text: - The biggies: Major cities like New York City and Boston also ranked at the bottom, coming in at numbers six and nine, respectively. "These cities rate high for desirability and both have robust landlord-tenant laws on the books, but both are notoriously competitive rental markets with substantial rent growth driving higher rent burden," said Milman, ApartmentAdvisor.com's editor.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Beware AI voice scams that could rip you off

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Tech Talk Kim Komando

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: You've heard the stories... A CEO was conned out of \(233,000 when someone copied the voice of his parent company's boss. A 75-year-old woman nearly lost \)27,500, thinking her grandson was in trouble.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: With as little as $4, anyone can copy a voice with super-cheap, super-powerful artificial intelligence software. I’ve got the inside scoop on tricks these scammers use so you don’t fall for it.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 10 popular tactics

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In the age of TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, LinkedIn and YouTube, where we broadcast our lives (and voices) to the world, scammers are having a field day. They're extracting voice samples, feeding them into their AI machines and producing chillingly accurate voice clones. With that, the stage is set for a scam that's as emotionally brutal as it is ingenious.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Pro tip: Unless you're trying to make it as an influencer or you're a public fig

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ure of some kind, set your social media profiles to private. You're just giving too much away with a public account.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Here's a rundown of 10 popular scams you can spot this crap before you get taken:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Kids’ summer camp upset: There’s been a gas leak and they need to evacuate immediately. The camp counselor wants you to pay for a hotel room and bus ride for your child.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Charity request: A voice you've definitely heard on TV called you, looking for cash to help disaster victims. What's your credit card number?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Neighbor needs help: She's crying that your dog was hit by a car and she took him to the vet. You'll pay the bill now, right?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Auto parts emergency: Your trustworthy mechanic calls with bad news: Don't tell your car because there's been a major recall and you need to buy the parts now!

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Urgent business expense: Your boss calls from an unknown number. They’re at a business conference and urgently need you to wire money for unexpected expenses. Can you handle it right away?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Medical emergency: A relative's voice frantically tells you they've been in a serious accident and need money immediately to pay the hospital bill be

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: fore they can be treated.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Stuck in jail: Your child has been arrested and needs bail money immediately. They instruct you to send the money to a specific account before things get even worse.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Utility shuts off: A representative from the electric company, sounding exactly like someone you've spoken to before, says your service will be shut off unless you make an immediate payment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: School fundraiser: Your kid’s school principal calls, asking for donations to support a new project. They just need your credit card information to process the donation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Travel trouble: A close friend calls from a vacation spot. They've lost their wallet and are stranded. Can you wire him a phone call to cover their hotel bill and return flight?

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Your plan of action

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Before you consider selling the family silver or clearing your savings account, let’s talk strategy. You need to know about this now so you’re prepared before something scary happens.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Check the caller ID: If the call's coming from a number you don't recognize or, even worse, a blocked or hidden

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: number, that's a big red flag. Even if it sounds like your kiddo or mom on the other end, hang up, then dial them on their cell.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Verify with video: In high-profile cons like those involving a business, scammers have used AI video, too. But most low-budget cons won't go that far.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Buy time: If the voice on the other end claims they're in a jam - say, an accident or they've been detained - tell them you'll help but want to check things out first. Immediately try to reach that person through other means or contact someone who might know their whereabouts.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ? Money talks: If someone demands a wire transfer or Bitcoin payment, your scam alert should be blaring. Authentic emergencies don't come with specific, shady payment demands.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: People fall for this stuff every day. Take care of the folks in your life by sharing this story. It could save someone's financial future.

layout_dets.text: Learn about all the latest technology on the Kim Komando Show, the nation's largest weekend radio talk show. Kim takes calls and dispenses advice on today's digital lifestyle, from smartphones and tablets to online privacy and data hack. For her daily tips, free newsletters and more, visit her website.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Economy

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1B

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: about half that inflow

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Here's a look at the debate:

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: How many immigrants enter the US per year?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Congressional Budget Office recently estimated net immigration to the U.S. was2.6 million in2022,3.3 million in2023 and a projected3.3 million this year. The figures are much higher than previously believed and above the900,000 average from2010 to2019.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: About 2.4 million of the entrants were unauthorized, the CBO says, with the vast majority entering at the southern border.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: How is the US economy affected by immigration?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Immigrants are doing work that lifts production, and earning income to buy homes, cars, groceries, clothing, health care and other products and services that expand the nation's economy.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In other words, they've helped keep the nation from slipping into a recession that was widely anticipated last year because of high inflation and interest rates.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In a study last week, the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas estimated immigration is increasing annualized economic growth in a given quarter by 0.7 percentage points at an annual rate. That means it could have comprised half of the tepid \(1.4\%\) annualized increase in growth early this year.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A JPMorgan Chase analysis of immigration in23 developed countries from1990 to2020 found that a1% annual increase in population from immigration – roughly in line with the U.S. gain last year – would boost economic growth by1.6 percentage points.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That's about half last year's \(3.1\%\) rise in U.S. gross domestic product.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Others say the immigration-induced GDP bump is more modest. A Brookings Institution report estimated it added a tenth of a percentage point to growth in 2022, two-tenth in 2023 and a projected two-tenths this year.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: What percentage of jobs is filled by immigrants?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Foreign-born people come to the U.S. at relatively young ages and64% to66% are in the labor force – meaning they're working or looking for jobs – compared with about60% of U.S. natives, according to JPMorgan Chase and the Brookings Institution.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Of the3 million jobs the nation added last year, about a third likely went to newly arrived immigrants, most of who entered the country illegally, RBC Capital Markets estimates.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Can immigration fix labor shortages?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The nation grappled with severe post-pandemic labor shortages from 2021 to 2023. To attract workers, employers pushed up the annual rise in average hourly pay to a peak of \(5.9\%\) in early 2022 from \(3\%\) before the pandemic.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The influx of immigrants helped ease the worker shortages and tamp down wage growth to about \(4\%\). The gains

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Hundreds of workers sort and package tomatoes during a shift at Quincy Tomato Company on June 12, 2023. Graves Williams, owner of Quincy Tomato Company, said his business couldn't operate without immigrant laborers. A LUCIA DEVINE/USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Across the labor market, Deutsche Bank estimates the immigration spike over the past four years has increased the number of people employed - and reduced total job vacancies - by as much as 3.9 million, easing wage pressures that intensify inflation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: have especially aided some low-paying industries that struggle most to attract employees, economists say.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: From December 2021 to December 2023, immigrant employment in leisure and hospitality - which includes restaurants and hotels - increased by 5.5 percentage points, reducing the share of job vacancies by 4.4 percentage points, according to a study by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Employers, in turn, could compete less vigorously for workers, and annual wage growth fell by3.9 percentage points – accounting for early half the drop in the industry's pay increases during the two-year period, from13.9% to4.1%.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Across the labor market, Deutsche Bank estimates the immigration spike over the past four years has increased the number of people employed - and reduced total job vacancies - by as much as 3.9 million, easing wage pressures that intensify inflation.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: How does wage growth affect inflation?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As businesses passed their higher labor costs to consumers, prices soared, especially for services such as dining and health care, auto repair and haircuts.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Pandemic-related supply chain troubles also fueled inflation by pushing up the price of goods such as furniture, appliances and cars.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Without the immigration spike, the Federal Reserve's preferred annual inflation measure, which fell from a peak of5.6% in2022 to2.8% in the first quarter,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ter, would have been as high as \(3.1\%\) to \(3.3\%\), a Deutsche Bank analysis says.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The quarter-to-half-point inflation decline spurred by immigrants is in line with the 0.37 percentage point slide estimated by the Center for Immigration Studies, an anti-immigration think tank. "It's too small to make a dent in overall inflation," says Jason Richwine, resident scholar at the center.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the pullback is still "notable" and has significant implications, Reid, of RBC Capital Markets, says. After raising its key interest rate to a 23-year high of about \(5.1\%\) to fight inflation, the Fed is widely expected to begin cutting interasset reates in September, lowering the cost of mortgages and other loans while juicing the stock market.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Absent the immigration surge, inflation likely would have hovered above \(3\%\) for several additional months, leading the Fed to keep rates higher for longer and raising the odds of a recession, Reid says.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Do immigrants take jobs from Americans?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At his debate with Biden last month, Trump said many of the jobs immigrants were taking otherwise would be filled by American citizens, particularly Black and Hispanic people.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Reid, though, says U.S.-born workers often aren't interested in many of the arduous, low-paying jobs sought by immigrants who lack permanent legal status. And Americans generally don't want for jobs. The share of employed prime-age(25-54)people born in the U.S. is at 83%, higher than before the pandemic, Jason Furman, former chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers, wrote in a recent opinion piece in the Wall Street Journal.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Are immigrants depressing wages for Americans?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At a Senate hearing last week, Vance acknowledged immigration has helped ease the labor crunch and slow wage growth.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But, he told the witness, Fed Chair Jerome Powell, "It also puts downward pressure on the wages that people earn for their family. Why do we see that as a good thing?"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Instead of relying on immigration, he suggested, employers should have jacked up wages high enough to attract

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: more Americans to their job openings. Presumably, pay increases would then moderate as labor gaps closed.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In a March report, Michael Feroli, chief U.S. economist of JPMorgan Chase, agreed that "wage gains for lower-skilled workers could suffer" because of immigration.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But remedying labor shortages by hiking wages even more sharply for Americans wasn't practical in many cases, Reid said. The deficits were so severe that there were two jobs for every unemployed worker and many firms couldn't fill vacancies even with big pay bumps.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Many people with the right skills didn't live near the jobs and were unwilling to move, he said. Others were reluctant to work because they were still benefiting from pandemic-related stimulus checks and other savings. And if businesses raised wages so high that Americans on the sidelines couldn't resist the offers, lots of companies wouldn't be profitable, Reid says.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Can immigration cause inflation?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yes. By stoking more consumer demand for products and services, immigration also fuels inflation. And immigrants are more inclined than people born in the U.S. to spend most or all of their income, Feroli wrote in the report.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The effect on prices is especially pronounced in housing, with new immigrants needing as much as 500,000 additional units a year, Feroli says. In June, rent and other housing costs made up about \(36\%\) of the monthly inflation rise, according to the consumer price index. The nation already is beset by a big housing shortage and it takes time for developers to respond to unexpected immigration spikes by building homes, Feroli says.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At the same time, because most immigrants living in the country without legal permission work in low-wage industries, they spend less overall than those born in the U.S., Reid says. Immigrants, he says, also send an average of $160 a month to their families in their native countries.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The bottom line?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Normally, the effects of an immigration surge on inflation are a wash or may even increase it in the short term, JPMorgan economists Alexander Wise and Jan Loeyes wrote in a note to clients. Besides the purchases by new foreign-born residents, immigration gooses demand from companies that need to buy computers, factory machines or other equipment for their newly hired immigrant workers, the Dallas Fed paper says.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yet during dire labor shortages, such as the recent episode, immigration may ease inflation because the benefits of expanding the supply of workers outweigh the jolt to household spending, Wise and Loey's suggested.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Do immigrants have a positive net impact on the economy?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Many economists think so. Normally, strong job growth triggers faster price increases by forcing employers to bid up wages to attract a limited pool of U.S. workers and by increasing consumer spending.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The immigration wave, though, "has provided a significant boost to GDP without a corresponding rise in inflation," said John Mai, an economist at the Dallas Fed.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Pain of Freedman's Bank collapse remains

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Author says it played role in the racial wealth gap

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Charisse Jones  
USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In "The Rise and Fall of the Freedman's Savings Bank and Its Lasting Socio-economic Impact on Black America" (Spiramus Press), former USA TODAY Deputy Managing Editor of Money Rodney A. Brooks tells the story of an institution created to give newly emancipated African Americans a place where they could deposit their earnings and begin to bank for a life that is in the wake of corruption, mismanagement and fraud committed by its white management, the bank was shuttered.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Brooks, an award-winning financial journalist, spoke to USA TODAY's Money and Consumer News Editor Charisse Jones about the bank's creation, collapse and bankruptcy 150 years later. The interview has been edited for clarity and length.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Question: Why did you want to write this book?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Answer: I think it's a lost piece of history. So many people know about the Freedmen's Bureau, but the Freedman's Bank, even with its sad ending, is not something that's really taught. It's also an underrated cause or root of the racial wealth gap because the money that people have invested in this country which was $3 million in 1874 but $80 million in today's dollars - that money would have gone to educating their children, buying homes and farmland. So the loss of generational wealth was immense.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Can you say more about how the loss of those savings impacted the building of generational wealth?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: White Americans have a homeownership rate of about \(73\%\) and Black Americans have a homeownership rate of \(42\% - 43\%\). Had the bank not failed, and people had not lost their money it would have meant Black former slaves would have been able to buy land, educate their children and build houses, and those are all important components of the racial wealth gap.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Another thing that has carried on is our distrust of the banking system. You might say, "This bank folded 150 years ago," but we still have a strong distrust of the financial system. This is not to take away from the fact that discrimination in the '30s, '40s and '50s at these financial institutions - and some of it is still happening today - is contributing. But there are things that people pass on to their children and grandchildren. A distrust of the banking system still exists and that's still impacting the wealth of Black Americans.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: What's the impact of that distrust?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One of the reasons the bank was established in 1865, besides providing a place for former slaves and Black Civil War veterans to save money, is it was also supposed to be able to provide financial education. So, imagine if financial education had gone back to 1865 for these families not only through the savings process, (but) that knowledge was also supposed to be passed on to Black Americans through jobs and training. They were supposed to be staffers, tellers and managers at these bank branches. Had that happened you would

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: have generational knowledge of finance that does not exist today.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: You note that the bank was initially successful. How so?

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Brooks

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Black people looked at it as a Black bank though it wasn't. It was created by

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Congress and had a board of white men in New York. People used to dress up to go to the bank because it was a big deal. It grew to 37 branches and  60,000 depositors, so you had people using it and actually gaining interest

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: on their money. Twenty percent of the depositors were children. So even though it was undercapitalized, the success was in how fast it grew and how far the reach was. But that also proved difficult. It could take two weeks for communication to go from the main branch, and many of the people running the (local) branches didn't have the financial experience or wherewithal to be in those jobs. Some were incompetent and some were outright thieves.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some people don't want to look at how systemic practices or neglect can have an impact decades later. What do you say to that?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It's very hard to argue against something needing to be done when you look at what brought down the Freedman's Bank. When you look at the housing disparities, the income disparities, there is much that ties racism and discrimination to these disparities. But there will always be people who want to deny history and I talk in the book about how some of these states are trying to whitewash history and remove it from schools

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: so what little people know about Black history is reduced even more.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: What are some of the ways we can remedy the racial wealth gap?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There's a handful of things you can do. All of them require some level of government support and that brings out the opposition, especially from conservatives, but let's start with reparations. One of the big arguments against reparations is how do you identify the people you're supposed to provide reparations for. Well, with the Freedman's Bank, the records are still there. The National Archives in College Park, Maryland, has been working with the local communities to name and information. So if you want to talk about reparations for this specifically, there are historical records that could provide some guidance to finding the descendants of these people.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Baby bonds is another. Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., has proposed legislation that would provide a savings account to every child born in America, and money would be added every year and there would be more money added for the lower income families. So when a baby of any color got to be 18, they would have money to buy a house, buy a car. Morningstar, which is a financial services company, has recently been asked by parents to help reduce the racial wealth gap by about \(50\%\). Increasing the number of Black families who own homes can have a huge impact but to get more Black families into homes, the biggest obstacle is the down payment. So programs that will help people to save the down payment, or finding alternative ways to do that down payment, will have a big impact on the racial wealth gap.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Disney World's sites offer accessibility for wheelchair users

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: A wheelchair user on the Jungle Cruise. PROVIDED BY DAVE PARFITT/FAMILYVACATIONIST

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Dave Parfitt FamilyVacationist.com

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Disney World's four theme parks are so well-known for their inclusivity that Disney trips are often among the top wishes of children with critical illnesses. Attractions in and around Walt Disney World are not only accessible to guests using mobility aids (walkers, wheelchairs and motorized devices) but also to those with cognitive impairments and visual or auditory limitations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: These accommodations make Disney World an outstanding destination for multigenerational groups, and one of the reasons my family returns again and again. My wife, Dana, uses a wheelchair due to her multiple sclerosis, so when we took our first post-pandemic trip back to Disney this year, we decided to see just what an accessible vacation at "The Most Magical Place On Earth" would actually be like. The verdict: It's still pretty magical.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Here's what you should know about getting around Walt Disney World in a wheelchair, starting from the moment you land.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Accessibility at Orlando International Airport

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Living in upstate New York, we often fly nonstop into Orlando, Florida, from our local airport in Rochester to minimize time on airplanes. Orlando International Airport is one of the busiest in the world, but also one that travelers with special needs can navigate easily.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The airport has three different terminals. After your airplane lands, an automated people mover takes you to the main terminal. This tram is roll-on/roll-off for those using wheelchairs and other mobility devices. Moving walkways and escalators help minimize walking distances throughout the airport. In addition, there are also visual, paging systems, companion care restrooms, adult changing tables and service animal relief areas to assist with accessibility.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: An accessibility map of the airport is available to identify all services ahead of time. Orlando International Airport also participates in the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower Program, allowing guests with a hidden disability to wear a sunflower lanyard to self-identify as someone who may need additional assistance passing through the terminal.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Accessibility within Disney's theme parks in Orlando

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Animal Kingdom, EPCOT, Hollywood Studios and Magic Kingdom each have

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: individual guides for guests with disabilities. These theme park guides give specific information about accessible entrances, mobility requirements, sign language, captioning, audio description, and use of companion restrooms and more.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Visitors can download these guides ahead of time from Walt Disney World's website. Visitors with impairments, including those on the autism spectrum, can use break areas in the parks to get away from sensory stimulation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: For our trip, we utilized the Disney World app to find attractions my wife could enjoy while staying in her wheelchair. We did this by filtering rides by park and mobility accessibility, selecting "may remain in wheelchair/EVC" to see which ones would work for our family. We discovered we also needed to select "must transfer to wheelchair" to see the full list of attractions Dana could ride.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Not surprisingly, most of the highspeed thrill rides were off-limits to those in a wheelchair, including newer rides like Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind. Still, we found more attractions than we expected where Dana could stay in her wheelchair, including some of our favorites such as Jungle Safari. Eight-hour's Space Ranger Spin in the Magic Kingdom, Toy Story Mania! in Disney's Hollywood Studios and the new Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in EPCOT.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Unfortunately, aside from Kilimanjaro Safaris, there were very few rides at Disney's Animal Kingdom where Dana could stay in her wheelchair (although there were shows and animals to watch). As a family of Star Wars fans, we were most disappointed to discover that neither of the two attractions in Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge accommodated someone who needed to stay in a wheelchair. This surprised us since the land just opened in 2019.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In addition to using the Disney World app to find attractions that accommodate your needs, Disney also offers the Disability Access Service to assist visitors who cannot wait for extended periods in a conventional queue due to their disability. Disney recently announced changes to the service, and it will only assist guests with developmental disabilities, like autism. Guests who qualify can register ahead of time for Disability Access Service via a live video chat between 30 and two days before arrival at the park.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: You then set a reservation time for an experience on the day of your theme park visit, and enjoy other aspects of the park until you can redeem your return time at the attraction. Once that return time has been redeemed, you can

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: then request another one. This type of "virtual queuing" has become commonplace in the theme park industry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: My wife's mobility limitations will now no longer qualify for Disability Access Service as she can wait in line while sitting in her wheelchair. On our most recent visit, it turned out she never needed the service and we navigated the theme parks just fine using the Disney World app. However, because heat also exacerbates her symptoms, she may sometimes be unable to wait in the Florida heat even while sitting in her chair.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Accessibility at Walt Disney World Resort hotels

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Disney World has a wide range of hotels of various points and amenities. When planning your Disney World vacation, consider what park is your highest priority to visit. For many families, it's Magic Kingdom, the quintessential Disney World theme park. Thus, one of the monorail resorts (Contemporary, Polynesian Village or Grand Floridian) would offer the most convenience to that park. However, Star Wars fans might want to stay closer to Disney's Hollywood Studios, making Disney's Boardwalk a good choice.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: My family loves Disney's Polynesian Village Resort. The Polynesian Village has smaller separate buildings, with wide, flat outdoor pathways. Accessible rooms on the first floor have a wheelchair-friendly door where you can roll out to the patio and enjoy those nice Florida breezes. Approximately \(10\%\) of the room is covered with a large-screen TV, with some with roll-in showers. The Polynesian also has a number of our favorite restaurants, including Kona Cafe (famous for its Tonga Toast) and Ohana,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: with its all-you-can-eat family-style Hawaiian dinner.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Disney's Polynesian is a short monorail ride to the Magic Kingdom right from the second floor of the hotel lobby (an elevator is available for those in wheelchairs). A short stroll along a wheelchair-accessible path will get you to the EPCOT monorail station. Accessible bus transportation is also provided from the resort to Disney's Hollywood Studios and Animal Kingdom.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On our most recent trip, we stayed at Disney's Riviera Resort, a Disney Vacation Club property in between EPCOT and Disney's Hollywood Studios. The Skyliner gondola station is a perk of Disney's Riviera Resort. My wife could roll her wheelchair into an aerial cable car to head to one of the two theme parks.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The larger one-bedroom wheelchair-accessible vacation club villa also provided more space to maneuver a wheelchair and walker after we rearranged some of the furniture. In addition to the extra space of the vacation club villa, we discovered some perks that made our stay more accessible, such as special breakfast menus. However, this Disney resort, your family says, visited the official Walt Disney World website to make sure the room has the specific accommodations you need.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Our recent trip to Disney World in a wheelchair was not without difficulties, but any family trip will present challenges along the way. Disney scores high marks for its commitment to making the parks accessible. As Disney World creates new attractions, I hope they continue to find ways to make those experiences available for all family members to enjoy.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Bloomington: A small, rare snake found almost exclusively in the Midwest could eventually gain protection under the Endangered Species Act after a settlement was reached between the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and two nonprofits. The settlement agreement between the FWS and the Hoosier Environmental Council and Center for Biological Diversity may not only help Kirtland's snakes, but also the wetlands where they live. The FWS will reevaluate the snake's status to determine if it should be listed as federally threatened or endangered. The agency has a deadline of June 30, 2026, to make its finding.

layout_dets.text: TROON, Scotland - As past U.S. Open champion Gary Woodland opened his sand wedge wide and practiced in the sand, Brennan Little, his caddie, took one look at the bunker with three steps to help golfers descend into the pit and said, "That must be the coffin bunker. It really does look like a coffin."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Colin Beard, a hole marshal and a member at nearby Troon Welbeck Golf Club, nodded in agreement and shot back, "It's death to the average player. It's a killer."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "There's no death for these guys," Little responded. "They're too good."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Just tell your guy, don't hit it there," advised Beard.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The eighth hole at Royal Troon is nicknamed The Postage Stamp, which sounds all warm and fuzzy, except it should come with one of those warnings on the side of a pack of cigarettes because it can be dangerous to a player's health and his scorecard this week.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At 123 yards, it measures as the shortest hole in the Open rota and as the fifth shortest hole in major championship history. It plays essentially the same distance - to a green 33 acres in width and almost 3,600 square feet in size - as it did 101 years ago when Troon first played the British Open. The L-shaped tree plays slightly downhill, with an elevation drop of 20 feet, and depending on the direction and strength of the wind it can be hit with just a flick of a wedge.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It looks smaller than it really is as we stand trembling on the tee with some form of pitching club in hand," Kate Bernard Darwin several years ago.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And yet players may prefer a 3 o'clock root canal to trying to escape its fortress of bunkers, surrounding the front, right and left of the green.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Architect and Troon club pro Willie Fernie, who won the British Open in 1883 at Musselbergh and was runnerup four times, is credited with creating the Postage Stamp, shortening a blind one-shotter over a dune, with the Ailsa Craig in the distance. layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ARLINGTON, Texas - Mason Miller and Garrett Crochet throw the baseball harder than almost anyone on the planet, play for two of the worst teams that compete at the game's highest level and still are years away from determining their fate through free agency.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is an odd and almost unprecedented place to be, a walking Statcast phenomenon and trade rumor all at once.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yet when you play for the 37-61, Sacramento-to-Vegas-bound Oakland Athletics and average 100.9 mph on your softball while converting 15 of 17 games, you're going to draw significant interest - and Miller most certainly has.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And when your first full season as a starting pitcher results in a major league-leading 150 strikeshroughs before the All-Star break, like Crochet, the fact your Chicago White Sox are off to a historically bad 27-71 start means he can figuratively pack his bags for Midway.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Never mind that Miller entered this season with less than a year of service time and will have five full seasons before free agency. Or that Crochet faces an unknown second half of usage and innings limit questions, and the White Sox control his rights for two seasons beyond this one.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They are that good, and their teams that bad, that their otherworldly talents might be best served to triage two organizations bleeding out at all levels.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This week, Miller and Crochet shared a locker room as first-time American League All-Stars who share a similar tool: compartmentalization.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Best to tune out the uncertainty and know that, deep down, it's good to be wanted. Even if it means a change of address.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's not something I necessarily expected, just with my age," says Crochet, a 25-year-old like Miller. "At the same time, it's a testament to the season that I'm having. When you're having a season like this, maybe the potential returns outweigh what you're receiving right now.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I don't know. I'm not the guy to make that call. But I think it's a huge compliment that the value I provide to you is right now, someone else wants."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Crocket's season has surprised himself and the White Sox; he lobbied general manager Chris Getz to join the rotation after spending the 2020-21 seasons as a reliever before Tommy Mendoza. On April 2022 shelved him until this year.

layout_dets.text:
With Simone Biles, Suni Lee, Hezly Rivera, Jordan Chiles and Jade Carey, right, the U.S. gymnastics team for Paris Games will be the most diverse yet.
MATT KROHN/USA TODAY SPORTS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Seeing Simone Biles, Jordan Chiles, Suni Lee and Hezly Rivera playing in the confetti after the U.S. gymnastics trials in June was a powerful moment, four women of color celebrating their status as Olympians in what has traditionally been a predominantly white sport.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Less than two weeks later, Talladega College announced it was dropping its women's gymnastics program after just one season because of a lack of resources, leaving Fisk University as the only HBCU school with a team.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The contrast between these two events represents the challenge gymnastics faces. Elite gymnastics, the national team in particular, has become a model of representation and inspiration

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: while diversity elsewhere in the sport remains harder to sustain, if not elusive.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But there is hope that just as Biles, Lee, Gabby Douglas and Dominique Dawes sparked interest from little girls of color, this generation of athletes - and the prospect of an Olympics in Los Angeles in four years - will do the same among community leaders and decision-makers.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We need more programs in more diverse areas," said Derrin Moore, founder of Brown Girls Do Gymnastics (BGDG). "We already have the parents and the kids who say, I want to do the same thing Simone did!" Moore said. "Now it's the city officials or (community groups). The people who can write checks are now starting to see it, and I think it's affecting it on that level."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Paris will be the third Olympics for Biles, now one of the most recognizable athletes in the world. She's redefined
