layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The hole played to a scoring average of 3.09 in both 2004 and 2016, the two most recent times the Open was played here. It has given fits to some of the greatest, including Greg Norman, who shot a final-round 64 in 1989 but made his lone bogey of the day at No. 8. Three golfers have enjoyed exhilaration, acting the hole in the championship: Gene Sarazen in 1973 in his penultimate Open, little-known pro Dennis Edlund and past champion Ernie Els.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Jim "Bones" Mackay, who was on the bag for Phil Mickelson when he finished second in 2016 and will be working as an on-course reporter for NBC Sports this week, tabbed the Postage Stamp one of the top-five spectator holes in golf.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "And I may be underselling it. It may be one or two," he said. "If I was a patron there this week and the gates opened, I'd be sprinting out there to spend the day. I just think it's an incredible hole."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Mackay said it may be short in stature but it will derail the dreams of someone in the field of 156 in quest of claiming the Claret Jug.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I got really lucky that I didn't caddie for anybody that had any train wrecks there. But as we go through the week, we're going to see quite a few 2s and also some 5 or 6s," Mackay said. "I can't wait to see how it plays out this year, especially if we get a little bit of wind."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Mackay's NBC colleague, analyst Brad Faxon, seconded the motion.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "If you were going to put together your top 10 list of the best par-3s in the world, I don't think anybody could leave

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: the Postage Stamp out as one of the best holes in the world," Faxon said. "It could be No. 1. It could be No. 3 or 5, but it can't be outside the top 10."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Indeed, the Postage Stamp is renowned as one of the great short holes, along the likes of No. 12 at Augusta National and No. 17 at TPC Sawgrass, but doesn't quite get the attention those famed holes do mainly because disaster isn't captured on TV for all to see every year.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the Postage Stamp does have one leg up on those other notable short par-3s: In 1994, the Royal Mail issued a postage stamp of The Postage Stamp. High praise for a hole that Tiger Woods described as a very simple hole.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Hit the ball on the green. That's it," said Woods. "Green good, miss green bad. It doesn't get any more simple than that."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "You don't need a 240-yard par-3 for it to be hard."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: her sport and rewritten its record books over the last decade-plus, putting a sledgehammer to the idea that gymnastics isn't a sport for people of color.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As great an impact as Biles has, though, she is at the top of what has been a rising wave in U.S. gymnastics. She, Douglas and Lee, the last three Olympic all-around champions, are all women of color. Since 1992, every U.S. women's team but one has had at least two athletes of color.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In Paris, four-fifths of the women's team that is heavily favored to win gold are people of color, as are Frederick Richard and Asher Hong on the U.S. Olympic men's gymnastics team.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Quite the change from when Biles was growing up, and mother Nellie recalled her two daughters and one of Biles' best friends often being the only girls of color in the gym and at competitions. Now the World Champions Centre, owned by Nellie and Ron Biles,

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: champions diversity while developing winners.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "When a girl, it doesn't matter what her ethnicity is, sees someone they can relate to on the television screen, they say, 'I want to be just like her,'" Nellie Biles said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I think the diversity is getting broader simply because there are Simones that people can relate to. More and more Black girls are in the sport. More and more Asian girls and Hispanic girls are in the sport.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's very good for the sport."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yet gymnastics overall remains overwhelmingly white. Most coaches are white. Same for judges. In USA Gymnastics' most recent survey of its members, 60% identified as white while less than 14% identified as Black (4.53%), Hispanic (5.15%) or Asian (3.09%); 7.46% identified as two or more races.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Roughly 19% of the respondents either left the question blank or said they were choosing not to answer, but the numbers are similar to a survey ahead of the Tokyo Olympics.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This isn't because people of color aren't interested in the sport. After ev

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ery Olympics, Moore said, she'll hear from people who want to know how they can get their daughters involved in gymnastics.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Her group is now planning to start Brown Boys Do Gymnastics because of demand.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But interest alone isn't enough.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Because most gyms are located in suburban areas, accessibility is an issue. Moore's group is trying to encourage community-based organizations to add even intro-level gymnastics programs so kids, and their parents, can decide whether this is something they really want to pursue.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Even at the lower level, gymnastics is not an inexpensive sport, making cost an issue. Hostile or indifferent atmospheres are also a turnover, Moore said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: People will reach out and say, 'Hey, I want to get my daughter involved in gymnastics, where do I go?' Moore said. Then the conversation becomes, 'It costs $175 a month' or 'It's too far' or 'My daughter doesn't feel like she's getting the attention,' and they're not doing it anymore.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The interest comes about, but it just

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: doesn't stick for whatever reason."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That has a trickle-up effect. If there are fewer gymnasts of color in high school and college programs, schools like Talladega see the gymnastics team as expendable. Talladega supporters launched a fundraising campaign to save the program, and BGDG is using its annual conference that begins Thursday in Atlanta to amplify the message.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If kids of color leave the sport early, or never have the chance to start in the first place, it also means they probably won't become coaches. Or judges.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But given the chance and the support, gymnasts of color can do anything in the sport they want. Just look at the Olympic team.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It is exactly what it should have been all along," Moore said. "If you have a team that for years is all white and you walk down the street and that's not what you see, something's wrong. You may not know where, but something's wrong. We had to break down barriers when it should have been normal."

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Miller, strangely, is in a similar yet opposite boat. A starter when he debuted in 2023, Miller suffered an elbow scare that compelled the A's to move forward to the bulletin. The A's acknowledge Miller may eventually have a future as a starter.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: For now, he is among the game's greatest relievers – a far better asset for a contending team than one in limbo until at least2028, when the A's hope to open a stadium in Las Vegas.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Miller usually toils before crowds of less than 10,000 in Oakland. Tuesday night, a capacity crowd at Globe Life

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Those numbers play particularly well in October. For now, they are the shiny hood ornament on a broken-down organization playing its final season in Oakland's Coliseum.

layout_dets.label: 段落

I'm happy being with the guys I'm with and honored to be here representing them and excited to work with them in the second half."

He's being used as normal now," says A's manager Mark Kotsay, a member of the L.A. Staff. "We just trying to get him to the finish line completely healthy, and 60-plus appearances would be amazing."

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.text: "But at the same point, we also know the value of having him. It provides for our club the stability on the back end. It comes with a high probability of winning baseball games, and that's important to us as well."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Miller's organization can't help but look at the big picture. Their Las Vegas move, Commissioner Rob Manfred says, remains on track even as owner John Fisher continues lining up financing to pay for their new stadium.

His prospects in November and the damaging impact it could have on Democratic candidates down the ballot.

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That said, a CBS News/YouGov poll taken Friday and Saturday showed how the debate had exacerbated the 81-year-old Biden's biggest vulnerability, his age. layout_dets.text: In major decision, Supreme Court allows cities to ban homeless camps

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Ruling comes as record numbers lack housing

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Maureen Grope and Bart Jansen  
USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: WASHINGTON - The Supreme Court ruled Friday that people without homes can be arrested and fined for sleeping in public spaces, overturning a lower court's ruling that enforcing camping bans when shelter is lacking is and unusual punishment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The 6-3 decision was the most significant ruling on the issue from the high court in decades.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It comes as record numbers of Americans lack permanent housing and as both Democratic and Republican leaders have complained a 2018 decision by a lower court has hamstrung their ability to address homeless encampments that threaten health and public safety.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The Court cannot say that the punishments Grants Pass imposes here qualify as cruel and unusual," Justice Neil Gorsuch wrote for the majority, referring to the small Oregon municipality at the center of the case.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The city imposes only limited fines for first-time offenders, an order temporarily barring an individual from camping in a public park for repeat offenders, and a maximum sentence of 30 days in jail for those who later violate an order."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Cruel and unusual punishment?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But Justice Sonia Sotomayor, writing for the court's liberal minority, said the laws essentially criminalized the act of sleeping.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Sleep is a biological necessity, not a crime," Sotomayor wrote in dissent, joined by Justices Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson. "For some people, sleeping outside is their only option."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sotomayor noted that Grants Pass jails and fines people who sleep in public, such as in a car, or for using as little as a blanket to keep warm or a rolled-up shirt as a pillow. "For people with no access to shelter, that punishes them for being homeless," she wrote. "That is un-

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text:
An unhoused woman named Kimberly Morris holds a notice given to her by a police officer that gives her 72 hours to move her tent from the park, in Grants Pass, Ore., on April 18. Justices on Friday ruled that cities can enforce camping bans.
DEBORAH BLOOM/REUTERS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: conscionable and unconstitutional."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Ann Oliva, CEO of the National Alliance to End Homelessness, said the decision gives "Free reign to local officials who prefer pointless and expensive arrests and imprisonment, rather than real solutions."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "This tactic has consistently failed to reduce homelessness in the past," Oliva said, "and it will assuredly fail to reduce homelessness in the future."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: `Urgent relief' to communities

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Theane Evans, who represented Grants Pass, said the decision brought "urgent relief to the many communities that have struggled to address the growing problem of dangerous encampments."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "For the past six years, the Ninth Circuit's decisions have tied the hands of local governments," Evangelis said. "The Court has now restored the ability of cities on the frontlines of this crisis to develop lasting solutions that meet the needs of the most vulnerable members of their communities, while also keeping our public spaces safe and clean."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which oversees nine Western states, ruled in 2018 that banning camping in areas lacking sufficient shelter beds amounts to cruel and unusual punishment under the 8th

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Amendment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Supreme Court declined to weigh in at the time on that case from Boise, Idaho, but took up the issue this term after that precedent was used to challenge anti-camping rules in Grants Pass.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Homeless residents of the southern Oregon city of 38,000 had faced fines starting at \(250 and leading to jail time for repeat offenses.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Criminalizing homelessness in a city without a homeless shelter

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Advocates for homeless people said the rules amounted to criminalizing someone for having nowhere to live. The city lacks sufficient affordable housing. The one shelter for adults requires attending daily Christian services and other rules. Hundreds of residents are unhoused.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We don't want to be in the parks," said Helen Cruz, a Grants Pass resident who lacks permanent shelter. "We want a place to live."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: City officials said without the Supreme Court's intervention, they would be forced to surrender their public spaces.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Department of Justice had mostly backed the challengers while also arguing that the appeals court ruling was too broad and didn't take into account the circumstances such as whether someone had access to a shelter and refused it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On any given night in the United States, more than 600,000 people are likely to be homeless, according to the federal government. Last year, \(40\%\) of homeless individuals slept under bridges, on sidewalks, in parks, cars, abandoned buildings and other public locations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The case, which is the City of Grants Pass v. Johnson, attracted an unusually large number of briefs filed by outside interests.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Advocates for the homeless hoped that even if the decision didn't go their way, the case would spur elected officials at all levels of government to do more to address homelessness.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Beryl

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hurricane warnings were in effect Sunday for Barbados, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and the Grenadine Islands, Grenada and Tobago. A tropical storm warning was issued on Martinique, a tropical storm watch was in effect for Dominica and Trinidad.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The hurricane center urged anyone living in the central and western Caribbean to monitor the storm's progression given the uncertainty of the forecast.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Wind speeds on the islands could be up to \(30\%\) stronger on the tops and windward sides of hills and mountains, possibly even higher, the center said, adding that "catastrophic" wind damage was possible. St. Vincent and the Grenadines and Grenada were most at risk.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rainfall could cause flooding, and is expected to dump 3 to 6 inches in Barbados and the Windward Islands into Monday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After Beryl's center moves across the Windward Islands early Monday, the storm will cross the southeastern and central Caribbean Sea through Wednesday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Beryl could bring 1 to 4 inches of rain to southeastern Puerto Rico on Monday night and into Tuesday.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Will Hurricane Beryl hit the US?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It's too soon to determine the path and strength of Beryl when the storm gets to the western half of the Caribbean later this week - and whether it could impact the U.S. Gulf Coast. The hurricane center expects Beryl to remain a hurricane as it reaches Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula on Friday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Forecasters warned U.S. residents to

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: stay vigilant. "At this point, the most likely scenario is for the storm to move westward into Mexico; however, it is very important to note that if the high pressure across the Southeast weakens, that can allow the storm to move farther south and reach the Gulf Coast," AccuWeather Lead Hurricane Forecaster Alex DaSilva said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Beryl is the first hurricane of what is expected to be an extraordinary 2024 season. Tropical Storm Alberto, the first named storm of the season, left at least four people dead in Mexico after it made landfall on June 20. Beryl underwent rapid intensification: It was declared a tropical depression and then a tropical storm on Friday, and by Sunday was a major hurricane.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As Beryl continues to strengthen, it's setting a number of records, according to Phil Klotzbach, a senior research scientist at Colorado State University. It's the third earliest Atlantic major hurricane on record, trailing Alma on June 8, 1966, and Audrey on June 27, 1957. Also, Beryl is now the earliest Category 4

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: hurricane on record. The record was held by Hurricane Dennis, which became a Category 4 on July 8, 2005.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: What is the outlook for the 2024 season?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Federal forecasters have predicted a hurricane season unlike any other, with as many as 25 named storms possible.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is the most storms the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has ever predicted in a preseason outlook. "All the ingredients are in place for an active season," National Weather Service director Ken Graham said in May.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: NOAA director Rick Spinrad said the Atlantic hurricane season is shaping up to be "extraordinary"-an  \(85\%\) chance for an above-average year. "The forecast, is the highest NOAA has ever issued for the May outlook," he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Contributing: Doyle Rice and Mike Snyder

layout_dets.text: Safety rules

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Institute in support of the challenge.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The challengers say OSHA may be the most egregious example of an open-ended delegation of authority from Congress to a federal agency.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But they're hoping for a ruling that will apply not just to workplace rules, but in all other areas as well.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The challenger in the OSHA case, Allstates Refractory Contractors, is represented by Don McGahn, who was former President Donald Trump's first White House counsel and played a top role in his Supreme Court nominations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970 has been used by the Labor Department to set safety standards to protect workers from falls, fires, electric shock, being hit by foreign objects, asphyxiation, chemical burns and more.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: A falling catwalk brace injures a worker: The penalty is \(5,967

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In 2019, OSHA issued a penalty against Allstates after a catwalk brace fell and injured a construction worker. Allstates agreed to pay a penalty of \(5,967 but then took OSHA to court, arguing that Congress improperly told the agency it could set safety rules for virtually every business in America.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "If there is any case in which the Court should stand up for the principle that Congress, not agencies, must write major rules affecting the American people, this is it," McGahn told the Supreme Court.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Cincinnati-based 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals disagreed.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Safety law OK'd by Richard Nixon

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A divided panel ruled 2-1 last year that the 1970 law, signed by then President Richard Nixon, gave OSHA sufficient direction and also set limits on its authority.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "So while Congress has conferred significant power to OSHA to oversee large sections of our economy, the discretion conferred by the OSH Act nowhere near approaches the line where the scope of its power is too great for the standard imposed," Circuit Judge Richard Griffin wrote.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Circuit Judge John Nalbandian, who was appointed by Trump, disagreed.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 'Nearly unfettered discretion'?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nalbandian said Congress gave the Labor Department "nearly unfettered discretion."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The challengers contend that if they win, most of OSHA's regulations would not be affected because they are based on other sources of rulemaking authority.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They also emphasize that they're challenging only permanent safety - not health - standards because Cori has placed more limits on health rules.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the Labor Department says several safety standards - those intended to prevent immediate physical harm - would fail, returning the nation to the patchwork of federal and state rules that have been used in the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Since the law was passed, workplace injuries have dropped significantly, according to the department.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Biden administration's lawyers say the challengers want to upend the approach that's been used for nearly a century to decide how much authority Congress can delegate to agencies and adopt a new test "with no identifiable concrete content or parameters."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the American Farm Bureau Federation, which filed a brief with several other business groups in support of the challenge, said Congress must stop delegating its job to the Labor Department and set whatever specific safety standards lawmakers think are necessary.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The decadeslong judicial path towards a watered-down nondelegation test," the groups told the court, "is inconsistent with the exclusive reservation of the legislative power to Congress and with the role of the people as the ultimate source of that legislative power."

layout_dets.text: NEWS

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: USA TODAY MONDAY JULY 1,2024

layout_dets.label: 页码
layout_dets.text: 3A

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Civil rights

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It propelled a movement that was able to make major civil rights gains," said Melanie Campbell, president of the nonpartisan National Coalition on Black Civic Participation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The law outlawed segregation in public places and banned employment discrimination based on race, color, sex, religion, or national origin.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marc Morial, president of the National Urban League, called the law "transformative."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It has not just only changed the arc for Black people. It has changed the arc for women and for other people of color in a profound way," he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: USA TODAY invited nearly a dozen leaders of national organizations to share their take on how far the country has come since the act was signed into law by President Lyndon Johnson on July 2, 1964. They also shared how far they think the U.S. has to go to achieve the full promise of the law.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Extended lives, improved educational success, helped people get better jobs

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Wiley

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Maya Wiley, president and CEO of The Leadership Conference Center, Civil and Human Rights

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Imagine a sweeping set of laws ushered in that extended lives, im-

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: proved educational success for kids, and helped people get better jobs. We'd not only celebrate it - we'd protect it. We have that law today.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 added years, literally about three to four years, onto the life expectancy of Black people when health care had to open its once segregated doors.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: More Black students saw their education improve, while white students continued on the same educational footing. It helped to reduce "intense segregation" schools with \(10\%\) or less white students - of Black students in Southern schools from \(78\%\) in 1978 to \(24\%\) in 1988.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Thanks to employment protections, Black job opportunities, while still far from sufficient, got significantly better, with less of a wage gap and less of an employment gap.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Instead of seeing the tremendous advancement that the law – with lots of legal and community activism – has produced, federal courts and right-wing advocacy groups are attacking the gains we’ve made by using division rather than multiplication.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: We should multiply its use rather than divide people by claiming what is good for people of color is bad for people who are white.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: We are living proof of progress

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Robinson

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Kelley Robinson, president of the Human Rights Campaign

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At moments like these, I can't help but think of my family – the first free Black family in a little town called Musca-

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: tine, Iowa. My great-aunt Bert, our matriarch, passed away recently at the young age of 102, and we went back to a little town to celebrate her homegosing.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There, we told the story of how Great-Aunt Bert sat at the feet of those who had been born into slavery. We told the story of how we made our way from bondage in Mississippi and Louisiana to freedom in Muscatine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That was two generations ago. Now, I am the first queer, Black woman to serve as President of the Human Rights Campaign, the country’s largest LGBTQ+ civil rights organization.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Progress is not simply possible – we are living proof of it. Our ancestors were jailed, beaten, and bled because they knew a better future was worth fighting for. They would be proud to see us standing tall today, but they would remind us that our work is far from over.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Today, bullies want to strip us of our hard-earned freedoms and roll back progress. As we mark 60 years since the Civil Rights Act of 1964, we must honor those who came before us, like Great-Aunt Bert, by recommitting to our fight for freedom and justice - without exception.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Still need to protect the civil liberties of all citizens

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Echohawk

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: John Echohawk, executive director of the Native American Rights Fund

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It has been 60 years since passage of Civil Rights Act, but the struggle for fair treatment re

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: mains.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Native Americans still face the type of discrimination that motivated the passage of the 1964 Civil Rights Act and we still see a failure to uphold our treaty rights under U.S. law.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At the Native American Rights Fund, we have been challenging the unfair treatment that Native Americans have been subjected to for far too long. For example, throughout Indian Country, Native Americans have to overcome unreasonable barriers just to cast a ballot. The most important barrier can be over 50 miles away and there is still no residential mail delivery on many Native American reservations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: States are also passing laws intended to disenfranchise Native Americans, especially after Native Americans exercise political power. We have also seen an uptick in discriminatory practices – last year a hotel instituted a no Native Americans allowed policy, which brought a new law from the Department of Justice under Title II of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. This blatant discrimination occurs too often.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: A conservative perspective: We've gone too far

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Roberts

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Kevin Roberts, president of The Heritage Foundation and Heritage Action for America

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Civil Rights Act was an extraordinary accomplishment. For the first time, a colorblind so

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ciety was codified into law.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But today, the Civil Rights Act is in bad shape. College campuses discriminate against certain racial groups in the admissions process in clear violation of the law. Mandatory Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion courses force workers to treat their co-workers differently based on race or ethnicity. The federal programs have been restricted to minority applicants and religious employers have been hit with penalties.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The law is a teacher, and for decades, Americans learned the lesson of the Civil Rights Act: every American deserves equal treatment and respect. But in recent years, many have forgotten that lesson, replacing equality under the law with equity of outcomes. Moving forward, our leaders must reverse the trend and commemorate this anniversary by abandoning discriminatory policies.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Our 'abiding commitment to freedom' is being undermined

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Morial

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Marc Morial, president and CEO of the National Urban League

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964, he said it represented "a more abiding com-

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: mitment to freedom, a constant pursuit of justice, and a deeper respect for human dignity.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A century after the Emancipation Proclamation, the Civil Rights Act ushered in a transformative era of open doors and unprecedented access.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the backlash triggered by the racial justice uprising of 2020 presents the gravest threat to the Civil Rights Act in its 60-year history.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Our "abiding commitment to freedom is undermined by discriminatory voting laws and gerrymandering.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Our "pursuit of justice" is derailed by persistent racism in policing and sentencing and the dismantling of diversity and inclusion policies.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Our "respect for human dignity" is betrayed by an unraveling social safety net and economic policies that uplift the health at the expense of working families.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: My predecessor, Whitney M. Young, was instrumental in the passage of the Civil Rights Act. He advanced diversity, equity, and inclusion policies, developing a "Domestic Marshall Plan" that has been incorporated into his Great Society program.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The National Urban League remains committed to his legacy, working to uproot the racial divisions embedded in the nation's institutions and realize the promise of 1964.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Souls lost to exploitation, racism

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Garcia

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Domingo Garcia, president of the League of United Latin American Citizens

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In the early 1900s, Mexican and Native American villages were burned by rangers in the

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: South in the name of "expansion." We've seen the tears and heartbreak of those who have lost loved ones to senseless violence like the victims of the Uvalde school shooting or the physical abuse that was experienced by people of color at the hands of individuals with no respect for human life.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Souls lost to exploitation and racism.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The League of United Latin American Citizens, founded in 1929, is the oldest Latino civil rights grassroots organization in the U.S. Throughout our history, we have significantly influenced legislative and federal legislation, military issues and gun safety.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On the 60th anniversary of the Civil Rights Act, we are reminded the work is ongoing. As we see an unidentified sea of individuals crossing the border from all over the world, we continue to urge government leaders for immigration reform for those who left their countries of origin and who have no rights there – and now here. It is our mission to contribute to the American fabric and we remain committed to the American dream.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the question remains where do we go from here? In 60 years, some things have changed and others remain the same. It is vital that Latinos and our allies come together. As the saying goes "—El puebloonio jamas sera vencido" (The people united will never be defeated).

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Every generation makes progress

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Yang

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: John C. Yang, president and executive director of Asian Americans Advancing Justice

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: To commemorate the anniversary of the 1964 Civil Rights Act is an honor- we do not take lightly

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: at Asian Americans Advancing Justice.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In the early 1960s, Asian Americans were only \(0.5\%\) of the population. Our community benefited from the Black Civil Rights Movement successes of the 1950s and 60s. The solidarity shown by Black civil rights leaders for Asian Americans demonstrated the success of intersectional/collective activism in civil rights movements. Even as Asian Americans have grown to represent \(7\%\) of the population, the 1964 Civil Rights Act serves as a reminder of progress made and the distance we have yet to travel to achieve true equity.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Every generation makes progress toward the goal of true equity in this country, but none of us will realize the full impact of laws like the Civil Rights Act until and unless we work collectively with the Black community to stop the rollback of our rights and realize the dream of a fair and equitable society for all.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: We still have a very long way to go.

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Campbell

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Melanie L. Campbell, president and CEO of the National Coalition on Black Civic Participation

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When the Civil Rights Act of 1964 was signed into law, it was described

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. as the "Second Emancipation."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Act banned segregation, barred discrimination by employers and labor unions, gave way to the formation of the EEOC; and paved the way for passage of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and Fair Housing Act of 1968.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Unfortunately, there are forces currently working tirelessly to reverse the rights and freedoms established by The Act.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Last year, there was a "reverse discrimination" ruling by the Supreme Court, Students for Fair Admissions vs. Harvard, restricting affirmative action efforts by public colleges/universities. This unjust ruling restricts the historic affirmative action efforts that have provided disadvantaged black and brown students the opportunity to attend the nation's elite schools. Further, these same forces are using this case as an excuse to attack Diversity, Equity and Inclusion programs in the public and private sector.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: These and other constant attacks on our voting rights and the rights of women to control our own bodies on a state level, requires those who believe in freedom, justice, equity, and equality for all to fight back at the ballot box and vote in record numbers in 2024 and beyond.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Channel discontent

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Barber

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Rev. William Barber, president of Repairers of the Breach and co-chair of the Poor People's Campaign

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In popular memory, the Civil Rights Act of 1964 was the legislative

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: response to the demands of the March on Washington.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: While it is true that the legislation would never have been won without that mass mobilization, the original demands of that march for "Jobs and Freedom" included an increase in the minimum wage for all Americans and the voting rights protections that would only be enshrined in the Voting Rights Act after the brutality of Bloody Sunday and the courageous Selma to Montgo

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: mery March of 1965.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sixty years later, we must be honest: the federal minimum wage, indexed for inflation, is lower than it was in 1964. What's more, because the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act in its 2013 Shelby decision and Congress has decided to do so. But if it, we have less voting rights protections today than we did on August 6, 1965.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The celebration of historic wins alongside this egregious decay is a source of discontent among everyday Americans. But we have no time for despair.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: We are determined to channel discontent for a resurrection rather than an insurrection.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: All created in the image of God

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Pesner

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rabbi Jonah Pesner, director of the Religious Action Center of Reform Judaism

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In our Jewish tradition, equality is based on the concept that all of God's children are "creat

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ed in the image of God" (Genesis 1:27).

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This precept has led the Jewish community to respond powerfully in the fight against racial segregation and discrimination: the Civil Rights Act of 1964 was drafted in large part in our building in Washington, D.C.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: However, racism, like antisemitism, has never been fully eradicated from our society; those who seek power weaponize it for their own nefarious purposes. We see it today in the forces of division that aim to restrict the freedom to vote by targeting communities of Color and other marginalized groups.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This blatant discrimination fuels the Reform Jewish Movement's nonpartisan Every Voice, Every Vote Campaign to strengthen our democracy by encouraging and protecting voter participation.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Our work ties together our Jewish values with our commitment to protecting all minorities, including the many in our Jewish communities who have been targeted due to their intersectional identities as Jews of Color, people with disabilities, or members of the LGBTQ+ community.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: It is all of our responsibility

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Ellis

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sarah Kate Ellis, president and CEO of GLAAD

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: I'm moved by how much progress we've made toward acceptance and equality as a society while still being remind-

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: ed of how deeply racism and violence against communities of color persists, and how much work there is left to do.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Change is often born from the pain and outrage of individuals courageous enough to imagine and fight for a more just world. It's impossible to talk about the quest for LGBTQ equality without first acknowledging the significant strides made within the civil rights movement and the historic interconnectedness between Black and LGBTQ communities.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The revolutionary Stonewall Uprising of 1969 was spearheaded by LGBTQ people of color. Progress for the acceptance and equality of LGBTQ people over the past 5 years would not be possible without a law that paved by civil rights leaders before us.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is all of our responsibility to speak out against racism and systemic injustice and to continue elevating voices and amplifying stories of people of color, especially those who are Black, queer, and transgender.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: We must take an active role in protecting its legacy

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Johnson

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Derrick Johnson, president of the NAAACP

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It’s important that we understand the journey that lies ahead of us.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: While the law was a first step, it was not until the amended legislation

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: passed in 1965 that we truly began to make significant strides toward equality and justice. It's also important to understand that the culture of racism is deeply embedded in the country's foundation. That's why, as systemic racism has become a social norm, the promises of the legislation have yet to be fulfilled for all Black Americans.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: While Black Americans continue to fall victim to a system that has, at many times, posed insurmountable barriers to progress, we also face mounting threats to the right to effect change.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As of today, more than 40 states have enacted anti-protest laws. And almost half of the country will face new restrictions to the ballot box in November.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Will we push forward or revert to a time where the color of our skin is used as justification for the degradation of fundamental freedoms?

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: 4A MONDAY JULY 1, 2024 USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: NEWS

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Refugees in NY mourn teens shot and killed by police

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Utica Police Chief Mark Williams and Mayor of Utica Michael Galime address the crowd inside City Hall in Utica, NY on Saturday.

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: DANIEL DELOACH/USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Casey Pritchard  
Utica Observer Dispatch  
USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: UTICA, N.Y. – The screams of a grieving mother could be heard through a city hall at a news conference in upstate New York Saturday morning, as officials detailed the shooting death of a 13-year-old member of the Karen community by an officer on Friday night.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: What started as rumblings turned into screams from all sides as Utica Mayor Michael Galime, through the help of an Interpreter, spoke to the mother and family of Nyah Mway, 13, who is a native of the community which originates in Myanmar.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Utica, a Rust Belt city in New York's Mohawk Valley, has become home to a burgeoning refugee population from around the world, including thousands of undocumented and ethnic minority displaced from Myanmar amid military junta and civil war.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Saturday's news conference was meant for reporters but was opened to the general public due to the sheer number of people, according to the mayor.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We called this press conference not to just explain and be completely transparent, but to offer our condolences to the family and the community for their loss," Galime said. "Yesterday evening, while a stop like the one that occurred is routine, it became tragic in near moments. We understand and we're here to be completely transparent and explain everything about the incident to the community and the process moving forward."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Timeline of events

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Police Chief Mark Williams then attempted to provide a timeline of events.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Williams said Utica police officers were conducting a pedestrian stop of two juveniles around 10:38 p.m. on Friday on a tree-lined residential street.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One of the juveniles, a young man, fled from police. Williams said that during the chase that ensued, the young man was played "what appeared to be a handgun."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: During the news conference, the moment these words were uttered by the police chief, some of the people – more than 100 packed into city hall – started screaming. Anger rose from the crowd with shouts of "No!" and attempts by some to calm the crowd down.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continuing, Williams said the officer discharged his firearm once and struck the teen "during a ground struggle." The 13-year-old was taken to Wynn Hospital where he died from his wounds.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Officers then recovered a replica Glock 17 handgun with a detachable magazine, but it was ultimately determined to be a pellet gun," Williams said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We will be releasing the names of the officers involved in the very near future. We ask for patience as this investigation continues."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yells of indignation came from the crowd after they learned the three officers involved in the incident had been placed on paid administrative during the investigation. One person commented aloud that the police were getting "... a paid vacation."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Galime told the crowd he was dedicated to being as transparent as possible and that directly after the press conference, he would invite the family and representatives of the community to speak with city officials.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Family present

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After this was translated, the mother of the 13-year-old began yelling and screaming. A member of the community translated: "She said she doesn't want to be in the same room as killers."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The mother's walls could be heard for a moment before the whole crowd drowned out the government officials.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Walking toward the crowd, Galime stood before the mother and spoke with her for a brief time as the whole crowd yelled for justice.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The public news conference was closed early and relocated to a private room upstairs, where officials answered questions about the next steps.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: State attorney investigation

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In officer-involved shootings, New York State Executive Law 70b mandates that the New York State Attorney General may be held responsible for taking the lead criminal investigative role.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Utica Police Department is conducting a parallel internal investigation with its Professional Standards Unit to determine the reasons for the incidents, procedures and training guidelines.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Over the next several days, police said they would publicly release more details about the incident and a comprehensive overview of the events. Po

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: lice also plan to release the full body cam footage from the officers involved.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Further questions

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: After the public news conference, the mayor, police chief and department spokesman Lt. Michael Curran were invited to state press conference for the media.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Our police department deals with investigations day in and day out and they don't end like this," Galime said. "They do not end like this. This situation unfolded due to the events very specific to this situation. And that is why we have to only speak to what we are saying, release and when it's released... And we're not going to offer information we're not absolutely sure of."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As it stands, Williams said the two juveniles were stopped as part of an ongoing investigation but declined to answer questions about the subject of the investigation until it was concluded.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When asked about lethal force being used, Williams said at the time, there was no way to know that the forces were actually effective until the officers got their hands on it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "You don't bring a Taser to a gunfight. When you, at the time, perceive deadly physical force, you have to match it," Williams said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Social media video

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The police department said it is aware of a video of the incident that was taken from a building in the town.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Officials said the video does not portray the incident in its entirety.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Galime said updates will be released as they become available. Investigations like this can take a long time, according to Williams.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Until then, Galime made it clear where the city stands.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "This office and our police department will operate with utmost efficiency and transparency," Galine said. "Following the closure of the press conference, myself and the translator had a conversation with the mother and her surrounding friends and family. She is not just distraught, she is grieving in the way that was (shown) downstairs. And it's not only acceptable, it's expected. "What we need to do from this side is make sure that... moving forward, we'll continue to be as objective as possible and every single incident that involves an investigation is met with objectivity and the letter of the law."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Contributing: Eduardo Cuevas, USA TODAY.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: The lessons of 'Access Hollywood'

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Biden may be applying a lesson to the US, but he stays in the race for the White House.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A month before the 2016 election, the Washington Post revealed a recording of Trump from 2005 bragging that he could grab women's genitals without consequences because "when you're a star, they let you do it."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There were consequences then, with some leading Republicans calling their nominee unfit for the presidency. But Trump bulldozed through their objections, dismissing or ignoring his critics. The former president was busy and solidified his hold on the GOP.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: About four years later, after the assault on the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, by rioters trying to overturn Trump's defeat in the 2020 election, Congress impeached him, though the Senate didn't seem to be able to win. But the firestorm that would have sabotaged most political careers in time didn't notably erode his political base.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Little surprise then that Trump's conviction on 34 criminal counts in a New York courtroom in May didn't unnerve his supporters. He has made his status as the first felon to run for presidency, but he is not a fundraising boon and a rallying cry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Trump has demonstrated the power of plowing ahead, regardless of what the party elites and the newspaper editorial writers may say.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Chaos at the convention: Not a political asset

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Biden has insisted that he will continue his campaign.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "When you get knocked down, you get back up," he declared to cheers at a rally in Raleigh, North Carolina, the day after the debate.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But holding the nomination is easier than winning the election.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Previous presidents have faced primary challenges in their bids for second terms, including Democrat Jimmy Carter in 1980 and Republican George H.W. Bush in 1992. After messy conventions that underscored party divisions, both won the nominations but lost the elections.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This year, Biden had no serious primary challenger in a party united by its opposition to Trump. That means almost all of the 4,672 delegates expected to win the election in Chicago are pledged to him, although that commitment is not a binding one.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It also means there is no ready alteration of normalising the possibility of a brutal floor fight.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Vice President Kamala Harris would be a leading alternative, although her position as Biden's running mate gives her no special standing to claim the nomination. There are also rising Democrats who might have run for the nomination this time if Biden hadn't, among whom John Jebeter, Whitney of Michigan, Gavin Newsom of California, Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania and J.D. Pritzker of Illinois.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: None of those governors are well known nationally, though, nor have they gone through the rigors and the scrutiny of a presidential campaign.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In a sign of how seriously the Biden campaign is taking the threat, deputy

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: campaign manager Rob Flaherty blasted out a memo Saturday arguing that changing the top of the ticket would nominate "candidates who are willing to commit to politics, be less likely to win than Joe Biden to defeat Donald Trump."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: However, the findings he attached didn't prove that point. In a survey by a progressive think tank called Data For Progress, there was no meaning- and data -difference between how Biden and eight potential alternatives fared against Trump.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Biden trailed Trump by 3 percentage points, 45% to 48%. Six of the other candidates tested also trailed Trump by 3 points, including Harris 45% -48%, Newson 44% -47%,Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg 44%-47%, Pritzker 43% -46%,Shapiro 43%-46% and Minnesota Sen. Amy Klobuchar 43% -46%.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Two of the candidates trailed Trump by only 2 points, 44% -46%-Whitmer and New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Flaherty also warned that Biden withdrawing would create problems.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It "would lead to weeks of chaos, internal food fighting, and a bunch of candidates who limp into a brutal floor fight at the convention, all while Donald Trump has time to speak to American voters uncontested," he said. He called it "a highway to losing."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It is true that chaos at conventions has never been a political asset. Witness a previous Democratic convention in Chicago in 1968 when protests against the Vietnam War created complaints for V.P. President Hubert Humphrey, the nominee.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He lost in November.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Gathering of 10,000 hippies shut down before it starts

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Max Hauptman  
USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A longtime counterculture festival now in its fifth decade and set to be held over the July Fourth holiday is being shut down, with U.S. Forest Service officials citing a lack of appropriate permitting and concerns over environmental impact.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Rainbow Family of Living Light gathering was set to be held the first week of July in California's Plumas National Forest. On June 25, however, the U.S. Forest Service officials issued an order asking people to leave the area, and those who refuse to go facing lines of up to \(5,000 or a six-month jail sentence.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The Forest is concerned about the 500-plus individuals already dispersed camping in a concentrated area. We are always willing to work with any organization or group interested in recreating on the national forest. There are existing and projected impacts on natural and cultural resources and other authorized uses. Our priority is maintaining public health and safety and the appropriate stewardship of public lands and natural resources," Plumas National Forest Supervisor Chris Carlton said in a statement on Wednesday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: While the current retro wave may be more focused on the 1990s and 2000s, the Rainbow Family gathering is a self-contained event. The event took place once a year in the first week of July.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Rainbow Family roots go back more than 50 years

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: First started in Colorado in 1972, the Rainbow Family gathering was founded in part by military veterans struggling with alcoholism, drug dependence and post-traumatic stress disorder; camping out on public land in an environment like Burning Man or a Grateful Dead concert is a central part of the expedition. The majority of people there is unknown and varies over a year, but the U.S. Forest Service this year estimated that the event could draw as many as 10,000 visitors.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This year, the U.S. Forest Service has described the gathering as having an "unauthorized noncommercial group use incident," that "can have significant impacts on traffic, communities, local resources, residents, and visitors."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That particular brand of lawlessness has often brought the gathering into conflict with local law enforcement over gun use, sanitation and damage to forests.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As USA TODAY has previously reported, many attendees will work to minimize their impact on the environment, but as with any gathering of this size previous iterations have involved incidents and arrests.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Every year, the Plumas National Forest sees a large surge in visitors in late June and early July, enjoying not only summer recreation in the forest, but also numerous events in our communities around the July Fourth holiday, said Plumas National Forest Supervisor Chris Carlton in a press release earlier this week. "We understand the addition of the Rainbow Family Gathering on the Plumas National Forest raises concerns about additional impacts to our local communities, natural resources and environment and we will be working with the incident team to minimize adverse effects as much as possible."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On Wednesday, Lassen County Supervisor Jason Ingram praised the U.S. Forest Service's decision on social media, writing on Facebook that, "my concerns with this gathering were always the illegality aspect, the increased fire risk this would have created, the environmental impact, and the blatant disrespect shown to our local tribes. Events are fine, but not events that blatantly disregard the law and endanger our land and community fire safety."

layout_dets.label: 段落

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: We went searching for hope.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In Hope.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: From Maine to Alaska, we reported from towns named Hope about the state of a nation that to all appearances is divided, angry and fearful about its future amid a ferocious election year. We found challenges everywhere, from the economic to the existential.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: By more than 2-1, Americans tell the USA TODAY/Suffolk University Poll that the country is headed in the wrong direction. Only half of likely voters, \(49\%\) are casting a ballot based mostly on what they hope their candidate would do if elected. Almost as many, \(41\%\) say their vote is based on what they fear the other candidate would do, given the chance.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A sense of alarm seems to be the sentiment that most unities us: the Anxious States of Ameri

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yet in fundamental ways, Americans continue to express an abiding faith in the nation's resilience and a buoyant optimism about what's ahead. By a margin of more than 6 to \(1 - 81\%\) to \(13\%\) - Americans say they have "hope for the future of the country," a view that stretches across lines of gender, race and political party.

layout_dets.text: HOPE, Maine - Wild blueberries have long blanketed the hills and valleys of this quiet hamlet 15 miles from New England's rocky shores.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They grew here before Native people roamed the lands, and before Sonia Howard's family decided to put down roots in the grassy, windswept territory nine generations ago.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Every summer since she can remember, Howard's relatives have flocked back, as the long sunny days begin to wane and the first breaths of autumn appear, to harvest the scattered blue clumps that emerge from these prickly bushes on the 800 acres of farmland the family owns.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The blueberries that grow here at the Brodis Blueberries farm aren't like the kind you usually find in the produce aisle at the grocery store. Nobody planted these. Instead, farmers have removed barriers - trees, rocks and weeds - to allow for the crops to naturally flourish.

layout_dets.text: What gives us hope? Tied at the top of list is "the American spirit," a gauzy concept, and the 237-year-old U.S. Constitution, a concrete document.

"The more people can't even talk to each other,and our friends are being not friends any more, and horrble social media posts and texts , the worse the country is going."

layout_dets.text: Official population: 113. Fact check? Likely overstated

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In Hope, Alaska, climate change and the warming coastal waters it has brought are threatening salmon fishing grounds. On the other side of the continent, Hope, Maine, sees strains between longtime residents and the newcomers who began arriving in greater numbers during the pandemic. Michigan's two Hope Townships are in the middle of a swing state barred with severe droughts that have fractured some families. Hope, New Mexico, barely stays on the map with an official population of I13 - a figure locals say is likely an overstatement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We're more or less a family here," said Bill Fletcher, the town's 85-year-old mayor. "None of us is kin, but we're a family anyway. You scratch one of us, we all bleed."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Then there's Hope, Arkansas, revisiting its downtown but struggling to reverse a population decline and low rates of voter engagement. It had a flash of fame when native son Bill Clinton won the White House after highlighting his hometown heritage in a "place called Hope," though to be fair he also attacked opponent George H.W. Bush during the campaign.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That convention video was in 1992, more than three decades ago. In 2008, Barack Obama's winning campaign slogan promised "hope and change," although he ran negative ads against John McCain as well. Obama's iconic campaign poster displayed that single word: "HOPE."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That has not been the dominant message of this year's campaign. Republican nominee Donald Trump predicts that  if he loses,a crushing depression and new world war could follow. Violent

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Clouds pass by the water tower in Hope, Ark., hometown of former President Bill Clinton, with a population of just over 8,000 people. The town is revitalizing its downtown but struggling to reverse a population decline. JASPER COLT/USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: crime and uncontrolled illegal immigration would threaten citizens' safety and the country's survival.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The only thing standing behind you and obliteration is me," the former president has declared.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Democratic nominee Kamala Harris has adopted more politics-of-joy language than President Joe Biden was using before he stepped back from his reelection race and his vice president stepped up. He had warned that Trump's election would endanger democracy itself. Harris' tone toward the former president tends to be more mocking than apocalyptic.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nonetheless, she calls Trump a would-be despot who, if he wins, would dismantle reproductive and other freedoms.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Harris voters are a tick more likely to be motivated by fear of Trump than by hope about her, \(47\% - 45\%\). (Fear was a much bigger factor for Biden supporters. In a USA TODAY survey in June, just \(27\%\) of those backing Biden were motivated mostly by hope for him; \(66\%\) cited their fear of Trump.)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In the August poll, one-third of Trump supporters, 33%, were motivated by fear of Harris, 58% by hope about him.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The intensity of those feelings - including the disbelief that anyone could possibly support the other side - can make it hard to reach common ground, or even recognize when it's there.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I'm terrified and sickened at the thought of what's going to happen if the other candidate wins," said Melissa Bennett, 54, an office manager from Pasco, Washington, who was polled. A Republican, she is supporting Trump. "My biggest fear... comes down to the security of our country (with) her as our commander in chief."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Shandee Gordon, 45, principal of an elementary school in Morrillon, Arkansas, is an independent who supports Harris.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I'm hopeful that she's going to do the things that she says she's going to do," she said. "With him, he's just a horrible, horrible person that does bad things. He's a criminal. I just don't understand why anybody's voting for him. I don't get it. I just don't get it."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Inspirational Obama for Democrats, Reagan for the GOP

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Considering the past few years, Americans aren't being irrational when they worry about the future.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The worst pandemic in a century, claiming more than 1 million lives in the United States. The most violent attempt to overturn a presidential election in history, an assault on the U.S. Capitol as Electoral College votes were being certified. The most serious invasion in Europe since World War II, with the conflict between Russia and Ukraine still raging.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Events in the world matter in that they kind of prime people to be anxious about certain things," said Shana Kushner Gadarian, a political scientist at Syracuse University and co-author of "Anxious Politics: Democratic Citizenship in a Threatening World."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "But politicians come in and through their ads and through talking to people and their speeches, they really hammer on particular issues," she said, "because they believe, or they have a sense from polling data, that it benefits their party for people to be anxious about those things."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Fear can be a powerful force in politics, she said, though research indicates hope is a stronger motivator in actually winning people's votes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The American presidents considered the greatest in our history struck themes of hope in times more desperate than these. Abraham Lincoln in his first inaugural address called for Americans to tap "the better angels of our nature"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: as the Civil War loomed. During the depths of the Great Depression, Franklin D. Roosevelt in his first inaugural address counseled the country, "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nearly 9 of 10 Americans say there has been a president during their lifetime who inspired them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On this, there are clear answers and a sharp partisan divide. Nearly half of Republicans, 48%, cite Ronald Reagan, compared with just 3% of Democrats. In the GOP, Trump ranks second, at 18%.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: More than half of Democrats, 56%, cite Barack Obama, compared with just 4% of Republicans. Among Democrats, John F. Kennedy is second, at 17%. (Since JFK was assassinated in 1963, those who were around during his lifetime would be 60 or older today.)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The earlier poll of 1,000 registered voters by landline and cellphone June 28-30 has a 3.1-point margin of error.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In their own lives, Americans tell us that their family, their faith and their friends give them hope. For the country, after the "American spirit" and the Constitution, they cite young people as a source of strength. For the forces feeding hopelessness, beyond the state of today's politics, they name world affairs.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Candidates and their campaigns can affect how hopeful, and hopeless, Americans feel.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In the poll, taken just before the Fourth of July, when Biden was the presumptive Democratic nominee, \(84\%\) of Democrats were hopeful about the future - a percentage that jumped nine points, to \(93\%\), when the same question was asked two months later, after Harris had become the nominee.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The reverse happened for Republicans. In late June, \(82\%\) were hopeful about the future, a percentage that sank by double digits, to \(72\%\), in late August. During that time, Trump survived an assassination attempt. What's more, the conventional wisdom became that he has a more difficult election ahead with Harris as his opponent than he did with Biden.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Well, I think the country has problems; I think the world has problems," says Jane Crosson, 67, a retired pediatric cardiologist from Durham, North Carolina. A Democrat, she supports Harris. "But I don't think the problems are insurmountable. I think that there's a lot of good things happening, and we can move forward if we can just get past this craziness."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hope has an unmistakable appeal, says Jeannine Jabaay, 47. That is, Hope, Alaska, which is just about the end of the road of the continental United States. Her family owns and manages the Dirty Skillet Restaurant and the Bear Creek Lodge Cabins there.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Hope has a weird way of drawing you in," she says. "Nobody ends up in Hope by accident. It has to be intentional."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Contributing: Trevor Hughes and Lauren Villagran
