layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Maine

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text:
A customer enters the Hope General Store run by Damon McClure and his wife, Simone-Claire Girard Delevett.
"You can feel like you've sort of gone back in time when you come in here," McClure said. PHOTOS BY JASPER COLT/USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Ron Howard harvests wild blueberries in July using a modified lawnmower at Brodis Blueberries in Hope, Maine, a town of just over 1,600 people.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: their yield to commercial growers, such as Wyman's, which freezes and ships them across the country.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But for those who have lent their labor and sweat to the land, the difference in the taste is clear.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Ron Howard, who married into Sonja Brodis' family 48 years ago and now manages the business, said the more popular high-bush blueberries "just don't have the same flavor and texture and sweetness" as the wild ones.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It's a comparison those in Hope would also find apt to describe their neighbors. Much like the wild berries, the town has been cared for by generations who have sought to preserve a quieter way of life that is increasingly hard to find elsewhere.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Many of the town's 1,500 residents are farmers, artisans and businesspeople working in trades forgotten by time—shoe cobbling, metal fabricating, fire truck restoration and bagpipe making, to name a few.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Brad Ellsworth, a longtime Hope resident who restores wooden boats, lovingly described his neighbors as

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "unique, eccentric people."

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Ellsworth

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This community in midcoast Maine is one of 19 towns of the same name across the country, six of which USA TODAY visited this summer.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In our visits to these

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: places called Hope, from Michigan to Arkansas, Maine to Alaska, we looked for signs of optimism and what was getting in people’s way. Here’s what we found just inland of the bustling Maine tourist havens of Camden and Rockport, in one of the country’s oldest states.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: The center of town

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At the heart of Hope is one of the oldest, if not the oldest, general store in

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Maine. Today, Damon McClure and his wife, Simone-Claire Girard Delevert, are its stewards.

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: McClure

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Like many of the people in Hope, the couple are "from away" – jargon locals use to delineate out-of-towners.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As a child, McClure's family traveled from Virginia every summer to visit Deer Isle, an island just south of Acadia National Park. But he didn't move to the area until 2019. He had recently lost his job and was looking for a new challenge when a buddy told him about Hope Genesee, McClure, Delevett and their daughter, who was going into her senior year in high school, visited and quickly grew attached.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “You can feel the age. You can feel like you've sort of gone back in time when you come in here,” McClure told USA TODAY. “That's what we fell in love with.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: One of the biggest challenges they faced when they first arrived in February 2019 was quieting fears among town residents that they were going to change the beloved landmark and "mess it up."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When the COVID-19 pandemic hit a year later, the general store, which typically acts as a convenience stop for locals to pick up coffee or the odd forgotten grocery item, became an even more essential part of town.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: For much of the crisis, McClure ran the store alone because his staff was wary of the health risks.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The pandemic was one of the only times McClure said he has seen politics bubble up in the more than four years he has lived in Hope. The store required customers to wear masks before face coverings were mandated by the state. Most regulars were understanding, but some pushed back, and McClure had to turn away people who refused to follow the rule.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Overall, though, he said the store's response to the pandemic helped him earn the trust of the community more quickly.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We made it feel as friendly and as safe as we could," McClure said. "We gained a lot of goodwill during that time."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Today, McClure jokes that he knows more about what's going on in Hope than anyone else, and he takes pride in the store's role as the hub of the community. He stocks four-packs of Lion Stout from Sri Lanka for a regular who buys it three or four times a week, and he always has various flavors of Larabars on hand for one woman who loves them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The general store also hosts "pub nights" twice a week in the back corner known as "the nook." Rain, shine or snow, locals pile into built-in pine wooden benches and colorful metal chairs to sip on pints and shoot the breeze. The one rule: no talking politics, or religion.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The most important thing about owning a store like this is just responding to what the community needs,"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: McClure said. "That's really the reason we're here."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Changing with the times

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Like much of the country, residents of Hope are still contending with changes since the pandemic. In many parts of the crisis brought the community together.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When Brodis Blueberries found that it was no longer able to operate out of the family's farm house for social distancing reasons, for instance, the town rapidly approved a permit to allow them to build a new structure. The same year, the city had moved several towns away caught fire, Hope allowed him to operate out of the farm.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "They knew that this was kind of critically important for us," Ron Howard said. "They said, 'Hey, these are local folks, and let's get this approval done.' And they approved it. That doesn't happen everywhere... It does give us hope."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But the pandemic also ushered in new dynamics. Every home in the town now has access to high-speed fiber optic internet. Locals say the change has encouraged more people in search of solitude to migrate from large metropolitan areas like Boston, New York and even as far as Texas to this sleepy Maine town.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Camden Road, one of the main thoroughfares in Hope, where the general store and other small businesses sit, used to see only a few cars pass in the morning and afternoon. Now, cars drive by at a slow but steady clip throughout the day.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Longtime residents are quick to say they don't mind new arrivals; they just worry the newcomers will rapidly change the community's way of life.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: “People move from other places, because they like it, but then they get here and they find that there are things that they liked from where they came,” said Stephanie Powers, a lifelong resident of Hope who works at Pine Ridge Carpentry, two doors down from the general store. “They want to try to sort of impose more bigger town ideas or processes.”

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A few of those ideas have been about creating new town public works and police departments, both of which Powers says are unnecessary in a community with fewer than 2,000 people. A registered independent, she said the drive to create a "public service" about "keeping everything exactly the same, just the spirit of it and the intent."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: It's a desire shared by many in town, across age, demographics and political parties.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On a cloudy afternoon, while he waited for a technician to repair his refrigerator, Creighton Drury, 75, sat in a lawn chair outside his home and explained

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: that the piece of the town's culture he most wants to safeguard is its integrity. Drury moved to Hope 15 or so years ago. He has lived in the pre-Civil War home he restored with his wife ever since.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I always was raised by the saying 'If you make a commitment, stick to it.' And it seems like that is kind of a dying concept," said Drury, a proud Democrat who displayed a 2020 Biden-Harris sign in the back of his garage.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He added, "I love this neighborhood, because if you ever had a problem, your neighbors would be there to help you."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: All politics is local

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Politically, Hope's population mirrors the rest of Maine. There are roughly 500 Democrats, 400 Republicans and more than 350 voters unaffiliated with a party. That's to say: the town is divided.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Most people avoid talking about national politics. More often, conversations revolve around local issues.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Emily Davis, who has owned Hope Orchards with her husband, Brein, for more than two decades, said the rule of thumb is that you bring up politics with people you know agree with you.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "There's a hesitation for most of us to even initiate conversation," Davis said at a potluck of 10 people hosted in the orchards.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The main divide in town falls more along geographical lines between Hope and South Hope. Hope tends to be more conservative, and South Hope is more conservative.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The former of the two sits closer to the coast and features many of the main attractions in town, including the general store, the town offices and Hope Orchards. South Hope is a five-minute drive away on winding mountain roads, with meadows on either side and small strips of houses every few miles.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Susan Pushaw, 66, co-owns Pushaw's Trading Post, the central store in South Hope. She remembers a time when the neighborhood considered seceding from Hope. People in the southern part of town didn't want to make the trek to the area near the general store for town meetings, she said. They later did

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: away with the initiative because of the legal complexities.

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Pushaw

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But today, the two areas might as well be separate towns.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Pushaw has never visited Hope General Store, despite the similarity of

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: the businesses and their proximity. She grew up in South Hope next to her store and bought it with her brother Jerry after she retired from a food processing plant.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: To Pushaw, Hope resembles Camden.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: the wealthier coastal town it borders.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Where Hope General Store sells sandwiches with brie cheese, apples and hummus and names like "the Tree Hugger," the South Hope trading post mostly dabbles in greasier comfort food items like spicy chicken burgers, fried chicken, and steak and cheese sandwiches.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Pushaw, a Republican, doesn't like getting involved with politics. There's an "8 o'clock crew" that will come into the store and occasionally get into spots about national and local issues, but just like in other parts of Hope, the main priority is getting along.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Every town has its politics," Pushaw said. "They start out with little arguments, but it all ends up good before they all leave."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Restoring and preserving hope

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Andy Swift's studio — a massive, three-story chicken coop — sits at the top of Hatchet Mountain Road, in between Hope and South Hope. His artform is restoring antique fire engines.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rusting ladder trucks and engine parts lay in the tall grass outside of his shop. On top of an old car at the entrance, an object designed to look like a missile reads "Jazz not War."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This is the place Swift, 71, goes when his frustrations at the daily news cycle hit a tipping point. Fire engines are "almost primeval in that people understand that they're here to help," said Smith, who was a firefighter in Alaska for years, before moving back to his home state of Maine.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Mechanically speaking, a fire engine is bringing the hope," he said. "There's a fire, and you hear that bell, you hear that siren, and you know the fire department is responding to the enemy that's out of control."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Although the Bernie Sanders sticker on Swift's car hints at his political beliefs, he declined to talk about his affiliation, instead saying fire engines are a reminder that the purest forms of hope don't have a political party.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sitting beneath flickering fluorescent lights in his shop - tools, engine parts and photographs littering the counters behind him - Swift recounted work he did for the New York City Fire Department after 9/11.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Feeling helpless and needing a place to put his energy, Swift offered to restore a piece of the NYFD's choosing. In December, a group of fire commissioners from the city arrived in Hope to deliver the hose wagon they wanted him to fix.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "This is very shortly after 9/11, and everybody's heart has just been tenderized," Swift says, with tears brimming. "One of the fire commissioners, Tom Fitzpatrick, looked around and he said, 'It's, it's being done in a town called Hope."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "So it is kind of cool to be in a town called Hope," Swift added, his voice cracking.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: When asked what brought them hope, over and over again, the people in Hope, Maine, pointed to the people around them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We need connection," said Kyle Rittenburg, who with his wife, Anna, helps the Davises run Hope Orchards. He and Anna had organized the potluck for participants in their community sustained-agriculture program, who subscribe to receive produce directly from the farm every week. They're hoping to use the orchards to help people "get connected with the food and hence the land."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Davises are all for the mission and take pride it's happening in Hope.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Having the name 'Hope' sort of inspires us to be hopeful and to live hopefully," Emily Davis said. "Live in hope, die in hope."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Springfield, Ohio's Haitian residents share their fears

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Erin Glynn  
USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Haitian immigrants in Springfield, Ohio, spoke out Saturday about the danger they feel in their community as the city remains at the center of the national debate on immigration.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Haitian Times and the Haitian Community Help and Support Center organized a conversation with activists, journalists and Haitian residents to respond to claims spread online. Some of the posts were shared by Republican vice presidential candidate JD Vance. The post was also posted by President Donald Trump tossed the city into the national spotlight claiming that Haitian immigrants are eating pets.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Saturday event was planned to be in-person in Springfield, but the organizers decided to make it virtual because of security concerns, Macmillvie Neel, executive editor of the Haitian Times, said. Springfield City Hall and two elementary schools were evacuated this week after receiving bomb threats. On Saturday, threats forced lockdowns and two area hospitals.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Wittenberg University announced Saturday that it was taking "extreme precautions" and increasing security following an email threatening a potential shooting on campus targeting Haitian members of the school's community on Sunday. Wittenberg is a liberal arts college located in Springfield. Founded in 1845, it is associated with the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I don't know what happened with the bomb threats?" Trump told reporters on Saturday. "I know that it's been taken over by illegal migrants."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Jims Denis, a Haitian immigrant in Springfield, said he moved to the city five years ago and owns three properties in the city, including a photography studio. He said he feels like Haitians in the city are being targeted.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "You can see it's pure hatred. They hate us," Denis said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Denis said Haitians are not safe in Springfield and that he no longer leaves his house very much.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I take my kids to the park usually, I cannot do that anymore.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "You know, I have to just stay home and just don't go out. We used to just go for a walk in the neighborhood, but we cannot do that anymore," he said, adding that his wife wants to move out of the city.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sophia Perralus, a Haitian activist who lives in Columbus, urged Springfield residents to care for their mental health and watch out for signs their children are experiencing bullying at school.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "You must keep your eyes open regarding your children," she said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Viles Dorsainvil, the president of the Haitian Community and Support Center, said the center helps Haitian immigrants find jobs and housing. He said the center is focusing on cross-cultural education, including Creole courses for Americans and ESL and driving classes.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Contributing: Elizabeth Weise, USA TODAY.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Erin Glynn is a reporter for the USA TODAY Network Ohio Bureau, which serves the Columbus Dispatch, Cincinnati Enquirer, Akron Beacon Journal and 18 other affiliated news organizations across Ohio.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Schools' AC

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: without the AC, but that is no longer their reality. Regions across the U.S. that never had the need now face mounting pressure to update facilities to keep kids cool. This summer was Earth's test, and it was not a time for a recession diagnosis of the Copernicus Climate Change Service.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The need to cool schools has increased markedly in the Upper Northwest and in states such as California, Alaska and Montana, according to a recent analysis by Climate Central which measures cooling demand from late July to early September.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hotter days around the start of the academic year will affect classroom and campus temperatures and threaten student learning more frequently, said Holsboer, a professor of public policy at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Soaring temperatures put a strain on already aging facilities that public schools have," Davis said. "And in places that are not likely to have up-to-date AC units, it's no surprise that learning is stopped, halted or postponed."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hundreds of poorly equipped schools facing late summer heat, including some in Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and Portland, Oregon, sent kids home early in September because of excessive heat warnings.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The abbreviated instruction time impairs student learning and further exacerbates the achievement gap, Davis said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Why do schools lack adequate AC?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Many classrooms and school gymnasiums are too hot without air conditioning in the summer months. But that didn't used to be the case. In regions of the world where temperatures are consistently high, some buildings are not equipped with cooling systems.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: There are also challenges in regions where it always gets sweltering hot. In areas with cooling systems, districts must contend during heat waves with aging and broken facilities. The urgency of these repairs is being shouldered by maintenance workers, including those in Los Angeles who have been responding to daily requests to fix air conditioning systems this school year.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A total of 50,000 AC units in the district need to be replaced because they are old, deteriorated or malfunctioning, and there is a lack of funding for replacement in the Los Angeles Unified School District.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Officials coordinating fixes to these cooling systems are offering teachers alternative indoor cooling units and they're placing misting fans at elementary schools to help keep exterior students in the cool during hotter days, Vaughn said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In Reno, Nevada, where the number of days AC is needed has increased according to Climate Central's analysis, some school gynaecsiams built in the 1980s

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: lack cooling systems, which weren't considered a necessity at the time, said Adam Searcy, chief operating officer of the Washoe County School District.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some of these Reno gyms now reach up to 80 degrees during volleyball practices in the early summer months, however, the district has no plans to install air conditioning because it's too costly, Searcy said. He said district schools do, however, plan to build future gyms with proper cooling systems.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The rise in cooling demand will likely continue as the planet warms, and schools will need critical building upgrades and face higher operating costs to maintain safe, comfortable temperatures," according to the Climate Central report.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Heat affects learning, teaching

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: All students feel the negative academic impact of hot classrooms because kids can't learn in unhealthy weather conditions, Davis said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Traditionally disadvantaged students will feel it even more in low-income communities with less access to air conditioning and shaded areas since they are more likely to walk to school and come inside to cool off, which is vital for student well-being, she said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We know historically that communities of color and low-income communities are in places that are less likely to have tree coverings," Davis said. "We're located in environmentally hazardous spaces without access to shade."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Are there solutions?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some regions have made major headway in addressing the shortfall. Chicago schools' classrooms have air conditioning units, but that wasn't always the case.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Years ago, the Chicago Teachers Union negotiated with the district to ensure classrooms were cool, Stacy Davis Gates, president of the teacher’s union, said. The group is now focused on pushing the district toward additional energy-saving solutions.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The doesn't just mean AC in the unit but also … solar panels on the roof to build the cost down," she said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some regions are shifting the school calendar year to make it easier for kids. Milwaukee Public Schools pushed back its academic calendar this year to start in early September rather than late August. This choice happened after the district was forced to cancel classes due to excessive heat in the early days of the last school year.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Other jurisdictions have passed laws or considered regulations requiring schools to keep classrooms cooled to a certain temperature.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A workers' rights law passed in California in July requires districts to keep schools at a comfortable temperature. However, some schools in the Golden State say they're struggling to keep up with that mandate.

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Students at Emerson College supporting Palestinian causes sleep in tents at an encampment at the Boston campus in April. JOSEPH PREZIOSO/AFP VIA GETTY IMAGES

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Colleges

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Continued from Page 1A

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: debatable. Two weeks ago the Muslim Legal Fund of America shrugged off the warning, saying the letter amounted to a fruitless attempt to force the Rhode Island school to comply with laws outside its jurisdiction. In a separate letter to Brown's administrators, lawyers for the fund called on the university to reject the "baseless threats of legal repercussions."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The debate marks a new phase in the campus divestment movement, as few colleges where administrators considered protesters' demands start a new school year. Though most schools ultimately dismissed requests to disentangle their investment portfolios from companies with connections to Israel, some seemed to entertain those asks more earnestly. In late August, for instance, San Francisco State University said its foundation would stop investing in companies that make money from weapons manufacturing. Other schools also took steps to assuage student activists.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: SFSU spokesperson Kent Bravo said via email that the university has not received any warnings about antibo-cott laws. Bravo also noted that the university's divestment policy is solely based on the amount of money coming from weapons makers and not the geography of those companies.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "University administrators are facing all sort of obstacles to divestment that the students are not really considering. It's a difficult thing for everyone involved."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Adam Gjesdal Fellow at the Heterodox Academy

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The letter to Brown also highlights the degree to which politicians, even at the state level, continue to see political opportunity in wading into the dynamics of campus protests about the Israel-Hamas war. Amid promises from some students that another law enforcement effort would be imminent, the legal arguments over antiboycott laws highlight how much resistance there still is to divestment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At a dinner earlier this month with reporters in Washington, D.C., several prominent college presidents commented on the difficult task of handling the anti-war protests in the spring. Some student activists, they suggested, were making requests that were unrealistic.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Carmen Twillie Ambar, the president of Oberlin College in Ohio, said she encouraged students on her campus to think about alternate avenues to push for change in the Middle East. Some of their demands surrounding divestment, she said, were "like trying to take cheese out of baked lasagna."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Antibocott laws: What are they?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Roughly 40 states have enacted laws, executive orders or resolutions meant to discourage the boycott, divestment and sanctions - or BDS - movement, according to the Jewish Virtual Library. In 2017, the Arkansas Legislature passed a law prohibiting public entities from contracting with and investing in companies that boycott Israel, arguing that companies that refuse to deal with the Israeli government for political reasons are engaging in discrimination. The law came at a time when pro-Israeli lawyers were successfully pushing through dozens of policies in state

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: capitals across the country.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In the recent warning letter to Brown, Arkansas' attorney general, Tim Griffin, said if Brown were to adopt the divestment proposal set for a vote in October, his state and others would be forced to consider terminating "any existing relationships with Brown." Many of the states mentioned in the letter said they're already reviewing their pension investments and contracts to determine if the university had done anything to violate their laws.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But Brown likely doesn't have much reason to worry, said Chris Marsicano, an education professor at Davidson College in North Carolina.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's not like the state of Arkansas is doing much business with Brown University," he said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: However, antidebtcott laws may pose a greater financial problem at public universities considering divestment, according to Adam Gjesdal, a fellow at the Heterodox Academy, a nonprofit group advocating diverse viewpoints on college campuses. He has argued that divestment at those schools could raise tuition prices.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "University administrators are facing all sort of obstacles to divestment that the students are not really considering," he said in an interview. "It's a difficult thing for everyone involved."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Brian Clark, a spokesperson for Brown, said in an email that the university has a longstanding process of examining any proposals for divestment and is committed to a fair and thorough review of students' requests.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: A free speech issue?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Supporters of state antiboycott laws say they protect against discrimination. Shira Goodman, the vice president for advocacy at the Anti-Defamation League, a Jewish civil rights group, said it's hard to predict how a school's decision to divest from Israel could impact students.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The fiduciary responsibilities that these investment managers have are really serious," she said. "What does this do to our campus and what does it mean going forward?"

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Opponents of antibocytcoil laws, meanwhile, have argued that they violate the First Amendment, which protects the rights to free speech and peaceful protest. Gadeir Abbas, a senior litigation attorney with the Council on American-Islamic Relation, a Muslim advocacy group, said the letter is part of an antiboycott "hysteria."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "In this climate, any university should take that letter as a threat," he said. "Brown University has constitutional rights as well."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Student activists unfazed

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In May, the National Lawyers Guild wrote to Brown, assuring the university that it could boycott Israel in a legal way. A 1982 Supreme Court decision established that political boycotts are protected under the First Amendment, the group said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Yet in the decades since that ruling, other court cases have created confusion about the legal merit of boycotts in specific circumstances. In 2018, a college in Arkansas tried to force a local newspaper to sign an antibioycott pledge before it would agree to continue advertising with the outlet. The paper in Arkansas, a state court, had an obliterated role in the antibioycott discourse, sued the school. A circuit court sided with the college, and the Supreme Court last year declined to take up the case.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Those cases, of course, did not involve the complexities of college endowments. Because investments in the U.S. are already strictly regulated, some courts may be more favorable to lawsuits that challenge campus divestment.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: At Brown, student activists said they remain cautiously optimistic. Rafi Ash, a junior student leader among those calling for the divestment,said he wasn't fazed by the letter from Republican officials.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: These are pretty clearly extremist politicians using the law as they make it up, he said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: A month to fly the flag for Hispanic diversity

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: The Houston Astros commemorate Hispanic Heritage Month before a game last year at Minute Maid Park. Hispanic Heritage Month has been recognized for nearly 40 years, but the month has gained popularity in the past decade through events, social media and media representation. THOMAS SHEA/USA TODAY SPORTS

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Ahjane Forbes

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hispanic Heritage Month, or "Mes de la Herencia Hispana" in Spanish, honors the history, culture, food, music and accomplishments of the Hispanic community.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The observation was held only for a week annually when it began in 1968 under President Lyndon B. Johnson. Two decades later, on Aug. 17, 1988, President Ronald Reagan signed a law that expanded it to a 30-day period, from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 annually, the U.S. Census Bureau said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "It's not a month," Jorge Zamanillo, founding director of the National Museum of the American Latino, told USA TODAY. "For us, we use the opportunity during this month to highlight the work that we do every day."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Although Hispanic Heritage Month has been recognized for nearly40 years, the month has gained popularity within the past decade through events, social media and representation in the media.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Andrés Acosta, a social media content creator, uses their platform to educate social media followers about Latino and Hispanic culture.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We're the largest minority group in the United States now and we're growing," they said in an Instagram post. "A lot of people have misconceptions about us, and a lot of people are only aware of Mexican culture or Puerto Rican culture, and I feel like Hispanic Latinx Heritage Month celebrates all of us."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Marking independence days

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The timing of the heritage month is significant to Hispanics as the period celebrates many independence days within the community. According to the National Museum of the American Latino, they are:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sept. 15: Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Sept. 16: Mexico.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sept.18:Chile.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Sept. 21: Belize.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: What is the difference between Hispanic and Latino?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hispanic and Latino are the most used terms to describe Spanish speakers. However, these terms can be used differently among people within the community.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hispanic is considered the universal term that describes "a person with ancestry from a country whose primary language is Spanish," according to Duke University.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Latino can be used to refer to a per

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: son who has ancestry from Latin America and the Caribbean, it said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Latinx is the gender-neutral term of Latino and Latina.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Museum in Washington showcases America's Latinos

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hispanic Heritage Month is important to Zamanillo because part of his career focused on making sure Hispanic history was included in U.S. history. After a trip to Washington, D.C., 30 years ago, he had a plan to make months like this more like this more visible in the public eye.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I really enjoyed what museums did, but I didn't see stories about Latinos and immigrants like my parents who are from Cuba," Zamanillo said. "I had an opportunity to come back and try to

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: make a difference and really give a space for Latinos to have that presence alongside other museums in Washington, D.C."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In 2020, the National Museum of the American Latino was created by Congress to display the artifacts and history of Hispanics.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: What should people do to mark Hispanic Heritage Month?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Gathering for events is a good way to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month. Zamanillo said he is excited for some of the events the National Museum of the American Latino will be hosting.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I'm really looking forward to Sept. 20," he said. "We have an event called Historic Change, an Evening Celebrating the Life and Legacy of Celia Cruz."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The event will have food, drinks and salsa dancing to celebrate Cruz's impact on the music industry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Another celebration Zamillio is looking forward to is in October.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The actual Hispanic Heritage celebration, also at American History Museum, is Latinos in Sports on Oct. 12," he said. "We're gonna have all-day celebration—highlighting different topics like how Latinos have shaped the history and culture of sports on a global scale."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Additionally, Acosta said this month is a learning opportunity, including for people who want to learn more about Hispanic countries and their cultures.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "If this is something you wanna learn more about, then you can find content creators online to listen to," they said. "You can look up articles that might be more specific into what interests you wanna get a better picture of within the Latinx community."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Acosta also said it's also important for people to support Hispanic small business owners year-round, not just during heritage month.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: FBI: Another Trump assassination attempt

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Police patrol near Trump International Golf Course in West Palm Beach, Fla., in this picture from a social media video Sunday. X/AREALDEREKUTLEY via REUTER

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Phillip M. Bailey and Antonio Fins  
USA TODAY NETWORK

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. – Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump is safe following gunshots in his vicinty,his campaign and U.S. Secret Service announced Sunday.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The incident took place at Trump International Golf Course where the former president was golfing, according to the White House.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The Secret Service, in conjunction with the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, is investigating a protective incident involving former President Donald Trump that occurred shortly before 2 p.m." Secret Service spokesman Anthony Guglielmi said in a statement.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The FBI said Sunday in a statement it is investigating "what appears to be an attempted assassination of former President Trump."at his Florida golf club, according to various reports.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: U.S. Secret Service agents opened fire on a gunman located near the property line of the golf course after seeing a rifle, according to law enforcement officials who spoke at a news conference Sunday afternoon.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Agents found an AK-47-style rifle, a scope, backpack and a GoPro camera on the scene, officials said. Trump was on the golf course, roughly 400 to 500 yards away from where the would-be assailant was.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A witness saw the alleged gunman

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: running from the golf course bushes and took a picture of his vehicle that led to the suspect's quick apprehension, Palm Beach Country Sheriff Ric Bradshaw said at Sunday's news conference.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We are able to catch a witness that came to us and said, 'Hey, I saw the guy

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: running out of the bushes, he jumped into a black Nissan and I took a picture of the vehicle and the tag, which was great," Bradshaw said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As a result, they were able to alert the Martin County Sheriff's Office, who detained the suspect. The witness also was able to then identify the alleged gunman.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Along with President Joe Biden and Vice President Kamala Harris, Attorney General Merrick Garland has been briefed on the incident at the golf course, the Justice Department said in a statement.Biden is monitoring the situation and is receiving regular updates.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Fox News host Sean Hannity conveyed having a brief conversation with Trump on Sunday. He joined a live broadcast after speaking with the former president.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Trump checked to see if others were OK, Hannity said, but then joked about wanting to finish the round.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "I guess in typical, 'fight, fight, fight' fashion Trump said ... 'I really wanted to finish the hole,' " Hannity said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Contributing:Reuters

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Phillip M. Bailey reports for USA TODAY; Antonio Fins reports for the Palm Beach Post.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: High-dose ADHD drugs pose mental health risk to patients

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Study links usage to psychosis, mania risk

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text:
Ken Alltucker  
USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "That is absolutely novel, very clinically relevant and very helpful because it also assures you don't necessarily increase your psychosis risk by taking lower to medium doses."

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Nina Kraguljac

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Professor of psychiatry at Ohio State University, saying the study clarifies that only higher doses of Adderall and other amphetamines are linked to higher risk.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Hospitalized patients who took high doses of ADHD prescription amphetamines were five times likelier to develop psychosis and mania than patients not on the medication, a study found.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The study of more than 1,300 patients at Mass General Brigham hospitals linked their risk for psychosis and mania to the dosage of prescription stimulants a person took. These medications are used to help people concentrate at school or work. Patients who took 30 milligrams or more of dextroamphetamine - or 40 milligrams of Adderall - developed psychosis and mania nearly 5.3 times more often than those who did not take the medication, according to the study published Thursday in the American Journal of Psychiatry.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The study found no such link for another common ADHD medication methyphenidate, which is sold under the brand name Ritalin.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Earlier research has shown that psychosis and mania occurred in fewer than \(1\%\) of people who took these commonly used prescription amphetamines. But for the first time, the Mass General Brigham study shows a link between prescription strength and certain side effects.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Although the side effects of the drug are rare, study lead author Lauren Moran said doctors who prescribe these stimulants for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder should "maybe stay away from (higher) doses, or just make sure that you're carefully monitoring patients."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Other researchers not involved in the study said it provides important information to doctors who prescribe stimulants such as Adderall.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nina Kraguljac, a professor of psychiatry and behavioral health at Ohio State University, said the study clarifies that only higher doses of Adderall and other prescription amphetamines are linked to higher risk.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Kraguljac said the study shows doctors may not want to exceed 30 milligrams when prescribing dextroamphetamine or 40 milligrams for Adderall.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That is absolutely novel, very clinically relevant and very helpful because it also assures you don't necessarily increase your psychosis risk by taking lower to medium doses," Kraguljac said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Higher doses pose a greater risk

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Researchers carried out the study because doctors had noticed some patients with psychosis and mania also had taken prescription amphetamines, said Moran, a psychiatrist and a pharmacoeidemiology researcher at McLean Hospital, a psychiatric hospital in Belmont, Massachusetts.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Moran wanted to investigate the possible link between stimulant use and certain mental health conditions.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Moran's research team gathered records of patients admitted to McLean from 2005 through 2019 after first visiting emergency rooms at other Mass Gen

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: erbalingham hospitals in the Boston region. The patients were ages 16 to 35

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Researchers examined the records of 1,374 patients hospitalized for psychosis or mania and 2,748 patients hospitalized for depression, anxiety or other reasons. People who had been prescribed an amphetamine within the previous month were more likely to be diagnosed with psychosis or mania than those who did not take the medication. Those who took the strongest doses had the greatest odds of developing psychosis or mania. Hospital workers contacted the patients' pharmacies to document which prescription medications and doses they had been given at the time of their hospitalization.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The study evaluated three types of prescription amphetamines: mixed prescription amphetamines, such as Adderall and Mydalis, dextroamphetamine and lisdexamfetamine, which is sold under the brand Vyyanse. Most patients who were prescribed amphetamines were on Adderall, Moran said.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Which ADHD drugs are not linked to psychosis or mania?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Researchers also examined the records of patients who took the ADHD medication methylphenidate and found no increased odds of psychosis or mania. This drug is sold under the brand names Ritalin and Concerta.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Even for people taking Adderall or other prescription amphetamines, the risk is rare. Past research showed psychosis and mania occurred in fewer than1% of the patients taking prescription amphetamines. However, Moran said her study suggests doctors should be careful when prescribing high doses of prescription amphetamines.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Moran said her research team is conducting a national study of patients who were prescribed stimulants to treat ADHD. The study will follow participants who are prescribed low,medicinal or high doses of ADHD medication. The study will compare rates of psychosis among those taking varying doses of the medication.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Amid shortages, risks of switching ADHD medications

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Kraguljac, of Ohio State University, said Adderall is generally a "first-line treatment" for patients with ADHD. Some doctors choose to prescribe Ritalin when patients get side effects from taking Adderall.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: But she said having information from the study suggesting higher doses of prescription amphetamines may pose a risk to patients will be helpful to doctors switching their patients' medications.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Guns are still leading cause of death for kids

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Report: 2,500 children, teens died by a firearm

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Thao Nguyen USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Firearms were the leading cause of death for children and teenagers in the United States for the third consecutive year, and homicides accounted for the majority of gun deaths among the age group, a new report found.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The report - published Thursday by the Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions - analyzed the latest data on gun violence from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, which revealed that more than 48,000 people across the country died from gun violence in 2022. Of those deaths, more than 2,500 children and teens ages 1 to 17 died by a firearm.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "In the U.S., gun death rates in this age group have increased by106 percent since2013 and have been the leading cause of death among this group since2020," the Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions said in a news release.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The report underscores the rapid increase of gun violence in the U.S. in recent years and its effect on young people. Health officials, including Surgeon General Vivek Murthy, have called gun violence a "public health crisis" that is the leading cause of premature death for Americans.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The rate of firearm-related deaths "reached a near three-decade high in 2021," an advisory on gun violence issued by Murthy in June said. There were 48,830 gun-related deaths in the U.S. in 2021, according to the CDC.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The second-highest total of gun deaths ever recorded was in 2022, when 48,204 people died from gun-related injuries, the report noted. It added that 19,375 deaths included more than 27,000 suicides, an all-time high for the country.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The death toll shows that "troubling trends" still persist among vulnerable demographic groups, including growing disparities across racial and ethnic groups such as Black and Latino youth, according to the report.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Gun deaths disproportionately affect Black youth

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: While the overall gun violence rate decreased in 2022 after "peaking in 2021 amid the social unrest of the COVID-19 pandemic," according to the Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions, guns remained the leading cause of death among children and teens.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "Gun death rates doubled from 2013 to 2022 for children and teens (ages 1-17)," according to the report. "In 2022, nearly three times as many teens (ages 18-24) died by gun homicide compared to 2013, meaning from 541 in 2013 to 1,486 in 2022."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The number of gun-related deaths among the age group surpassed the number of deaths from car crashes, overdoses and cancers, the report said. It noted that an average of seven people died each day in gun violence, and firearms accounted for \(30\%\) of deaths among older teens ages 15 to 17.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The report also highlighted the disproportionate consequences of gun violence on children and teens of color:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: In 2022, Black young people ages 1 to 17 had a gun homicide rate 18 times higher compared with white children and teens. And the rate for Hispanic/white children and teens was more than three times higher than for white youth.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: · Gun suicide rates have increased over the past decade, tripling among Black youth ages 10 to 17 and more than doubling for Hispanic/Latino youth ages 10 to 17.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: - Fifty-five percent of deaths among older Black teens ages 15 to 17 in 2022 were caused by guns.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Across all age groups, American Indian/Alaskan Native people were five times more likely to die by gun homicide compared with white people in the same age group.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Rise in gun violence incidents across US schools

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The U.S. already has seen 389 mass shootings in 2024, according to the Gun Violence Archive, a nonprofit that defines mass shootings as incidents involving four or more victims. And so far this year, there have been 28 school shootings that resulted in injuries or deaths, according to data compiled by Education Week, a news organization that covers K-12 education.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: A study released last month by the nonprofit Everytown for Gun Safety found that there was a \(31\%\) increase in school shootings over the past academic year compared with the previous year. After the 2021-2022 school year, which had the highest number of gun violations on campuses, Everytown tracked at least 144 incidents of gun violence on campuses for the 2023-24 school year.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Nearly four in 10 of those shot in these school incidents were students, Everytown said in the study.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: What can the US do about gun violence?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Recent gun violence incidents, including Sept. 4 when officials say a 14-year-old opened fire at a Georgia high school and killed two teachers and two students, have renewed debates on gun violence and calls for stricter gun laws.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions report provided several policy recommendations to address the gun violence crisis among young people, including strengthening and adopting Child Access Prevention laws.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: More than half of all U.S. gun owners do not practice safe firearm storage, the report noted. "In fact, 4.6 million minors in the U.S. live in homes with at least one gun that is loaded and unlocked, exposing children to firearms and increasing the risk of gun violence among children and youth."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Other recommendations were firearm licensing laws with background checks and required safety training; removing firearms from those at risk of violence to themselves or others; community violence intervention programs; regulating carrying firearms in public; and repealing stand-your-ground laws.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "The research is clear - these policies can help reduce rates of gun violence, including the record-high rates we're seeing among our nation's youngest and most vulnerable," Cassandra Crifasi, report co-author and co-director of the Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions, said.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Contributing: Kayla Jimenez

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Speaker would risk shutdown for Trump

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Chris Brennan USA TODAY

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Politicians returned to the Congress in Washington, D.C., last week from

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "their August break, and House Speaker Mike Johnson was eager to get back to not working for the American people."

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Johnson

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rep. Johnson, R-La., serves only one person as speaker - Donald Trump. He'll do anything for the

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: former president now attempting a return to the White House.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Johnson will even threaten to shut down the government.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Johnson inserted what he had to know was a poison pill in his new proposal to keep funding the government until March. It injects one of Trump's most common lies - that Democrats rely on voters from noncitizens to win federal elections and presidency - into the everyday duties of politicians running the government.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Or, in Johnson's case, not running it.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: His threat to push our government into a shutdown has nothing to do with what happens when government funding runs out Sept. 30 and everything to do with Nov. 5, when voters pick our next president.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Trump on Tuesday doubled down the demand he made recently that Republicans shut down the government, lying on his social media platform that "DEMOCRATs ARE TRYING TO 'STUFF' VOTING IN RENSTRATIONS WITH ILLEGAL ALIENS" to have you ever met a rational person who conversed on social media that way?

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Johnson, with a constituency of one

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: these days, appeared on CNN Tuesday afternoon and supported Trump, even as his own Republican colleagues were backing away from him on all this.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: If the House speaker wants to swap in shameless pandering for running the government, then we should stop paying him. I'll come back to that.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Johnson tried to handcuff government funding to the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act (SAVE), which would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And Americans who don't always have access to documents necessary for registration, who happen to lean Demo.gov or their voting? Well, tough luck for them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The bill is voter suppression barely camouflaged as election security. It's a "messaging bill" that stands no chance of passing in the Democratic-controlled Senate. But it pushes into the national conversation the bogus and often racist theory that Democrats are trying to replace American voters with foreigners.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: As I wrote in May, the notion that noncitizens vote in ways that can shift the results of elections is just not supported by facts.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And it has been illegal since the 1920s for noncitizens to vote in federal elections, something that Congress further codified in 1996 with legislation signed by then-President Bill Clinton.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: You might remember Clinton. He's a Democrat.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Even some Republicans are fed up with Johnson

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Johnson has more immediate problems with his plan to amplify Trump's lies with the threat of a shutdown. His own Republican colleagues in the House think the speaker is out of order here.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rep. Cory Mills, a hard-right Republican from Florida who co-sponsored

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: the SAVE Act, called Johnson's attempt a "farce" last Monday while telling Fox News there's no way to implement the law between now and the election.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Roll Call reported last week that Johnson, who rules with a narrow majority in the House, could only afford to lose four Republicans on the vote but at least five were against linking SAVE to the funding. Politico also found plenty of House Republicans pushing back against Johnson's move.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: On Wednesday, the House speaker postponed the government funding vote. Looks like his fellow House Republicans don't want to own a shutdown so close to an election.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The last shutdown, which lasted from Dec. 22, 2018, to Jan. 25, 2019, crimped America's gross domestic product by $1 billion. Try being the party that claims to be competent on the economy while rolling those dice again.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Tie government shutdown to paying members of House, Senate

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Rep. Angie Craig, a three-term Democrat from Minnesota, has a solid way to fix the lack of consequences her colleagues feel during shutdowns. Craig last year reintroduced legislation that she first sponsored in her 2019 rookie position. She also has 13 members of the House and Senate get no pay during a government shutdown.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: See, as of now, there are no financial consequences for members of Congress when they play politics with funding the government. They don't feel the pinch, like the 850,000 federal employees whowent without pay during the last shut-down, which lasted35 days.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The paychecks kept coming for the politicians, who left so many others to go without.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Craig's bill, bottled up for nearly a year in Republican-controlled commit

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: tees, would withhold one day of congressional pay for every 24 hours of shutdown.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: They would get that pay on the last day of their session in office to avoid conflicting with the U.S. Constitution's 27th Amendment, which says congressional pay can't change until after the next election.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Members of the House and Senate are paid $174,000 a year. So each day of shutdown would cost them $475.41 in this leap year, at least until terms end.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Don't feel too bad for them. Their pay is nearly three times the national average for salaries at the end of 2023.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 'It's not something that is easily proven'

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Johnson doesn't care about the consequences of a shutdown. His speakership is all about Trump.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Johnson on Tuesday declared that "I am in this to win this" after so many members of his caucus made clear he could not win this.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: He already gave away the game in May when he said this about his unsubstantiated claims that noncitizens vote in large numbers in federal elections, impacting the outcome:

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: "We all know intuitively that a lot of illegals are voting in federal elections. But it's not something that is easily proven."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: That hits the Trump-Republican brand for lies about election fraud. They can't prove it, but they want to believe it. And that's all that matters. The lack of proof - and logic - is irrelevant.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The impact on people and the country's economy from a shutdown matters not to Johnson. He's only here to do Trump's bidding.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Follow USA TODAY elections columnist Chris Brennan on X, formerly known as Twitter: @ByChrisBrennan

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Colleges need to fight antisemitism on campus – starting now

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Sharon Nazarian Opinion contributor

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: This September, colleges and universities have the opportunity - and legal obligation - to ensure a safe and inclusive return of Jewish students to their campuses. After last year's unprecedented rise in antisemitic incidents that have led to multiple Title VI investigations, and with Jewish students confronting isolation, bullying, harassment and exclusion across a large number of international universities, administrators and safety officers must recommit themselves to having a solid plan for welcoming back Jewish students to campus.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The Anti-Defamation League and Hillel International's survey of Jewish American students last November provided a crystal-clear picture of how Jewish students were feeling just over a month after the Oct. 7 attacks committed by terror organization Hamas (Hillem). The survey gives us all an important look at the different aspects of planning that need to go into a holistic plan of action.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The spillover of the horrors of the Oct. 7 attacks and the ensuing war between Israel and Hamas onto university campuses in the form of encampments and protests across the United States, Canada, Australia and Europe led to an atmosphere of intolerance and insecurity for many Jewish students.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: University presidents and administrators have also experienced one of the toughest academic years in current memory, being under a microscope about public and private statements and actions.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Some have been hailed in front of deeply political congressional hearings to answer for their campus climate, and some have even lost their jobs.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: These steps are based on guidance issued by the Anti-Defamation League, the American Jewish Committee, Hillel International, the Conference of President of the American Jewish Organizations and the Jewish Federations of North America.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Universities must ensure Jewish students' safety

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 1. Clearly communicate the standards and rules governing the campus community, including policies on protests and demonstrations. Make sure students and faculty are aware of your campuses' codes of conduct, including policies and procedures for managing protests, demonstrations, postings and other speech activity - including time, place and manner regulations.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 2. Make clear to administrators, faculty and staff their obligations as employees and members of an academic community to uphold a commitment to no tolerance for antisemitism or any form of hate. In advance of the start of the academic year, prepare communications about what these policies are, why they are important, how they align with core campus values and the consequences of violating them.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: And if those policies are violated, make sure steps are taken to enforce those policies. Students and their parents will be asked to know your words mean something.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 3. Take assurances that members of the academic community are not silenced, harassed, intimidated or threatened; that the university's normal teaching, learning and research activities are not disrupted. These policies must then be enforced in an even-handed, content-neutral and competitive manner. The university's activist faculty bringing their activism into a class unrelated to their activism should be warned and if they persist, removed from teaching that course.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: How colleges can combat antisemitism on campus

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 4. Directly respond to antisemitic incidents as well as other forms of hateful acts when they occur. University leaders should publish strong, timely statements that (a) explicitly condemn the incident and explain what steps will be taken by the university to address the situation and prevent its recurrence, (b) describe specific support available for the Jewish community and (c) establish clear expectations for respectful campus discourse tied directly

layout_dets.label: 图注
layout_dets.text: Pro-Palestinian supporters demonstrate with a protest encampment on the campus of Columbia University on April 29 in New York City. SPENCER PLATT/GETTY IMAGES

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: to the mission of the institution.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: The fact that the incident may involve protected free speech in no way reduces the university's obligation to step up and speak out, as indicated by the U.S. Department of Education: "The fact that harassment may involve conduct that includes speech in a public setting or speech that is also motivated by an individual's personal or social interests does not relieve a school of its obligation to respond under Title VI ... if the harassment creates a hostile environment in school for a student or students."

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 5. Support Jewish students by preventing discrimination against Jewish students in campus organizations, clubs, and institutions. Pronouncements such as “Zionists are not welcome” should not be tolerated. This form of exclusion becomes even more insidious when the word “Zios” (a term coined by former Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke) is invoked as an antisemitic slur applying this type of litmus test.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 6. Unequivocally denounce the targeting of Jewish student organizations. Recently, Jewish institutions such as Hillel, the primary center for Jewish student life on campus, and Chabad, another essential Jewish campus organization, have increasingly become targets of attacks, with protesters calling for schools to sever ties with Hillel and

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Chabad. This is antisemitism pure and simple and should be called out as such.

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Jewish students and faculty deserve to be seen and heard

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 7. Ensure Israeli students and faculty are welcome and reject BDS (bobby, divestment and sanction campaign). Covert or "soft" boycotts of Israeli institutions and academics that include canceling agreements with Israeli academic students and institutions, denying Israeli academics visiting professorships and canceling lectures by Israeli professors negate the pursuit of a good university. Universities must reaffirm their opposition to BDS and explain to the campus community why that movement is harmful and antithetical to campus values.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 8. Provide antisemitism education and training for all students and front-line faculty and staff. Too many students don't know the red lines between criticism of Israeli policy and outright antisemitic speech and behavior.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 9. Proactively prepare for Oct. 7 and other moments with high potential for disruption to university operations. Remember that many campus demonstrations crossed red lines when they used antisemitic rhetoric and symbols (often in support of terror organization Hamas, Hezbollah and others). Campus encampments violated campus rules and harassed students.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 10. And finally, get to know your Jewish students, their diversity, their identity, their sense of community. Show up, be inquisitive, be curious. Don'tckenize your Jewish students and faculty. Don't allow small fringe groups who claim to speak for all Jewish students to stifle the sentiment of the core Jewish groups. Show your Jewish students how to think and be heard. Show their parents that your motivation is not one of averting legal trouble, but that all your students feel safe.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (1.中国科学院国家空间科学中心北京100190;2.中国科学院大学北京100049；3.中国科学院光电研究院北京100094)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 摘要：针对传统国内外热流算法以及某些国外商业软件只计算单行星轨道航天器外热流的不足，提出了太阳系行星际轨道航天器的外热流计算方案。本文方案采用积分定义法，平行光线法，近似法，插值法，考虑行星椭圆轨道的影响以及面元遮挡。仿真计算结果表明，该方案符合行星际轨道外热流物理特性，其计算效率和精度较高。

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 关键词：外热流；角系数；行星际轨道；航天器；辐射换热

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 中图分类号：TN92

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 文献标识码：A

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: Study of external heat flux calculation method for interplanetary spacecraft in solar system

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: LIU Yang\(^{1,2}\), PENG Xiao-dong\(^{1}\), ZHANG Han-xun\(^{1}\), GUO Song\(^{1,2}\), MING Xing\(^{3}\)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: (1. National Space Science Center, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, China;2. University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100049, China;3.Academy of Opto-electronics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100094, China)

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Abstract: Focus on the problem that the domestic traditional external heat flux calculation algorithm and some foreign commercial software only support single planet satellites' external heat flux calculation, this paper comes up with a solution which combining with the method of integration, the method of parallel light, the approximation method and the interpolation method. In the solution, the influence of planetary elliptical orbit and the occlusion of spacecraft's faces are considered. Simulation results show that the solution is in accordance with external thermal properties of the interplanetary orbit, meanwhile its computational efficiency and precision is high.

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: Key words: external heat flux; view factor; interplanetary orbit; spacecraft; radiation heat transfer

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 外热流计算是航天器热分析和热设计的前提，目前外热流计算主要采用MonteCarlo法(MC法)和积分法^{[1]}。文献[2]采用积分法计算了平板的太阳辐射角系数，地球红外辐射角系数以及地球反照角系数，被文献[3]等作为在无遮挡状况下的标准计算值。文献[3]采用MC法计算任意凸面物体所受的外热流；文献[4]提出采用MC法求解凹面和可视面的外热流；文献[1]采用均匀分布法求解外热流；另外还有通过坐标变换和矢量计算求解外热流的方法

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 这些文献和方法均为地球轨道卫星的外热流计

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 算，考虑了太阳辐射和地球对航天器空间外热流的影响。目前大多数国内文献以及传统算法只考虑单星球轨道航天器的外热流，其中地球卫星的外热流计算研究最多，没有对行星际轨道航天器外热流计算方法进行研究和分析。国外热分析软件进行了单星轨道卫星的热分析，比如ThermalDesktop软件，只对各大行星以及月球单星轨道卫星进行热分析，且计算过程中未考虑行星位于椭圆运行轨道不同位置对其太阳常数的实时影响，只以经验常数代替，这对于近日行星卫星外热流计算会产生一些误差

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 文中针对传统研究的以上待研究处，考虑太阳

layout_dets.label: 脚注
layout_dets.text: 基金项目：中国科学院科研装备研制项目（YZ201309）

layout_dets.label: 脚注
layout_dets.text: 作者简介：刘洋(1991—)，女，山西阳泉人，博士。研究方向：航天系统建模仿真与可视化。

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: 《电子设计工程》2017年第09期

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 实际远近距离对计算的影响以及除地球外其他行星和行星自然卫星的影响，并且考虑遮挡因素，平衡算法的精度和效率，开展了太阳系行星际航天器外热流计算方法的研究，总结出行星际轨道航天器的外热流计算方案，并进行仿真计算。

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1 外热流计算方法

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 地球轨道卫星外热流主要由太阳辐射外热流、地球的红外辐射外热流和反照辐射外热流构成^{[3]}。地球轨道卫星面元 i 的外热流 Q_{ei} 公式为：

layout_dets.text: 对于太阳系行星际轨道航天器外热流，主要由太阳辐射外热流、各行星以及行星自然卫星的红外辐射外热流和反照辐射外热流构成。面元 i 的外热流 Q_{i} 公式为：

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 其中： Q_{i1} 为太阳辐射外热流， Q_{i2} 为各行星及行星自然卫星的红外辐射外热流， Q_{i3} 为各行星及行星自然卫星的反照辐射外热流。 a_{si}, a_{si} 分别为航天器面元 i 的太阳辐射吸收率和表面红外发射率，是与航天器材质有关的常数。A_{i} 为面元 i 的面积。 S, E_{2}, E_{3} 分别为太阳常数，各行星以及行星自然卫星红外辐射密度，各行星以及行星自然卫星反照辐射密度，单位为 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^2 。F_{1}, F_{2}, F_{3} 分别为太阳辐射角系数，各行星以及行星自然卫星红外辐射角系数，各行星以及行星自然卫星反照辐射角系数。行星际航天器外热流的计算主要为这6个参数的计算。其中，关键是 F_{1}, F_{2}, F_{3} 的计算方法。

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1.1 航天器模型与互视遮挡判断

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 文中采用离散网格表示航天器各表面，建立航天器的三维模型，进行三角面片划分，提取三角面片信息，作为外热流计算的输入，再通过规则网格划分将模型重新解析，以方便遮挡的计算。首先对航

layout_dets.text: 天器面片进行一次外层面片和一次互视判断，保存结果；有互视的面片才有可能相互遮挡，故只对有互视的面片在外热流计算值大于零的情况下计算遮挡。

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 关于S的计算。跟据斯蒂芬一玻尔兹曼定律，σ 为斯蒂芬一玻尔兹曼常数，取太阳表面有效温度 T_{s} 为 5766\mathrm{K}，则太阳的辐射力为：\sigma T_{s}^{4}(\mathrm{W / m}^{2})^{[2]}。以往文献中 S 均为地球附近太阳常数，取经验值 1353W/m^2，这里我们取 S 为太阳附近太阳常数（因为 F_{1} 的计算方法也不同），即：

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 关于各行星以及行星自然卫星 \(E_{2}, E_{3}\) 的计算，不同星体计算方法相同。

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 其中，ρ 为各行星以及行星自然卫星对太阳辐射的平均反射率；S_{e} 为各行星以及行星自然卫星附近太阳常数，S_{e} = 62673162.7*(R / d)^{2}, R 为太阳半径，d 为各行星以及行星自然卫星到太阳的距离。

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 传统计算方法计算地球轨道卫星外热流时，取日地平均距离处的 E_{2}, E_{3} 常数。然而对于行星际轨道航天器，各行星以及行星自然卫星运行轨道为椭圆轨道，与太阳的距离实时改变，某些行星近日距离和远日距离相差较大，计算所得的 E_{2}, E_{3} 也相差较大，以往取平均距离计算的 E_{2}, E_{3} 常数，对外热流计算带来相当大的误差，尤其是对于近日行星。

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 表1列出了各行星近日点，远日点，平均距日距离下 E_{2},E_{3} 的值，比较可以看出，对于金星，地球，火星，近日点，远日点的 E_{2},E_{3} 相差十 W/m^2 左右。对于水星，近日点，远日点的 E_{2} 相差高达千 W/m^2 ，E_{3} 相差百 W/m^2 。故文中用实时距离计算 E_{2},E_{3} ，可避免由此带来的计算误差

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1.3 角系数计算

layout_dets.label: 标题
layout_dets.text: 1.3.1 太阳辐射角系数 \(F_{1}\) 的计算

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 在距离太阳一定远时，太阳辐射密度衰减为小

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 于 10 W/m^2 或 1 W/m^2 或更小时，我们认为此范围的航天器太阳辐射外热流为零，记航天器的这个高度为极限高度。

layout_dets.label: 页眉
layout_dets.text: 刘洋，等 太阳系行星际航天器外热流计算方法研究

layout_dets.label: 段落
layout_dets.text: 在极限高度范围内，当航天器距离太阳足够近时， \(F_{1}\) 计算用积分法，我们称这个高度为 \(F_{1}\) 分界高度；当高度超过 \(F_{1}\) 分界高度时把太阳光看成平行光，用平行光法，即
